Sports.title: Will anyone topple Infantino? How Fifa president is trying to cling on after World Cup sell-off debacle
Sports.content:
For Gianni Infantino there is no international break. The Fifa president is widely expected to make an appearance at the United Nations general assembly this week in New York, where he will lobby heads of state for their federations’ support as he continues his campaign to be re-elected next year.

Infantino has not been idle during the lull since Fifa abandoned its World Cup sell-off plan last month, instead crisscrossing the globe on a private jet provided by Qatar Airways as part of its sponsorship deal with world football’s governing body.

From his strongholds in Doha, Rabat and Miami, Infantino has also visited Colombia, the Dominican Republic, Kyrgyzstan and various other countries, his trips often coinciding with the approval of funding for development projects worth millions of dollars. His would-be opponents have been conspicuous by their silence.

Whether Qatar Airways facilitating Infantino’s re-election campaign should be considered legitimate Fifa presidential business is a moot point, which neatly encapsulates the huge incumbency bias that will benefit Infantino if a vote takes place at the Fifa congress in March. That ballot appears to be in doubt, with multiple sources involved in the push to remove Infantino telling the Guardian they are running out of hope of finding a candidate to beat him.

Although dozens of the 200 member associations that had submitted letters of endorsement for Infantino withdrew them after the emergence of his Fifa Forward Enterprise sale plan in July, the prevailing view is that the silent majority remain steadfastly behind him.

A meeting with the Caribbean Football Union, where funding projects were approved, may have splintered the vote at Concacaf – the North and Central American and Caribbean confederation – and there are increasing concerns that the European alliance may not be watertight.

“As long as Gianni is running, I don’t think anyone else will raise their hand,” one source said. “They would effectively be running against Fifa the institution. Fifa declared his candidacy, provides staff, aeroplanes and cars, even a personal video team.

“If he doesn’t step down before March, the election will not be contested. Uefa and others could stage a boycott so the victory would be tainted, but Gianni will win a clear majority of whoever shows up.”

Infantino first declared at the April congress in Vancouver his intention to seek a fourth and final term of office. Fifa statutes limit presidents to three full terms but under a recent change he will be permitted a fourth because his first term lasted three years, rather than the usual four, after his 2016 election to replace the disgraced Sepp Blatter.

The 56-year-old reasserted his intention to stand after attending the first match of the Under-20 Women’s World Cup in Poland a fortnight ago. That came via a statement issued by Fifa’s media team.

As it stands Infantino does not have an opponent, despite Uefa, Concacaf and the Asian Football Confederation calling for him to go. Beyond the obvious difficulties of taking on an incumbent who controls the machinery of office and funding budgets – the last Fifa president beaten at the ballot box was Sir Stanley Rous in 1974 – there are specific reasons why none of the would-be candidates have declared.

The most credible challenger is regarded as Concacaf’s president, Victor Montagliani, but the Canadian is committed to standing for re-election at his confederation, and the vote is due to take place in February. Standing in both elections is not regarded as feasible, and Montagliani is understandably reluctant to walk away from Concacaf in favour of fighting a potentially losing battle against Infantino.

View image in fullscreen Victor Montagliani (right), president of Concacaf, is reluctant to walk away from his current role but would be the most credible challenger to Infantino. Photograph: Elizabeth Ruiz Ruiz/Getty Images

The AFC president, Salman bin Ibrahim Al Khalifa, was beaten by Infantino in the 2016 election, the only time Infantino has faced an electoral opponent, and is further hamstrung by the fact that his confederation’s main powers, Saudi Arabia, Qatar and the United Arab Emirates, are backing Infantino. Qatar’s position would also appear to rule out a challenge from Nasser al-Khelaifi, the chair of European Football Clubs, and an openly European move led by Uefa’s president, Aleksander Ceferin, would have no chance of success. Ceferin, in any case, has his own presidential contest in March to focus on.

To compound the difficulties for Infantino’s would-be challengers, any election would be a secret ballot, making any promises from member associations during the campaign period all but worthless. As a result, Uefa is focusing most of its efforts on legal avenues to remove Infantino, accusing him of “criminal mismanagement” in a 56-page document lodged with US state courts in New York, Miami and Colorado last month seeking the disclosure of all documents relating to FFE.

Fifa responded strongly the week after Uefa made its legal complaint, filing a response in New York in which it sought to block the discovery process. Its submission accused Uefa of mounting a smear campaign against Infantino in the absence of any evidence of wrongdoing.

Fifa’s submission said: “Uefa’s application suffers from a fundamental defect: Uefa seeks discovery in aid of a foreign criminal proceeding that does not exist and that Uefa admittedly lacks the authority to initiate.

“While these applications are styled as legal pleadings with captions and docket numbers, they are little more than press releases in further support of Uefa’s smear campaign against Fifa and its leadership.”

Although there is widespread confidence that at least one of the three jurisdictions will grant discovery, the process grants Fifa the right of appeal, so there is little prospect of new material being made public before the 18 November deadline for presidential candidates to come forward.

An initial decision from the courts is expected next month, but an appeal from the losing party appears inevitable whatever the outcome.

“The issue with discovery is that it takes a long time,” a source said. “It’s likely to run beyond the date of the election in March. If the process is under way by then, Fifa congress could decide to wait until we find out what the courts discover and postpone the election. But there would still have to be a vote on that.”

Uefa’s not-so-secret hope is that the discovery process finds evidence that FFE was deliberately undervalued at $20bn (£15bn) to provide a guaranteed future windfall for Joshua Kushner’s Thrive Capital, which had seemingly agreed to pay $4.2bn for 21% of the new commercial venture, giving it a significant share of future Fifa revenues.

Thrive subsequently bought 20% of the LA Lakers last month as part of a larger transaction with the former Disney chief executive Bob Iger that valued the NBA franchise at $12.5bn, a deal that has further highlighted Infantino’s valuation of the World Cup.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Fifa’s revenues for the four years to 2026 were $15bn, a figure projected to grow to $18bn over the next four-year cycle owing to larger broadcast deals, without accounting for any expansion of the World Cup and Club World Cup, which remains on the agenda.

A corporate fraud lawyer said that undervaluing FFE could potentially constitute a criminal offence by Fifa, a case Uefa would take to the Swiss courts. “If you’re doing a deal that is way off market then you are deceiving the stakeholders, in this case the member associations,” the legal source said. “That is criminal. If Uefa has a criminal case that’s where it will be. It’s about how the valuation was done, by whom, and what conflicts were there.

“All of that should come out during disclosure. If beyond that there were personal deals being struck on the side, that could also be criminal. All those details should be disclosed.”

Beyond the $20bn valuation, the identity of the would-be investors and Fifa’s claim that it would retain control over governance, very little has been made public about the development of FFE, with a sales deck produced by the US bank JP Morgan containing no details of a tender process, voting rights or future exit terms. A senior investment banker who has been involved in similar deals said it is inconceivable such details were not agreed before Thrive agreed to commit $4bn, albeit much of the funding was due from other investors.

View image in fullscreen Gianni Infantino before the World Cup final. Photograph: Pablo Morano/BSR Agency/Getty Images

“I don’t think Thrive was going to be involved with Fifa for the next 25 years,” they said. “This looks like a quick in-and-out play. The plan would have been to buy it low and sell it high. I think the investors saw an amazing deal.”

There is no evidence of any wrongdoing or criminality on the part of the any of the parties involved in the proposed FFE deal.

Thrive has revealed little about its intentions beyond a statement issued last month in which it presented FFE as a proposal to be voted on by Fifa’s members, rather than a done deal.

Significantly, however, it also expressed an element of regret at getting involved given the political backlash, which many within football have interpreted as an attempt to distance the firm from Infantino.

“It was an idea that every member association would vote on, not an obligation or determination,” Thrive said. “While we stand behind the motivations of FFE, we failed to appreciate the political dynamics of global football, and the lengths some would go to. Thrive has a long track record of being a partner to all constituents. Had we known what this would devolve into, we would not have gotten involved.”

Uefa and Concacaf, in particular, appear prepared to dig in for the long haul, despite concerns that Infantino will be re-elected. The two confederations are continuing to work together to develop a unified Nations League competition, revealed by the Guardian last month, and last week wrote a joint letter to Fifa demanding that it release funds from its $6bn reserves to fund an additional payment of at least $10m to each of its 211 member associations during the next four-year cycle.

Some sort of payment appears inevitable given Infantino promised to provide $20m more to the member associations via FFE, but Uefa and Concacaf are hoping Infantino does not accrue political and electoral credit for it.

Ceferin and Montagliani are expected to meet at next week’s general assembly of the European Football Clubs in Copenhagen, where Infantino may also make an appearance. Infantino addressed the EFC’s 900 members at last year’s EFC meeting in Rome, where his suggestion that more international tournaments should take place during European winters to accommodate the global south caused controversy, although that pales compared with his pronouncements and plans since.

Uefa has made one accommodation with Fifa by withdrawing its threat to boycott the Under-20 Women’s World Cup that finishes on Sunday, and Infantino has agreed to its demand to commission an external governance review, which he communicated in a letter to the member associations this week. Suggestions that this move could lead to a truce with Uefa are given short shrift by those close to the leadership.

Despite the electoral gloom, those agitating for change are also clinging to memories of the fate of Infantino’s predecessor, Blatter, who was forced to resign in 2015 amid an FBI corruption investigation days after winning a fifth term against Prince Ali bin Al Hussein of Jordan. Blatter himself has never been charged in relation to the investigation.

For those looking to remove Infantino, the presidential election is not necessarily the end of the process. “This is a fight to the death now and we have to keep going,” one source said.

“The fact that Gianni is the only guy running at the moment does not mean it’s over. Look what happened to Blatter. He was re-elected in May 2015, but was gone in June. Eventually the truth will come out.”

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta agrees contract extension expected to keep him at Arsenal until 2030
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta has agreed a long-term contract extension with Arsenal that includes a hefty pay rise in recognition of his success last season and could take his reign as the manager beyond a decade.

The three-year deal he signed in September 2024 expires at the end of this season and talks have been ongoing since May when Arsenal ended their long wait to be champions. Negotiations were put on hold during the summer transfer window but the Spaniard has reached a ­verbal agreement to extend his stay for a second time.

The length of the contract is unknown but it is understood Arteta, who took over from Unai Emery in December 2019, will commit his future for at least another three years. The 44-year-old is the Premier League’s longest-serving manager after the departure of Pep Guardiola from Manchester City at the end of last season.

Arsenal have been keen to reward Arteta for transforming the club. His current contract is believed to be worth about £10m a season plus a £5m bonus for reaching the Champions League. The new deal will cement his status as one of the best-paid managers in the world.

As well as leading Arsenal to a first Premier League title since 2004, Arteta last season guided them to the Champions League final, which they lost to Paris Saint-Germain in a penalty shootout in Budapest. The club started this season with seven straight wins in all competitions before Saturday’s surprise 3-0 defeat at Brighton.

Arteta reiterated before that game that he was relaxed about his contract situation. “I think we are all very much aligned,” he said. “Whenever the time is right, we’ll get that done. There is nothing to be concerned about. I think we both have the same ambition and the same will.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Arsenal are also keen to extend Declan Rice’s contract, the England midfielder having entered the final two years of his deal. It is understood the club have an option to extend it by 12 months but would like to agree new terms in line with their policy of securing Arteta’s most important players on long-term contracts.

Sports.title: Mariona Caldentey penalty provides late WCL relief for Arsenal against Køge
Sports.content:
Mariona Caldentey’s 93rd-minute penalty delivered a win and a hefty dose of relief to fans bouncing behind the goal in the North Bank after the ball hit the back of the net, but ­Arsenal’s narrow defeat of HB Køge in their Champions League opener left more questions unanswered than answered for the struggling Gunners.

The puffed cheeks of the manager, Renée Slegers, said it all when the full-time whistle went. If it had been revealed after the final whistle that a force field surrounded the opposition goal at Meadow Park, many would have believed it, such was the extent of Arsenal’s ridiculous profligacy in front of goal in their league-phase opener.

“It was a mentality and resilience win today,” said Slegers. “The football didn’t give us the win … but we get the goal as a squad.”

Exactly what is stopping Arsenal from getting the ball in the back of the net with a swagger reflective of their talent-laden squad is hard to pinpoint.

Yes, teams are defending excellently against them, as a battling Køge and their goalkeeper Alberte Vingum did on Tuesday night, but this feels like an Arsenal problem: a mentality one, a training ground one, a ruthlessness one.

Practically solving the issue is a multifaceted undertaking, but “making things simple and easy to understand and easy to execute are probably the main two” focuses for Slegers.

“Then it’s also about involving the players as much as possible. Getting their input: ‘What do you see? What do you feel on the pitch? What’s your perception in the moment and your analysis afterwards?’”

The shadow of Sunday’s trip to Stamford Bridge loomed large at Meadow Park with eight changes made to the team that salvaged a point against Manchester United deep into added time on Saturday.

The hope, without being ­disrespectful to their Danish opposition, was that this game would alleviate the frustration the Gunners are experiencing in front of goal, breaking the mental block several players seem to be suffering from. ­Unfortunately, the A-Liga leaders had other ideas.

The Gunners’ pressure in the opening 20 minutes, which the Køge manager, Kristian Mørch, described as “like plunging into ice-cold water” that they just had to “try to survive, calm the panic, calm the fear, and then act our way out of it”, seemed to have yielded the breakthrough in the 13th minute, when Caitlin Foord kept an attack alive before sending the ball to Taylor Hinds. The full-back fed Kyra Cooney-Cross and the Australian midfielder’s neat flick was turned in by Chloe Kelly on the volley with the outside of her leg. It was a fine finish but the video assistant referee intervened to penalise an offside Stina Blackstenius for straying into the line of sight of Vingum. Had the hosts got an early goal, the game may have opened up for them a little.

View image in fullscreen Chloe Kelly scores in the 13th minute before the goal was disallowed with Stina Blackstenius ruled offside. Photograph: Justin Setterfield/Getty Images

That the match reached half-time still goalless was somewhat inexplicable, but also symbolic of Arsenal’s stuttering start to the season, with just five points from their three Women’s Super League games after consecutive draws, against Crystal Palace and Manchester United.

The scale of the achievement for the visiting team was demonstrated by the buoyant celebrations of their coaching staff as soon as the half-time whistle was blown. Mørch bellowed “good job in here”, before tripping on a railing and receiving a chorus of boos from the home fans behind the opposition dugout. He walked across the pitch towards the dressing room with a smile on his face and a finger to his lips shushing the crowd.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Their decision to celebrate every positive action was a conscious one. “We agreed before the game that we’re going to celebrate every possible win, even just the goalkeeper sometimes catching the ball, that’s a win,” said Mørch. “I could see that some of the Arsenal players got a bit annoyed by it, but we had to try and do whatever we could.”

“We noticed it,” said Slegers with a smile. “And I understand it from their perspective. It’s a good tactic, I guess, to keep morale in the team high and maybe intimidate the opposition.”

Felicia Schröder gave the Spanish club the lead after just 96 seconds to make it six goals in five appearances since her June transfer from BK Häcken. But Sakina Karchaoui (pictured) was on target from the penalty spot with 16 minutes left to secure a point for PSG. Marit Bratberg Lund scored twice – once from the spot – as Benfica dispatched Juventus 2-1 at Allianz Stadium. Alba Redondo grabbed a late consolation for the hosts. Thank you for your feedback.

As the clock edged towards full time, every effort placed high, wide or cut out was wildly celebrated by the Køge substitutes. They were silenced eventually, when Yukina Sakabe upended Selina Cerci in a rare blip from the visiting team and Caldentey converted from the spot.

It was crushing for the visiting team, but Mørch was delighted with his team. “Around minute 80, I came to terms with the idea that if something happens, something happens,” he said. “We were so pressed at that point that these things will sometimes happen. So, for me, I’m not going to say the game ended there, but my judgment of the overall ­performance kind of ended there. I’ve seen what I could dream of from the team.”

Relief filled the stands packed with red and white after the goal, but with Chelsea up next, nerves of another wasteful season will not settle.

Sports.title: Wamser rescues point for Manchester City in WCL fightback at Bayern Munich
Sports.content:
Manchester City produced a gutsy performance to fight back and earn a valuable 2-2 draw away at Bayern Munich on their return to the Champions League. José Barcala’s side took the lead through Giulia Gwinn and an unfortunate Kerstin Casparij own goal but Beth Mead and Carlotta Wamser earned the visitors a hard-earned point.

City’s head coach, Andrée Jeglertz, was pleased with the resolve of his side after a difficult first half. “It [a comeback] has happened before because we know the quality is there,” he said. “The mentality of ­winning and the belief is there. It shows ­something about this group again.

“There were definitely two phases of this game. In the first half, Bayern were very good. I think we were a bit slow on the ball … It was almost like we were surprised by the tempo. I know we weren’t but it looked like that. At the end of the first half, we got a little bit back. The trust and the belief at half-time was good so I felt that this is still possible.”

It was always going to be a challenging start for the English champions against a Bayern team who have historically thrived in the league phase of this competition. They came into this unbeaten in their last 15 home group-stage matches and on the back of a semi-final run last ­season that, according to Gwinn, had left them “even hungrier and eager for more”. Not only that but the German team have kicked off the defence of their Frauen-Bundesliga title in stunning fashion with five wins from five.

City also arrived in Germany full of confidence after an equally impressive start to the season. Their 4-2 win over Liverpool on Friday had been a further sign of their mettle, finding a way to win despite not being at their best.

Quick Guide WCL roundup: PSG peg back Real Madrid Show Paris Saint-Germain came from behind to clinch a 1-1 draw at Real Madrid in their Women's Champions League opener. Felicia Schröder gave the Spanish club the lead after just 96 seconds to make it six goals in five appearances since her June transfer from BK Häcken. But Sakina Karchaoui (pictured) was on target from the penalty spot with 16 minutes left to secure a point for PSG. Marit Bratberg Lund scored twice – once from the spot – as Benfica dispatched Juventus 2-1 at Allianz Stadium. Alba Redondo grabbed a late consolation for the hosts. The Malta striker Haley Bugeja settled a hard-fought opening game for Inter with a fifth-minute winner that condemned Swedish side BK Häcken to a 1-0 defeat at U-Power Stadium. Häcken's keeper Jennifer Falk was sent off in the 90th minute for a trip as Inter staged a late attack. Press Association Photograph: Alberto Gardin/Getty Images Europe Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

European football, however, presents a different test altogether and they came into this game with plenty of unknowns. How would they measure up after a year out of the competition? Could their injury-hit squad juggle the load of European football and domestic challenges?

Reality hit in a first half during which a refreshed Bayern took control of proceedings. Barcala had been able to make five changes to his starting XI, having completely rested Klara Bühl and Gwinn against Köln on Saturday, and they looked full of energy.

Bühl immediately stretched every sinew of City’s fragile-looking defence with her pace and guile. The 25-year-old was at the heart of everything Bayern created early on, firing a volley wide before setting up the equally prolific Pernille Harder for a half chance.

It did not come as a surprise, therefore, that the hosts broke the deadlock with 11 minutes on the clock. It was a move that cut through the heart of Manchester City as Linda Dallmann broke clear to send Gwinn on her way. The full-back saw the pitch open up in front of her, dispatching a cool finish past Ayaka Yamashita in the City goal.

View image in fullscreen Giulia Gwinn reacts after opening the scoring. Photograph: Matthias Schräder/AP

It was moment when the 4,291-strong crowd raised the decibel level, buoyed by their team’s domination and, perhaps also, the Oktoberfest celebrations. This was Bayern’s first outing at Sportpark Unterhaching and the raucous crowd seemed to settle in straight away at their new home.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The pressure on City continued. Struggling to find space in possession, they were guilty of playing into Bayern’s hands, channelling their attack centrally rather than trying to exploit the wide areas. Things got worse when an unwitting Casparij diverted a dangerous Harder cross into her own net to double the score.

This City side are made of stern stuff, however, and Jeglertz’s ­players were handed a lifeline just before the break, albeit in controversial fashion. As a blue smoke flare blazed on the pitch, the referee allowed play to continue while Casparij burst forward. Her cross was met by Khadija Shaw, whose shot was deflected into the path of Mead, who tapped home.

View image in fullscreen Bayern Munich and Manchester City try to stay focused despite a flare on the pitch. Photograph: Michaela Stache/AFP/Getty Images

The second half was a much more even affair as the pendulum of momentum swung between the teams. City should have had an equaliser when Aoba Fujino was brought down by Ena Mahmutovic only for the goalkeeper to step up and save Shaw’s penalty.

Despite the hosts still looking potent going forward, City could sense that the tide was shifting and found an equaliser with four minutes to play. Wamser, signed from Bayer Leverkusen this summer, arrived unmarked on the edge of the box to rifle home a finish on her return to Germany.

The substitute Edna Imade had two big chances to win it for Bayern late on but the visitors held strong. With one of their most difficult games out of the way, they face Real Madrid next week in Manchester with a chance of making another statement on the European stage.

Sports.title: Real Madrid call for La Liga president’s removal over his response to derby complaints
Sports.content:
Real Madrid want a new La Liga president in light of what they called “intolerable” comments from the incumbent, Javier Tebas, ⁠who said on Tuesday that claims of officiating bias against the club belonged to “another galaxy”.

After losing 2-1 to Atlético Madrid on ⁠Sunday, Real headlined the ⁠match report ​on their website: “Terrible refereeing decides the derby.”

Real were furious that Atlético’s Cristian Romero was not sent off for a stamp on ⁠Jude Bellingham and also complained about a challenge by Lee Kang-in on Federico Valverde.

Real’s manager, José Mourinho, aimed sharp criticism at the referee, Miguel Ángel Ortiz ⁠Arias, and those who appointed him. Mourinho said his side could win the title “if they ​let us compete on a level playing ‌field”.

He brought two printed screenshots of what he thought were red-card tackles committed by players to his post-match press conference.

Tebas responded to a pro-Real article on social media with a lengthy riposte to allegations of a “conspiracy” against the 15-time European champions.

“Here they go again, the mouthpieces and the regime’s television, building the same old narrative – the permanent conspiracy,” said Tebas, who has often been at odds with Real Madrid and the club’s outspoken president, Florentino Pérez.

“This article goes further – it claims that referees harm ‘the business that feeds them’. What exactly is it asking for? Refereeing based on revenue, viewership, or the badge? What a way to understand equality in the competition.

“Real Madrid are crucial to La Liga. But claiming that ‘La Liga is worth nothing’ without them reveals the disdain for the other clubs, their fans, and their history. The competition belongs to no one.”

Real responded with a statement on their website, saying: “Our club considers it intolerable that the president of La Liga uses his institutional position to continue discrediting and attacking ​Real Madrid.

“Given this inappropriate and persistent behaviour, we believe that the professional football competition in Spain urgently needs a leader capable of managing it and realising its full potential with the fundamental duty of neutrality.“

Real sit six points behind the reigning champions and early leaders, Barcelona.

Sports.title: Branthwaite reveals brain study helped him conquer injuries and earn England call
Sports.content:
Jarrad Branthwaite has credited a “complex” rehabilitation programme in Germany, which analysed links between his injuries and his brain and movement, with his return to the England squad.

The Everton defender’s fine start to the season has been rewarded with a place in Thomas Tuchel’s squad for the Nations League fixtures against Spain, Czechia and Croatia. If selected, it will be Branthwaite’s second appearance for the England senior side having been blighted by hamstring and groin problems in recent years.

The centre-half has been ever-present in the Premier League after being restricted to 10 appearances last season by repeated hamstring issues. In the search for a solution to his injury problems, Everton sent the 24-year-old to the MYOS sports and health clinic in Munich at the start of the summer. Branthwaite believes that was a turning point.

“I sat down with the club after the three or four times where I was picking up the injuries,” he said. “It was to look at the wider picture, look at the holistic approach of the body essentially. I went over there for three or four weeks working with a team alongside the club, just to assess different things, and hopefully that has helped. There were a lot of different things looked at like movement patterns, the brain; it was quite complex, but fingers crossed it has worked.”

Branthwaite was carried off in tears after sustaining another hamstring injury in the Merseyside derby defeat by Liverpool in April. The setback ended his season and his prospects of making a late play for the World Cup squad, and Everton’s form also plummeted in his absence.

“It is probably the worst thing as a footballer not to be on the pitch and I think when it keeps happening it is mentally tough because you are sort of doubting your body and going on the pitch wary of what is going to happen. I think now I am in a position where I got managed throughout the pre-season, managed my load well and hopefully I can stay on the pitch this season.”

Branthwaite made his England debut as a substitute in a win against Bosnia and Herzegovina in June 2024, and a recall was a target this season alongside a return to full fitness.

“I found out when I was having breakfast – it was a good start to the day,” the Everton defender said of his call-up last week. “It is a proud moment. Over the last season or so it has been a target of mine. When I have been out and not on the pitch, I wanted to get back playing and give myself the best possible chance to be in and around the England squad after missing such a lot of time.

“The season has started well individually and as a team. England’s got unbelievable talent and players all over the pitch. I believe I am good enough to be in the England squad so hopefully I can show that.”

Sports.title: Reform UK-led council ends support for Show Racism the Red Card
Sports.content:
Anti-racism education in some schools will be scrapped after a city council now led by Reform UK ended its 30-year support for the charity Show Racism the Red Card.

Announcing the decision last week, the Reform leader of Sunderland city council, Christopher Eynon, said it would no longer support “politically charged organisations with an agenda”.

Gary Bennett, the former Sunderland AFC captain and the charity’s head coach, said he was “shocked and disappointed” that Nigel Farage’s party had withdrawn vital funding.

The move prompted a furious backlash from opposition politicians including Labour’s Bridget Phillipson, who described it on Tuesday as “misguided, cruel and in no way backed by the people of Sunderland”.

Bennett, who became only the second black player in Sunderland’s history when he joined the club in 1984, was a founding member of Show Racism the Red Card when it was established in 1996.

View image in fullscreen Gary Bennett in Sunderland’s stripes in 1994. Photograph: PA/Alamy

The former centre-back, who remains a cult hero on Wearside, said he was “surprised, shocked and disappointed” that Sunderland council – the first local authority to have supported it – was cutting its ties after 30 years.

Bennett said it would immediately disrupt the charity’s ability to teach local children in schools and provide workshops in prisons and workplaces.

He said: “We’re not a political charity – they’re trying to say we are but we’re not. Sunderland were the first council to come onboard to help fund us, that’s the annoying thing. For something like this to happen now, we just want to know the reasons why.”

Bennett said the racist riots across many English cities including Sunderland in 2024 showed there was “still lots of work to be done”.

While Britain had come a long way since the 1980s, he said, there remained issues to confront around attitudes towards asylum seekers and migrants.

“You’ve got all different issues going on now. It keeps moving, it’s always something else which causes some form of racism,” he said. “It’s something that is challenging every single day and we’ve got to keep the fight. There’s still lots of work to be done and we can’t just ignore it and think it’s going to go away because it’s not.”

Eynon, whose party gained control of the council in May, said the authority was not “stepping back from its opposition to racism or discrimination” and that “racism has no place in Sunderland”.

He took issue with Ged Grebby, the chief executive of Show Racism the Red Card, describing Reform as a “very dangerous organisation”.

Grebby defended his right to express personal views and said the charity had support across the political spectrum.

Separately, Reform UK has been accused of “vice signalling” after its councillors in Bradford proposed to pull out of the Local Authority of Sanctuary scheme, which is intended to show a city is a safe place for migrant communities.

The Reform group that runs the council said it would be putting forward a motion at the next meeting in October to end the status, which it said has meant the council had “led Refugee Week engagement and utilised local libraries to celebrate all new arrivals into Bradford”, adding that “public services should instead be prioritised for Bradford residents”.

The Reform councillor Jayne Morgan said the move “may upset oversensitive political opponents” but was firmly in the public interest.

In response, Imran Khan, the leader of Bradford’s Labour group, said: “Reform failed to deliver on various promises they made to Bradford residents this summer, so instead they fall back on their usual toxic recipe of hate, victimhood and division.”

He said pulling out of the scheme would “do nothing to help a single person” in Bradford. “This is vice signalling from Reform and all it does is damage integration and promote division and resentment, which helps no one,” he said.

Sports.title: ‘It’s bordering on exploitation’: how pseudoscience is duping football
Sports.content:
Dr Claire-Marie Roberts was working at Coventry City when she received a call from someone asking whether she knew how much oxygen was in the atmosphere. As the performance director, responsible for optimising players’ potential, she was accustomed to being pitched the latest gimmick promising miraculous gains. At times, she could receive up to 50 LinkedIn messages a week offering a device, supplement or technology that claimed to produce magical results.

“It is only 21%,” the caller told her. That’s GCSE chemistry, she thought. Then came the sales pitch: “So what we’ve done is put oxygen in a can and we think you might want to use it.”

“Right … oxygen in a can,” Roberts says, laughing at the memory. Suffice to say, she did not take the caller up on his offer to buy oxygen in a can for Coventry’s players.

Roberts has spent decades working in elite athlete performance and professional football, including nine years at the Premier League and two at Coventry, where she played a key role in their promotion as Championship champions before joining the Formula One team McLaren as director of human performance in the summer. She is shocked by how professional football is being duped by pseudoscience: from coaches and performance staff misled by snake-oil sellers, to players desperate for a shortcut and with money to burn.

“It’s the science-practice gap, which is widening in my experience,” Roberts says. “I think it’s getting much worse. There’s so much sparkly marketing behind all these things. It’s bordering on exploitation.

“They’re taking a population that is very susceptible to: ‘How can I hack my performance advantage? How can I shortcut my preparation and recovery?’ Which I don’t think is a great starting point.”

Roberts says some of the practices commonplace in elite football have little evidence behind them. She includes cryotherapy chambers – a common feature at elite training grounds. If unavailable, ice baths are a fallback. Players enjoy them so much that Harry Kane was photographed standing in a wheelie bin full of ice after a Bayern Munich match at last year’s Club World Cup.

View image in fullscreen Claire-Marie Roberts was part of Frank Lampard’s staff during Coventry’s Championship-winning season. Photograph: Hannah McKay/Reuters

“Most clubs have got cryotherapy chambers – most people cannot articulate to you why they use them, because there’s no evidence for them apart from a very slim piece of work that says it might help prevent dementia,” Roberts says. “There’s very sketchy evidence on cryotherapy.”

They could even be detrimental to recovery, Roberts says. “There’s a recent suggestion that cryotherapy might blunt muscular adaptation. When are you using it and why are you using it? If you’re using it for recovery, sleep and nutrition are your best recovery modalities. No amount of putting anybody in a whole-body cryotherapy chamber is going to help them recover more if those two things aren’t taken care of.”

But players are constantly attempting to shortcut nutrition, too. Supplements are a multibillion-pound industry that has its claws in the game. But beyond vitamin D, in which it is “evidence-based” that people in the northern hemisphere are commonly deficient owing to a lack of sunlight, and vitamin C, which is usually short in our diets, supplementation should, Roberts says, be targeted to deficiencies.

“You’ve got people popping pills not really asking what they’re for. It should always be needs-based. If you don’t eat fish and fish oil is important to you, you might supplement it. It should all be based on need.

“Your athletic performance and recovery is based on sleep quality and nutritional quality and amounts. No amount of supplementation will improve a bad diet, but people think it will. We don’t do enough of the basics and think we can shortcut and hack everything.”

View image in fullscreen Claire-Marie Roberts: ‘Most clubs have got cryotherapy chambers – most people cannot articulate to you why they use them.’ Photograph: Eddie Keogh for The FA/Rex/Shutterstock

Roberts says she used an evidence-based, scientific approach to support Frank Lampard’s squad and that many clubs follow practices from the top of the game when often they are flawed.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Sport in Focus Our picture editors select their favourite sporting images from the past week, from the spectacular to the powerful, and with a little bit of fun thrown in Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“People passively suck these things up,” she says. “Because England or Manchester City or Chelsea who have all the resources under the sun have got this, there’s a misappropriation of confidence and understanding of the scientific basis or evidence. It’s powerful in driving behaviour, but it’s driving the wrong behaviour.”

Roberts, a former swimmer who missed the 1996 Atlanta Olympics owing to injury, says: “Football is more susceptible to it than any other sport I’ve experienced first-hand. I think because the stakes are higher.”

Kinesiology tape – or k-tape, as it is commonly known – is another trend that baffles Roberts. Players from Cristiano Ronaldo to Gareth Bale and David Beckham have been spotted wearing it over the years, often resembling strips of gaffer tape stuck to limbs.

“There’s no evidence kinesiology tape has any impact on injury prevention or performance-related outcomes. It gives you a bit of proprioception – maybe you feel like someone has done something – but in any environment I’ve worked in you’d never see anyone wearing k-tape. It’s a big white elephant.

“If an athlete has dislocated their shoulder, you should strap it – strapping is different. It provides an element of external support that can provide minimal protection to the joint and reminds the person they’ve got a problem. It’s a risk-mitigation strategy. It’s not hugely successful, but you’d do it rather than not do it. K-tape is a placebo.”

Often, managers who have been in the game for decades insist on practices they have adopted for years, or because another coach, with no scientific background, has heard about a revolutionary new product. Roberts believes that until football puts science at the centre of decision-making and employs qualified staff to scrutinise claims, the problem will worsen.

“We think we can accelerate to an outcome without putting the hard yards in – the basic things: diet and sleep and the quality of your training,” she says.

“Football in general is very anti-intellectual and it has been for a long time. There are a few clubs that do it well, but the majority don’t. The game is definitely anti-science. There’s a reason for that. There isn’t a critical mass of people that are applying critical thought to situations.”

Sports.title: ‘Why wouldn’t I?’ – Ex-Premier League star admits he made Saudi Arabia move for the money
Sports.content:
Former Manchester City star Tijjani Reijnders has admitted his move to Saudi Arabia was financially motivated.

The midfielder also revealed his plan to no longer work again once he has hung up his boots.



3 Reijnders swapped Man City for the Saudi Pro League this summer Credit: Getty

The Netherlands international called time on his City career last month after just one season at the club.

The 28-year-old completed a lucrative switch to Saudi Pro League club Al Qadsiah following the arrival of new City boss Enzo Maresca.

The Italian was quick to make reinforcements to his midfield with the big-money signings of Elliot Anderson, Ayoub Bouaddi and Enzo Fernandez.



With Reijnders seemingly now down the pecking order and with Saudi Arabia calling, the Dutchman’s choice was a simple one.

Atletico Madrid showed an interest in the star but the two clubs were unable to agree a fee.



Al Qadsiah had no such issue in meeting City’s £60million valuation and quickly tied up the deal.

Having now played six games for his new club, Reijnders opened up on his motives behind the switch and said the idea of staying at City made him unhappy.



"There were other options, but they did not come through or they stalled over the asking price," Reijnders told Dutch outlet Voetbalzone.

"In the end, I started to think: do I want to stay another season at Man City without being completely happy, or do I choose to take on a new adventure?

“That was when I spoke with Al Qadsiah and with the coach. And after that conversation, I became very excited."

3 Reijnders' hopes of a starting spot decreased significantly after Enzo Maresca's summer shopping spree Credit: Getty



Asked if money was a huge factor behind the move, Reijnders was forthcoming in his reply.

A financially-motivated move

"Money definitely plays a part in it. After my football career ends, I don't want to work again," he added.

“I didn't have to after leaving Manchester City anyway, but now I can also help future generations of my family.

“Security was the priority. I won't lie about it, if my grandchildren can live off this, then why shouldn't I?"



"When you moved to Saudi Arabia, some people accused you of doing it just to fill your pockets with money.

“When you’re offered that kind of salary, just try saying no,” he said.

3 Reijnders netted seven goals in 50 games at the Etihad Stadium Credit: Getty

“Everyone can take the moral high ground and say, ‘I would never do that,’ but I’m pretty sure most people would accept it. In fact, most people would probably accept a promotion in their own job.



“We’re talking here about the kind of money that is almost impossible to turn down.”

The midfielder also quashed the idea that his career would fizzle out by opting for the Saudi Pro League over a top five European league.

"I think many people believe that a player's career ends by moving to Saudi Arabia, but that's not true,” he said.

Netherlands manager Xavi has called upon Reijnders up for the upcoming international matches, which sees them face Germany, Serbia and Greece in the Nations League.

Sports.title: Wayne Rooney says Man United squad is ‘weak’ as he lays out challenge for Michael Carrick
Sports.content:
Wayne Rooney says Man United squad is ‘weak’ as he lays out challenge for Michael Carrick

Manchester United legend Wayne Rooney believes the current squad is weak and needed more signings in the transfer window.

After only signing three outfield players, Man United have gone on to win just one of their opening five Premier League games.



3 Rooney thinks Man United needed to do more summer business and now thinks their squad is 'weak' amid a poor start to the season Credit: Getty

It leaves them 12th in the table and ten points off the top, with any hopes of a potential title push already quashed.

Pressure is starting to build on manager Michael Carrick too, following his permanent appointment in the summer.

Rooney maintains hope that his old teammate and fellow club legend can turn things around after the international break.



But he has admitted that he thinks United should have spent some more money over the summer to improve the squad.

"There's always going to be pressure, Michael knows that," Rooney exclusively told talkSPORT at the premiere of his new Disney+ series 'Real Rooneys'.



"If you're not winning football games at Man United, then that pressure is there if you don't win one game.

"So, it hasn't been the ideal start to the season… there are certain things which I felt the club had to do before the window shut, in bringing players in… the squad is a bit weak."



How can Carrick turn things around?

Rooney then added: "He's got to find a way to get more and the best out of these players to get up the table after this international break… I think the break has come at the right time.

"He's shown that he can get results out of this group of players.

"They have to get their head down and work and hopefully get some better results."

3 Carrick has only won one league game this season and Man United are sitting 12th in the table after five matches Credit: Getty

Rooney: Carrick would have wanted more

Rooney, who went through plenty of hardship himself as a manager, was then asked if he feels some sympathy for Carrick.



The Man United manager only added Youri Tielemans, Carlos Baleba, Andrey Santos and Karl Darlow to his team over the summer.

The Red Devils didn't sign any new defenders or forwards, while Marcus Rashford has also returned to the fold this term.

"He [Carrick] knows what's in for there and listen, you always want more as a manager, I'm sure he would have wanted more from the transfer window, but he's left with what he's left with," Rooney said.

"I think the Premier League has got better, there's better teams in there.



"But if you don't win at Man United, or at any club, at the minute it's very tough, so I hope he turns it around."

3 Rooney spoke exclusively to talkSPORT from the premiere of his new Disney+ series 'The Real Rooneys' Credit: Getty

The Real Rooneys airs on Disney Plus on September 24

Sports.title: Wayne Rooney: JJ Gabriel wanting to leave Man United is no shock, everyone saw this coming
Sports.content:
Wayne Rooney: JJ Gabriel wanting to leave Man United is no shock, everyone saw this coming

Wayne Rooney has admitted that he had seen JJ Gabriel's bombshell request to leave Manchester United coming.

The 15-year-old wonderkid wants to have his registration at Man United cancelled in the hope of securing a move elsewhere.



5 Gabriel's request to leave Man United came as a shock to many, but Rooney wasn't surprised by the news at all Credit: Getty

He has interest from Premier League giants, as well as from Barcelona and Real Madrid, and the player travelled to Spain last week to hold transfer talks over a potential switch.

The news surprised a lot of fans, considering Gabriel was set to become United's youngest ever player just one day later.

He was going to be named in the Red Devils' squad for their Carabao Cup meeting with Brighton at Old Trafford, but after his desire to leave was made clear, he didn't appear.



It now seems like the writing's on the wall, with Gabriel pushing through his wish to depart for a new challenge.

But Man United legend Rooney has revealed that he was not shocked at all to hear that the wonderkid wanted to go...



'Everyone has seen it coming'

Speaking exclusively to talkSPORT from the premiere of his upcoming Disney+ series 'The Real Rooneys', the former striker gave an insight into his knowledge of the situation.

"With the JJ situation, I've seen him growing up, he's been in Kai's team, and I think, if I'm being honest, everyone has seen it coming," Rooney admitted.



"There's been a desire to maybe play abroad, maybe in Spain.

"But we have to remember he's 15, he's still a kid. That's a lot of pressure and you hope that the decisions are being made for the right reasons.

"I actually listened to Michael Carrick talk about it after the Brighton game and I thought he spoke really well. It's such a big story with everything that's going on at Man United that you forget there's a kid involved here."

5 Rooney has known that Gabriel wanted to leave Man United to join a club abroad Credit: Getty

5 Rooney's son Kai has played with Gabriel within the Red Devils' youth system Credit: Getty



Could Kai Rooney take a similar path?

Rooney then went on to speak about his own young star, his 16-year-old son Kai, who currently plays for Man United's U18s.

He has recently signed a one-year scholarship, with the deal turning into a three-year professional contract when he turns 17.

So, it seems the young Rooney is going to be staying in Manchester for the foreseeable future - and his dad says so too.

He told talkSPORT: "Kai has signed a long-term deal at Man United and he's at the place he wants to be, the place I want him to be.



"That's important. He's been at the club a long time and he wants to go and try and play for the first team and be successful."

Kai, a forward, has scored twice and provided one assist in seven appearances for Man United's U18s to date.

5 Rooney is hoping that his old teammate Carrick can turn things round with the 'weak' squad he has available Credit: Getty

What does Rooney think of Man United's start to the season?

Away from Man United's next generation, Rooney then discussed the Red Devils' current first-team squad and the season so far.



Carrick's side have only won one of their opening five Premier League games, having also been knocked out of the Carabao Cup.

It leaves them sitting 12th in the table and pressure is already starting to build on the boss amid boos at Old Trafford.

"There's always going to be pressure, Michael knows that," Rooney said on the tough situation for his old teammate.

"If you're not winning football games at Man United, then that pressure is there, if you don't win one game.



"So, it hasn't been the ideal start to the season... there are certain things which I felt the club had to do before the window shut, in bringing players in... the squad is a bit weak.

5 Rooney spoke exclusively to talkSPORT about Man United's current situation at the premiere of his new Disney+ series 'The Real Rooneys' Credit: Stream The Real Rooneys on Disney+ from 24th September

"But he's got to find a way to get more and the best out of these players to get up the table after this international break... I think the break has come at the right time.

"He's shown that he can get results out of this group of players.

"They have to get their head down and work and hopefully get some better results."



The Real Rooneys airs on Disney Plus on September 24

Sports.title: Liam Rosenior told he lacks class and called ‘crazy’ by former player in astonishing tirade
Sports.content:
Liam Rosenior told he lacks class and called ‘crazy’ by former player in astonishing tirade

Liam Rosenior has been slammed by Strasbourg's former captain following his wild post-match celebrations last weekend.

Paris FC manager Rosenior celebrated in front of his old side's fans after his current team's 2-1 win in Ligue 1 on Saturday.

2 Rosenior sparked a brawl after holding nothing back when celebrating in front of his former club's fans Credit: Shutterstock Editorial

A brawl broke out as Strasbourg's players rushed over to confront the Englishman as he aggressively waved his arms and shouted.

But he refused to apologise for his actions, citing insulting chants about his family from some of the supporters as the reason he goaded them.

However, ex-captain Dimitri Lienard has now launched a tirade on the club's old manager following the incident.

'Have a little more class'

Speaking on the Club Racing show on YouTube, Lienard, who played over 300 games for Strasbourg, said: "Of course I don't condone insults that target family, it's happened to me too.

"But well, if coaches start doing that too, acting like show-offs or going to the stands..."

He added: "He forgot that in his last five matches, and I'm not talking about the European Cup matches... he had three defeats and two draws with Strasbourg before he left. His last victory dates back to November 9, 2025 against Lille."

Lienard then continued his rant against Rosenior, criticising him for leaving Strasbourg for Chelsea in the middle of the season.

The 42-year-old left the French outfit to replace Enzo Maresca as Blues boss in January, also recalling loanee Mamadou Sarr from his old side to join his squad in the Premier League.

"He talks to us about the Champions League. 'If I win it', 'Be happy if I win the Champions League', 'Be proud for me'," Lienard recalled. "But are you kidding me?!

"You go to Chelsea in the middle of the season, you take a defender who's the rock for us [Mamadou Sarr] to play him for one match, 90 minutes. You're joking, right?!

2 Rosenior's Paris FC are third in Ligue 1, two points off leaders Monaco Credit: AFP

"And then you come and give us a moral lecture? It's ludicrous, it's ludicrous. Frankly, I was seriously disappointed because I wasn't expecting that.

"I don't condone him being insulted either, but be a little more humble, have a little more class."

What else did Lienard say on Rosenior?

Rosenior explained that despite his decision to hit back at the Strasbourg fans he will always respect the 'wonderful' club.

But Lienard wasn't having any of that, slamming him once again for leaving the club mid-season and causing chaos on his return to face them with Paris FC last Saturday.

He said: "It wasn't 'thank you, you're welcome', it was 'goodbye'. Not a thank you to the people of Strasbourg.

"What did he think? That we were going to erect a statue in his honour? That we were going to roll out the red carpet for this gentleman? What did he think? That we were going to open a bottle of champagne for him?

"But you are crazy my friend! You are crazy my friend!

"I think he had forgotten the club's values ​​too: humility, respect, hard work."

Sports.title: Real Madrid go to war with LaLiga as they make damning ‘dishonest’ claim
Sports.content:
Real Madrid go to war with LaLiga as they make damning ‘dishonest’ claim

Real Madrid have published an explosive statement aimed at LaLiga president Javier Tebas following comments on social media.

Tebas was critical of the 36-time LaLiga champions following Sunday’s 2-1 defeat at city rivals Atletico.



4 Jude Bellingham was the recipient of a heavy challenge form Cristian Romero that angered boss Jose Mourinho Credit: Getty

4 There were other incidents that left Real Madrid incensed too Credit: Getty

Real Madrid released a statement after the match titled ‘A dreadful refereeing performance decides the derby’, criticising the referee Miguel Angel Ortiz’s decision not to send off both Kang-in Lee and Cristian Romero for robust challenges on Federico Valverde and Jude Bellingham respectively.

Boss Jose Mourinho later produced a picture of Lee's challenge on Valverde while slamming the decision not to dismiss the South Korean.



But Tebas further angered Real Madrid on Tuesday when he responded to an article on social media claiming there was a 'conspiracy' against the club.

What did Tebas say about Real Madrid?

“Here they go again, the mouthpieces and the regime’s television, building the same old narrative – the permanent conspiracy,” Tebas said.



“This article goes further – it claims that referees harm ‘the business that feeds them’. What exactly is it asking for? Refereeing based on revenue, viewership, or the badge? What a way to understand equality in the competition.

“Real Madrid are crucial to LaLiga. But claiming that ‘LaLiga is worth nothing’ without them reveals the disdain for the other clubs, their fans, and their history. The competition belongs to no one.”



The 15-time European champions responded to the statement on their website on Tuesday evening describing Tebas’ comments as ‘intolerable’.

The statement read: “In response to the statements made by the president of LaLiga, Javier Tebas Medrano, Real Madrid C. F. wishes to state the following.

“Our club considers it intolerable that the president of LaLiga uses his institutional position to continue discrediting and attacking Real Madrid in the manner he does in each of his public interventions.

“It is also very concerning that someone who is responsible for representing and protecting the interests of all LaLiga clubs is repeatedly obsessed with targeting Real Madrid, turning our club into a constant subject of his public attacks.



4 Mourinho came well equipped to his post-match press conference Credit: Getty

“His latest remarks are particularly serious and incomprehensible, unbecoming of a responsible manager, as they are made in response to an article by an independent journalist in a digital media outlet.

“However, he reacts against our club and goes as far as to comment on our sporting strategy, which is entirely inappropriate and irresponsible.

“It is utterly surprising that the president of LaLiga dedicates his time and personal platforms to constantly trying to publicly discredit Real Madrid, instead of contributing, from the responsibility of his position, to fostering trust in the institutions that must ensure the impartiality of the competition.



“By doing so, he continues to damage the image of our competition and Spanish football worldwide.”

Real Madrid call for new leadership

Los Blancos then called upon senior figures to consider replacing Tebas, claiming the league needs a leader who shows impartiality across the league’s 20 teams.

“Given this inappropriate behavior, which has persisted over time, we believe that professional football in Spain urgently needs a leader capable of managing it and developing its full potential with the fundamental duty of neutrality.

4 Tebas has been LaLiga president since 2013



“It needs someone who understands the nature of their role, as the president of LaLiga is not the owner of the competition but a manager serving the clubs that comprise it and entrust him with its direction. The clubs need someone who serves this mission with honesty.”

Real Madrid have made a mixed start to the LaLiga season having picked up 15 points from their opening seven matches.

Mourinho’s side sit in fourth place, six points adrift of pace setters Barcelona and are also behind Atletico and Real Betis.

Sports.title: Paul Gascoigne reveals the one thing that ‘drives him nuts’ about England players
Sports.content:
Paul Gascoigne reveals the one thing that ‘drives him nuts’ about England players

Paul Gascoigne has expressed his deep frustration at the lack of emotion shown by modern England players.

Gascoigne, who played 57 times for the Three Lions revealed the pride he felt every time he wore the national shirt.



3 Will Thomas Tuchel include showing more emotion in his pep talk during the international break? Credit: Getty

The debate about players' commitment to England has been brought to widespread attention after a number of players withdrew from the squad.

Five high-profile players pulled out of Thomas Tuchel's squad for the upcoming UEFA Nations League fixtures against Spain, Czechia, and Croatia.

Cole Palmer is one of several players who have left the squad, with Declan Rice, Tino Livramento, Kobbie Mainoo and Marcus Rashford all returning to the parent sides 'due to respective injury issues'.



However, four of those players had started for their clubs in the Premier League over the weekend and did not appear to leave the pitch injured.

Morgan Gibbs-White and James Garner have since been drafted into the England squad for the upcoming Nations League clashes.



Speaking on talkSPORT Breakfast, Gazza highlighted his dismay at what he perceives as a lack of patriotism and pride among the current generation.

He said: "I mean, I loved playing for my country. You know, putting on that white shirt, I just thought of my family, made them proud, you know.



"It's quite emotional now talking about it. Playing for your country means so much.

"I see some of the players when they score and they don't really celebrate. And that drives me nuts. You know, I remember when I made my debut for the Under-21s and it was a tournament tour...

"I scored and there was no one in the crowd. So I jumped over the fence and celebrated on the motorway. Yeah, I was on the motorway again.

3 Gascoigne is regarded as one of English football's best ever talents Credit: GETTY



"You see some of them and they pull out the squad. It's not very good.

"But the thing is with Bobby Robson, it didn’t matter how bad you played for your club, if you played well for England, he would pick you again. So you knew that, but when you keep chopping and changing, some players get fed up with it."

Palmer out

Many pundits have specifically been critical of Palmer, who was reinstated into Tuchel's squad with the Chelsea man suffering a 2026 World Cup snub.

The 24-year-old had the entire summer break after his omission to recover from a lingering groin injury and critics have pointed out that the midfielder has only played five games in the Premier League so far this season.



Gascoigne, considered one of England's greatest ever players, was called up to the England under-21 side in the summer of 1987 and scored with a free-kick in his debut in a 2–0 win over Morocco.

Following his performance, he was then called up to the senior squad by Bobby Robson for a friendly against Denmark in September 1988 and came late in the game for Peter Beardsley in a 1–0 win.

Teammate Bryan Robson referred to the midfielder as 'challenging Maradona as the best player in the world' at the 1990 World Cup.

3 Gazza demanded more emotion from the current crop of England players on talkSPORT Breakfast on Tuesday Credit: talkSPORT



Graham Taylor replaced Robson as the England boss and switched Gascoigne in favour of 32-year-old Gordon Cowans.

However, once Gascoigne returned to peak fitness, he immediately reclaimed his spot for a crucial World Cup qualifier against Norway.

He remained an integral figure for England across successive managerial reigns, including under Glenn Hoddle.

However, prior to the 1998 World Cup squad selection the midfielder was pictured on a night out, prompting Hoddle not to pick him in the final squad.



After hearing the news, Gascoigne wrecked Hoddle's room in a rage. He would never play for England again.

Sports.title: Premier League rival offers Dejan Kulusevski return update
Sports.content:
Dejan Kulusevski's international teammate and Premier League rival Yasin Ayari has given the latest on his injury recovery.

Kulusevski is now nearing 500 days out of action after suffering a knee injury in May 2025 that has seen him sidelined.

3 Kulusevski has not played a game since May 2025 amid a long, gruelling recovery, but he is now getting closer to a return to action Credit: Getty

The Tottenham midfielder has been through multiple setbacks, missing an entire season and a World Cup with Sweden.

But Brighton's Ayari has lauded his good friend and teammate for his mental strength during his 'not normal' recovery period.

Kulusevski finally returned to Spurs training earlier this month and has been back alongside his teammates this week.

It marked an incredible feat to work his way back and it seems that he is closing in on long-awaited return to action.

When could Kulusevski return?

Speaking to Swedish outlet Fotbollskanalen, Ayari admitted he didn't know any specifics but that he is making progress.

Ayari said: “He has started training and is making progress. I’m happy for him, that he can come back and do what he loves.

"I just hope things will go well when he’s 100 per cent."

"I don’t know [when he will be back]. I don’t see him every day,” he added. "We’ve all missed him in the national team. Hopefully soon.

"It’s hard for me to say [if he’ll be match fit soon]. I don’t see him every day, I only talk to him. I hope soon.

"He’s back on the training pitch, so step by step we hope he’ll be back. When he’s back, he’ll be 100 per cent.”

3 Kulusevski is back in Spurs training and is nearing a comeback, with Ayari positive when giving the latest on his Sweden teammate Credit: Getty

Sweden manager Graham Potter opted not to select Kulusevski in his squad for the three-week international break.

Potter was keen for him to reintegrate at Tottenham first before considering bringing him back to the national set-up.

Ayari hails 'incredible' Kulusevski

Ayari also discussed his envy for Kulusevski's mentality after going through such a long period away from football.

“He has always been fit and taken care of his body," the 22-year-old said. "It’s mostly mental, seeing how mentally strong he has been during this process.

“That he has managed to have a smile on his face even when it has taken so long. There have always been setbacks, but he always wakes up happy."

“It’s incredible how strong he has been during this journey," he added. "There aren’t many people who can wake up and keep fighting when they’ve been through so much.

3 Ayari has hailed Kulusevski for his mental strength throughout his time on the sidelines Credit: Getty

“He keeps fighting and is happy at the same time. When it comes to that, it’s not normal.

"He’s very strong mentally. I learn a lot from it.”

Sports.title: Roy Keane refuses to apologise to Andy Robertson over iconic ‘big baby’ jibe
Sports.content:
Roy Keane has refused to apologise to Andy Robertson for calling him a ‘big baby’ following an altercation with an assistant referee.

Whilst at Liverpool in 2023, Robertson claimed he had been elbowed in the throat by linesman Constantine Hatzidakis during a 2-2 draw with Arsenal.



3 Robertson brought his nine-year stint at Liverpool to an end in the summer Credit: Getty

The Scotland left-back was incensed after Hatzidakis appeared to swing at him on his way off the pitch for the half-time interval.

But in the Sky Sports studio, pundit Keane had little sympathy for Robertson and told him to get on with the game.

"He should be more worried about his defending," said the Manchester United legend on television at half time.



"Do you know what he is? That Robertson, I’ve watched him a number of times. He’s a big baby. That’s what that guy is.

"Just get on with the game and concentrate on your defending. He does grab the linesman first."



Unimpressed, Keane went on to repeat the word 'baby' in a hilarious reaction which had Jamie Carragher, Gary Neville, Micah Richards and host Dave Jones in stitches - and it's regularly found online to this day.

Keane meets Robertson

Now, more than three years later, Robertson and Keane came face-to-face and revisited the notorious incident.



The former Liverpool defender, who currently plays for Tottenham, was a guest on the latest episode of The Overlap alongside Keane, Ian Wright, Gary Neville, Jamie Carragher and Jill Scott.

After the incident was brought up on the podcast, Robertson admitted the incident had been 'something over nothing', before Keane shared the reason behind his frosty reaction.

Keane remarked: "Players have to remember, and this is not an apology, when in the studio, we can have long days can't we?

3 Robertson had claimed to have been elbowed by linesman Hatzidakis in the 2023 incident



3 Keane was typically honest as he doubled down on his 2023 comments Credit: X @WeAreTheOverlap

"It can be a bit flat, sometimes a player can do something and you're agitated by having a long day."

Responding to Keane, Robertson jokingly quipped: "The first two 'babies' were alright, the third was one too far."

This left all pundits amused, before Keane responded in light-hearted fashion by insisting he felt under pressure to react strongly on air.



He said: "In my defence, when I said it - we get agitated with traffic all the way to game, but then none of them [his fellow pundits] are saying anything.

"I'm looking at them going: 'You've got to say something', that's why I put the last 'baby' in.

"They're all staring at me like, 'f****** say something'. Am I right?"

Robertson then finished by jokingly taking aim at Carragher, who had laughed at Keane during the original incident.



"I wasn't happy with you [Carragher] laughing either by the way," the Scotland captain said.

Ultimately, linesman Hatzidakis faced no punishment from the PGMOL for the incident, but then went almost two years before assisting another Liverpool game up in January 2025.

Robertson, meanwhile, left the Reds in the summer after nine years at Anfield and has since joined Spurs on a free transfer.

His start to life in north London has been far from easy though, with Roberto De Zerbi's side without a win from their first five Premier League matches this season and bottom of the table.

Sports.title: Olympic gymnast Simone Biles reveals three masked men broke into Chicago home and stole her six-figure Porsche
Sports.content:
Simone Biles has revealed three masked intruders broke into her Chicago home and stole her luxurious Porsche.

The legendary Team USA gymnast dropped the bombshell news during a TikTok video this week. It remains unclear when the burglary happened or if the police have made any arrests but Biles confirmed the car was recovered.

'Feel like I need a new car because during our last few months in Chicago, three men in masks came to our house and stole my Porsche,' she said.

'Stole the GTS. But that's another story. If you guys want to know, I'll do a story time on that.'

Biles shared the property in Chicago with her NFL husband Jonathan Owens, who now plays for the Indianapolis Colts but did play for the Bears in 2024 and 2025.

'I feel like I need a reality TV show,' Biles added. 'The things that happen to me are absolute insanity, and so it would be really easy for producers to just film regularly.'

Simone Biles revealed three masked men broke into her Chicago home and stole her Porsche

The legendary Team USA gymnast dropped the bombshell news during a TikTok video

In another TikTok posted soon after, Biles could be seen uncovering an expensive new Lamborghini at a dealership in Houston.

Biles, who said the burglary was one of the reasons why her and Owens got their new Doberman, joins a growing list of superstar athletes who have been the victims of burglaries in recent years.

In May, Argentine police arrested two Chilean citizens suspected of being part of a transnational gang that orchestrated burglaries at the homes of well-known athletes, including stars from the NBA and NFL.

According to local police, the two were part of a crime ring that targeted the homes of prominent athletes in the US and Argentina, including NFL stars Patrick Mahomes and Travis Kelce and former tennis player Juan Martín del Potro.

Targets also included the homes of NBA players Luka Doncic and Mike Conley Jr.

In 2024, the NFL issued a security alert to teams and the players´ union following the burglaries involving the homes of Mahomes and Kelce.

According to the FBI, organized crime groups from South America used publicly available information and social media to track athletes´ habits and travel.

The groups used technology allowing them to bypass alarm systems, block wireless internet connections and disable devices, cover security cameras and hide their identities.

Jewelry, millions of dollars in cash, trophies and medals were among items stolen from residences while the athletes were out of town.

In another TikTok posted soon after, Biles could be seen uncovering a new Lamborghini

Biles shared the Chicago property with husband Jonathan Owens, who now plays for the Colts

In July, there was also a break-in at the home of Philadelphia Eagles running back Saquon Barkley.

Earlier this month, Biles was seen on the sidelines supporting her man for his first NFL game of the season.

Biles stepped onto the turf at Lucas Oil Stadium to watch Owens make his debut for the Colts against the Baltimore Ravens after arriving in Indianapolis in free agency.

She continued her tradition of dressing up in custom gear with Owens' name and number on it. This time, she arrived in a royal blue dress made out of Owens' brand-new jerseys. His name and number were seen down the left side of the garment as well as on her chest.

Sports.title: Man City flop Tijjani Reijnders brazenly admits he went to Saudi Arabia for the money - insisting he doesn't want to work after retiring from football
Sports.content:
Man City flop Tijjani Reijnders brazenly admits he went to Saudi Arabia for the money - insisting he doesn't want to work after retiring from football

Manchester City reject Tijjani Reijnders has admitted that he moved to Saudi Arabia for the vast financial benefits.

The 28-year-old midfielder left Man City over the summer for the relatively unknown Saudi outfit Al-Qadsiah in a £52million deal.

He spent just a season at the Etihad and, despite a hugely impressive debut after joining them from AC Milan for £46.5m, he struggled to make a consistent impact across his 50 appearances.

Reijnders is on a five-year contract with Al-Qadsiah, who are managed by Brendan Rodgers, and is reportedly set to earn around £86million over the half-decade.

Now a month into his time there, he said: 'Once my playing career is over, I don’t want to have to work anymore.

'Of course, I probably wouldn’t have needed to work anymore after my contract at Manchester City either, but this move allows me to secure the future of the next generations of my family.

Former Manchester City midfielder Tijjani Reijnders has admitted he moved to Saudi Arabia for the money

He says he wants to secure generational wealth, thinking ahead to his future grandchildren

'I’m not going to lie about that. By signing this contract, I can make sure even my grandchildren are financially secure, so why wouldn’t I do it?'

He currently has one son, Xavien, with his wife Marina. Speaking about what attracted him to the club in August, Reijnders was not so quick to mention cash.

He said at the time: 'Especially the ambition of the club (is what attracted me).

'The club wants to be the biggest in Asia and what they did already in the past and what we can do now in the future, it triggered me a lot.

'And, yeah, I want to help the club to bring it to the highest level.

'I came here to try and win trophies with my teammates - we're playing for four trophies, if I'm right.

'We want to win as many as possible and we are all very eager to do that. And, personally, I hope I can help the team as much as possible with goals and assists.'

The Netherlands international has scored three goals in five Saudi Pro League outings for Al-Qadsiah, who also feature in the AFC Champions League.

They are currently fourth in the Saudi Pro League, where they have finished for the last two seasons.

The club is owned by the Saudi Arabian Oil Company, the majority state-owned petroleum and natural gas firm.

They do not have as many big names as some of their Middle Eastern counterparts but do have some respected faces from around Europe, such as former Spain and Italy defender Nacho Fernandez and Italy striker Mario Retegui.

Reijnders played three matches for the Netherlands at the World Cup.

Sports.title: Furious Real Madrid turn on 'intolerable' LaLiga president Javier Tebas with explosive statement calling for him to resign after mocking their 'conspiracy' complaints over refereeing
Sports.content:
Furious Real Madrid turn on 'intolerable' LaLiga president Javier Tebas with explosive statement calling for him to resign after mocking their 'conspiracy' complaints over refereeing

Real Madrid have called for 'intolerable' LaLiga president Javier Tebas to resign - after he mocked their complaints about refereeing.

The Spanish giants were furious with the officiating in the Madrid derby, which they lost 2-1 to city rivals Atletico.

It prompted Jose Mourinho to rant about the 'poor' referee Ortiz Arias, who he suggested was unqualified, and led to the club releasing an official statement condemning the 'very terrible refereeing'.

They felt that Cristian Romero and Lee Kang-In should have been sent off - the former for a stamp on Jude Bellingham and the latter for a challenge on Federico Valverde.
