In the aftermath, LaLiga boss Tebas responded to an article which claimed there was a 'conspiracy' against Madrid, saying that 'claiming that referees are directed against Real Madrid is living in another galaxy.'

But now Madrid have hit back, writing: 'Our club considers it intolerable that the president of LaLiga uses his institutional position to continue discrediting and attacking Real Madrid.

Real Madrid have called for LaLiga president Javier Tebas (above) to resign after he mocked their complaints over refereeing in the capital city derby

Jose Mourinho was furious at the refereeing performance of Ortiz Arias (right) on Sunday

Mourinho was so livid at the refereeing performance that he printed out fouls he felt were missed, calling for two red cards

'Given this inappropriate and persistent behaviour, we believe that the professional football competition in Spain urgently needs a leader capable of ​managing it and realising ​its full potential ⁠with the fundamental duty of neutrality.

'His latest intervention is particularly serious and incomprehensible - unbecoming of a responsible administrator - as it involves commenting on an article by an independent journalist in a digital media outlet.

'Yet, he reacts against our club by taking the liberty of critiquing our sporting strategy - an utterly absurd and irresponsible move.'

Tebas' comment in full had read: 'Claiming that referees are directed against Real Madrid is living in another galaxy.

'That narrative serves as an excuse to cover up other shortcomings that are plain to see in these first matches of the season.

'It's more comfortable to point to a conspiracy than to explain what's happening on the pitch.'

Real Madrid were reduced to 10 men in the derby after Dean Huijsen dragged down Giuliano Simeone in the penalty box.

That allowed Alejandro Grimaldo to convert from the spot, before Jonathan David doubled Atletico's lead. Madrid got a late goal back via Antonio Rudiger.

Mourinho was in disbelief at a referee he is adamant will never make it to the highest level

Real Madrid's Jude Bellingham was furious at officials after Cristian Romero was not sent off

The result leaves Madrid fourth in the table, six points behind league leaders Barcelona, who have a perfect record. They also trail Atletico and Real Betis.

Manager Mourinho was seething in his press conference and arrived with printed out photos which showed, in his opinion, a series of major calls missed by the referee.

'We could save ourselves the press conference,' an irritated Mourinho began.

'Here they are [shows photos of the possible red cards], two clear reds. It would have been 50 minutes of 11 against nine. All I can do is hug my players, who gave everything, who produced a first half full of class and personality. I prepared the match so we could win it in the second half.'

'The one who should be happy is the Refereeing Appointments Committee because the whole thing was very strange,' Mourinho's rant continued.

'A week in advance, they already knew who the referee would be, when it used to be 24 hours before. A 41-year-old referee, who has never been an international, that won't be top level.

'The poor guy came here and couldn't handle the pressure.

'The pressure here is like something out of the 1980s. Trujillo, the VAR official, called him over for the first red and didn't call him over for the second, which was even clearer. This Trujillo has a history with Real Madrid: last year in the Copa final, Osasuna, Girona...

🚨🫵🏽 Jude Bellingham against the referee at full time: “Two red cards! Two!”.@postunited — oscarolleroo on IG 📸 pic.twitter.com/1qkCTlsMUO — Fabrizio Romano (@FabrizioRomano) September 20, 2026

'If the poor referee has no experience, no stature for a derby, then this man is either under no pressure, or under a kind of pressure we know nothing about.

'I would have liked to leave here with the win or without having to speak. I arrived here three months ago and you know I'm not usually one to go in this direction.

'Two reds against Elche and we won. Two reds today, that's already more difficult. It's a referee with only small matches behind him and a VAR official who has a history.

'Congratulations to the Refereeing Appointments Committee.'

In an official club statement, Real Madrid said: 'Real Madrid lose the derby at the Metropolitano in a match marked by Ortiz Arias' VERY TERRIBLE REFEREEING.

'He failed to send off Cuti Romero in the first half for stepping on Bellingham's knee (despite going to the monitor to review the incident), nor did he send off Lee Kang-In for stepping on Valverde's left ankle.

'Both decisions had an impact on the match, which was ultimately decided in Atlético's favor in the second half.'

Sports.title: Alan Shearer accuses Tottenham of overspending on £330m summer makeover and claims splurging an 'absolute fortune' has only piled on pressure - as he questions the 'ability' of Sandro Tonali, Savio and Co
Sports.content:
Alan Shearer has accused Tottenham of overspending as their £330million summer splurge has left them bottom of the Premier League.

Spurs splashed huge money on Sandro Tonali (£100m), Mateus Fernandes (£85m), Savio (£85m), Jan Paul van Hecke (£52m), and Tosin Adarabioyo (£7m) but have picked up just two points in five games.

Shearer has questioned the 'ability' of Tottenham's new signings, with pressure mounting on Roberto De Zerbi to get a tune out of them.

He told Betfair: 'I guess De Zerbi went into this summer with a list of players that he wanted and they have spent a fortune perhaps on all those players.

'I'm not sure the fees warrant the ability, but no one would have expected them to be bottom of the league.'

He added: 'I've said many times, that they brought the players in this summer, but they spent an absolute fortune on them. On everyone, I think.

Alan Shearer has accused Tottenham over overspending and questioned the 'ability' of their signings

The club have endured a nightmare start to the season under Roberto De Zerbi and are bottom of the Premier League

'Van Hecke was a lot of money, Tonali was incredible money, Savio, and Marmoush (on loan) are others as well. It is a long, long three weeks for Tottenham and they simply have to start winning football games when they are back from the international break.

'All the bigger questions will start to be asked, if not already, if they don’t start winning football games very, very soon.

'I still think they'll have enough to stay up. They'll use the Aston Villa situation and what happened to them at the start of last season when I don't think they won in their first five games and they then managed to climb the league and qualify for Europe again.

'They will look at that and think there's still loads of football to be played, which there is, but there's a massive amount of work to be done at Spurs.

'I had them to finish in the top six this season and I am not sure that that will happen now.'

Tottenham did manage to register their first Premier League goals of the season late on in the 3-2 defeat by Aston Villa.

But that was only late on, when the game was lost and many of the fans had already left the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.

De Zerbi tore into his men after an abysmal performance in that defeat, saying: 'I am very disappointed, sad and frustrated with the performance.

Spurs spent £329million over the summer, including £85m on Savio from Manchester City

New man Jan Paul van Hecke was at fault for one of Aston Villa's goals over the weekend - but did score later

'We can’t lose the game in this way, we can’t concede the second goal (a simple ball over the top), we can’t lose balance just because we are losing.

'I spoke with our four attackers in minute 51, I asked them to use their head, all second half I was telling people to be calm. But the second goal was incredible.'

Van Hecke fluffed his lines when Villa goalkeeper Zion Suzuki punted it long, allowing Nicolas Jackson to race through for the opposition's second goal.

De Zerbi added: 'We knew this season Aston Villa are playing 86 per cent more long balls than last season and we spoke in many meetings about it. Now we have to explain another game like (Newcastle) where we played the first half well, got to 60 minutes OK, and then we lose.'

The only match Spurs have won this campaign was a 5-1 thrashing of Championship side Charlton in the second round of the Carabao Cup.

This is the first time they have been bottom of the Premier League since January 2009.

They are second-bottom of the league goalscoring charts, just one goal ahead of Coventry, but have had the ninth-most shots, suggesting that finishing is an issue.

Steven Gerrard pointed to their striking issues on TNT Sports, saying: 'I think Spurs have improved in certain areas, but they've not got a poacher.

'They've not got a goalscorer. They've got some exciting players in the front line, but who is going to get you 20 goals?'

Their only natural striker is Dominic Solanke - with Richarlison exiled - and he has scored 12 goals across two full Premier League seasons with Spurs.

In the summer they sold young English striker Will Lankshear to Middlesbrough for £10m, potentially rising to £20m, and he has scored eight goals in 10 games there.

Tottenham will be looking to make amends quickly after the international break, with their first fixture back coming at Manchester United on October 10.

Sports.title: Liverpool's new Virgil van Dijk, three Chelsea stars and a Spurs summer signing make the cut as stats boffins reveal their Premier League team of the season so far - but there's NO room for Arsenal's David Raya in goal
Sports.content:
It's advantage Manchester City as the Premier League pauses for the first international break of the season after Arsenal suffered a shock 3-0 loss at Brighton.

After five matches, a revamped Tottenham have hit rock bottom while unbeaten Leeds United (fifth) sit above a reviving Liverpool (sixth), an inconsistent Chelsea (tenth) and a struggling Manchester United (12th).

Enzo Maresca has big shoes to fill but he could not have asked for a better start to his reign at City while Alexander Isak could well be the one to challenge Erling Haaland for the Golden Boot... finally.

Newly promoted Hull are enjoying their return to the big time while fellow promoted side Coventry secured their first win of the season in matchweek five.

But which players have stood out and done enough to earn a place in Sofascore's team of the season so far?

Daily Mail Sport takes a look at the Premier League's best XI – and there are a few surprise names...

GK: Emiliano Martinez (Chelsea) – 7.70/10

Sold to Chelsea for a throwaway price of £7.5million by Aston Villa, Emiliano Martínez had every chance to start the new season as the bargain buy of the summer. But the 2026 World Cup finalist has not fully lived up to his billing under new manager Xabi Alonso.

Martinez replaced Robert Sanchez immediately in goal but has struggled to become a fan favourite so far this season. So, how did Martinez make the cut for this team?

In his first game against Brighton, Martinez made four saves in the 4-3 win at home; the visitors had six shots on goal with four big chances. In the London derby against the defending champions, the Chelsea goalkeeper produced eight saves – the most on the Premier League matchday.

With zero clean sheets, Chelsea's defence averages 2.4 goals per game in the top flight. Martinez averages 4.5 saves per game.

His average rating of 7.70 is the highest by any goalkeeper so far this season with his saves per game the highest. Arsenal's impressive No1 David Raya averages 1.8 saves per game.

Emiliano Martinez tops Sofascore's rankings of Premier League goalkeepers with an impressive number of saves among the goals Chelsea have conceded so far

CB: Jeremy Jacquet (Liverpool) – 7.72/10

Signed by Liverpool for £60million in July, Jacquet has already won his first senior call-up to Zinedine Zidane's French national side for their respective international matches.

With Liverpool losing Ibrahima Konate to Real Madrid and Giovanni Leoni to an anterior cruciate ligament injury, the 21-year-old has stepped up seamlessly to team up with captain Virgil van Dijk at the back.

The former Rennes centre back is also showing Liverpool fans what life after the Dutch veteran could look like at Anfield.

Though Isak grabbed the headlines after Liverpool's 1-0 away win at Bournemouth, Jacquet was equally impressive, settling quickly into defence and providing much-needed composure at the back.

The Jacquet-Van Dijk pairing has also earned Liverpool three consecutive clean sheets for the first time in two years. Jacquet has won 76 per cent of his duels this season.

CB: Jan Paul van Hecke (Tottenham) – 7.62/10

For the first time since the 2008-09 season, Tottenham are bottom of the Premier League after five games. At a time when Spurs are struggling badly under Roberto De Zerbi following heavy summer spending, a consistent presence in central defence is a genuine boost.

Jan Paul van Hecke has played every minute of Tottenham's forgettable Premier League campaign so far this season.

Playing all 450 minutes matters early in a season when many new signings are still rotating. With a consolation goal to his name in the 3-2 defeat against Aston Villa, the Dutch centre-back has two clean sheets despite Spurs' winless run.

CB: Lewis Dunk (Brighton) – 7.70/10

Fresh from smashing a showstopper against Frank Lampard's Coventry, Brighton defender Lewis Dunk has played 360 minutes for Fabian Hurzeler's men.

His second Premier League goal from outside the box was also his first since his clever free-kick against Liverpool in 2019.

Averaging four clearances per game, Dunk has enjoyed two clean sheets in four starts.

Nursing a knee injury, Dunk was replaced by Olivier Boscagli for Brighton's crucial league clash with Arsenal.

Despite missing the services of the 34-year-old, Hurzeler's men stunned holders Arsenal 3-0 to secure third place in the table.

CDM: Granit Xhaka (Sunderland) – 7.66/10

Losing his place in the Switzerland squad over a fake vaccine certificate, Granit Xhaka is the only central defensive midfielder named in the team of the season after five rounds.

Xhaka has created five big chances for Sunderland and the 33-year-old is averaging 1.2 interceptions and 1.8 tackles per game across the first five matches.

The Sunderland captain has also impressed with his ball recoveries (6.6 per game) this season.

With a 67 per cent dribble success rate, he has won 60 per cent of his duels across 450 minutes for Regis Le Bris's men.

Xhaka's sublime delivery paved the way for hat-trick hero Brian Brobbey to complete a historic treble against Manchester City, although the Sunderland midfielder is still waiting for his first assist of the new season.

Granit Xhaka has impressed both defensively and as an a creative force for Sunderland

CAM: Martin Odegaard (Arsenal) – 7.60/10

Leading the Gunners from the front, Martin Odegaard delivered when it mattered the most – the London derby.

The Arsenal captain earned a 9.2 rating after he netted the winner against Chelsea. He also made four key passes and created two big chances against Alonso's men.

Odegaard enjoys 1.4 shots per game and has a goal conversion of 29 per cent after five matches.

Arsenal's captain has found the net with either foot for his side. With a passing accuracy of 91 per cent, the 27-year-old is also drawing 1.2 fouls per game.

A calm and smooth operator on the field, Odegaard averages 2.4 balls recovered per game.

He has made the team of the week twice and has looked back to his best so far this season.

CAM: Morgan Rogers (Chelsea) – 7.68/10

Before Odegaard flourished, Morgan Rogers announced his arrival in the London derby with a volley to beat Arsenal's Raya.

The £117million signing registered an assist in Chelsea's high-scoring Stamford Bridge draw with Brighton and found the net against Hull City, only for the Blues to then turn in a toothless performance at Brentford.

With three goals and one assist under his belt, Rogers averages 88 minutes per game for the Blues so far this season.

He is expected to draw at least one foul from the opposition and his passing accuracy ranges from 75 to 80 per cent. The former Villa star is also defensively strong averaging 4.6 balls recovered per game.

RW: Bukayo Saka (Arsenal) – 7.56/10

Besides being a constant threat on the right wing and threading defence-splitting passes, Bukayo Saka has been pivotal for Mikel Arteta's Arsenal so far this season, and like Odegaard is in fine form.

It only took 23 minutes for Saka to open his Premier League account in Arsenal's 3-0 win over Coventry City on matchday one at the Emirates Stadium last month.

When the Gunners travelled to Birmingham to face Unai Emery's Aston Villa, Saka scored the only goal of the match to give the defending champions all three points.

The England international then converted his penalty late in the 97th minute against Sunderland to further enhance his goal tally. He has an XG of 3.21 goals.

LW: Marcus Tavernier (Bournemouth) – 7.62/10

Marcus Tavernier slotted home Bournemouth's only goal in their 2-1 loss at Manchester City on matchday one, before the Cherries shared the spoils in a 1-1 draw with Everton.

With his side developing a trend of conceding late goals, the 27-year-old opened the scoring again at Newcastle – only to witness a Jacob Ramsey equaliser in the 88th minute.

The scoreline remained identical against Brentford for the hosts when Tavernier scored in the 52nd minute, before the visitors found the equaliser four minutes later.

Tavernier has three goals to his name, has featured in team of the week twice and averages 1.6 shots on target per game.

Marcus Tavernier has already bagged three goals for Bournemouth this season

ST: Joao Pedro (Chelsea) – 7.63/10

Fernando Torres, Radamel Falcao, Alvaro Morata, Gonzalo Higuain, Romelu Lukaku and Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang all failed to live up to expectations after taking the No 9 shirt. Joao Pedro has flipped the script at Stamford Bridge.

Scoring in the first minute, Pedro assisted Cole Palmer, who decided Chelsea's five-goal thriller against Fulham at Craven Cottage. A goal and an assist – the same story followed against Brighton.

Following a quiet outing against Arsenal where he only managed a solitary shot on goal, the 24-year-old returned with his 'assist, goal and repeat' drill against Hull City.

Three goals and three assists. A strong start. Chelsea lost 3-0 at Brentford last week with the Brazilian forward out injured.

ST: Erling Haaland (Manchester City) – 7.60/10

No surprise here. With Haaland leading the Premier League goalscoring charts, Maresca's City have opened the season with five straight league wins for the first time since 2017.

Haaland added Sunderland to the 25-team strong list of different clubs against which the Manchester City forward has found the back of the net in the Premier League.

The Man City striker needed three meetings to score his first goal against Sunderland, after failing to do so in both outings last season.

After ending his goalless run against Sunderland, Haaland is now averaging one goal per game in the English top flight.

Averaging two shots on goal per game, the 26-year-old has an XG of 4.43 goals.

Haaland has taken his goal tally to 117 in 137 league appearances. Will anyone be able to stop him this season?

Sports.title: OLIVER HOLT: Thomas Tuchel is indulging in some elite-level gaslighting by blaming Argentina defeat on his players. No, it was the England manager's first big test - and he blew it spectacularly
Sports.content:
OLIVER HOLT: Thomas Tuchel is indulging in some elite-level gaslighting by blaming Argentina defeat on his players. No, it was the England manager's first big test - and he blew it spectacularly

Thomas Tuchel wants to forget about the recent past. Argentina in the semi-finals of the World Cup just over two months ago? Our best chance to get to the final for 60 years?

Let’s move on, eh? In fact, let’s have a bit of a laugh about it. Tactics? Nobody wants to talk about tactics, Tuchel says.

Only the pesky press want to talk about tactics, Tuchel says, as if that is something the media should be ashamed of. Heaven forfend that some England fans still feel bitter about why the dream died. The real people, Tuchel says, just want to remember Mexico and the glory of the Azteca.

I want to remember Mexico, too. I’ll never forget it. It was one of the greatest football occasions I’ve ever witnessed. I’ll always be grateful to Tuchel for the fact he masterminded that beautiful victory. It was one of England’s greatest performances at a tournament. It was also a last-16 game.

Unfortunately, I’ll never forget the Argentina tie, either. I’ll never forget the missed opportunity. Tuchel and the FA might want to move on to the Nations League campaign stretching ahead of us over the next few weeks and the tie against Spain at Wembley on Saturday but I can’t do it. Not yet.

Tuchel seems flatly unable to accept that he got anything wrong against Argentina. He and those around him are trying to style it out. It’s not him, it’s us. And by ‘us’, I mean English football. We are petty for still dissecting it, apparently.

Thomas Tuchel wants us all to move on from the World Cup semi-final defeat to Argentina. Well, I'm sorry, I can't do that yet

Tuchel seems flatly unable now and in the immediate aftermath to accept that he got anything wrong in that match

It’s not his fault we blew it against Argentina, he is saying. The fault is in ourselves that we are underlings, he continues to tell us. It’s in our DNA, you see. There’s really absolutely nothing he can do about it.

There is some elite-level gaslighting going on here. Most of us can see through it so let’s be honest about what happened in the Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta on July 15: Tuchel faced his first big test as England manager and he blew it. He blew it spectacularly.

He was not hired to get us to the World Cup semi-finals. Gareth Southgate did that. Tuchel was hired to get us beyond the semi-finals. He was hired to coach a talented group of England players to win the World Cup. He was hired, famously, because he would have the ability to get us ‘over the line’.

But when the test came, he wasn’t up to it. That’s the truth. I’ve heard all his excuses and all his deflections. But when the test came, he blew a 1-0 lead against an ordinary Argentina side. He was comprehensively out-coached by Argentina’s Lionel Scaloni. When the heat was on, Tuchel folded.

England always find a way to lose the big games at World Cups and lo and behold we had done it again. Tuchel was being paid the big bucks to fix that glitch in our psyche but he couldn’t do it. When it mattered most, England froze. And he froze with them.

In a weird way, I admire his front. There is something awfully bold about blaming his players and saying there was nothing he could do about their inability to keep the ball. ‘I should be coaching them to keep the ball?’ Tuchel asked on Friday, as if it were an utterly alien idea. ‘That’s my job? I’m not sure that I have the time.’

That’s why many England fans are finding it hard to let the mistakes of the Argentina game go. Because if Tuchel can’t accept that mistakes were made, then how can England move forward? How can we have any confidence at all that the next time we face a critical match, Tuchel does not blow it again?

If I were one of his players, I’d still be thinking about what he said in the aftermath of that Argentina tie. I’d still be thinking about the way he ducked responsibility. I’d still be thinking about what he said about English players and their DNA.

Enzo Fernandez celebrates his goal against England in the World Cup semi-finals

If I were one of Tuchel's players, I’d still be thinking about what he said in the aftermath of that Argentina tie

Put it this way, it wasn’t a surprise to me when the news came through on Monday morning that Cole Palmer had pulled out of the squad for the games against Spain, Czech Republic and Croatia with a ‘small muscle injury’. A few hours later the FA announced that Kobbie Mainoo, Marcus Rashford, Declan Rice and Tino Livramento would also be absent due to 'respective injury issues'.

Palmer didn’t make the World Cup squad, of course. Tuchel discarded him. Mainoo went but he didn’t play a single minute in the USA and Mexico. Tuchel humiliated him. Palmer and Mainoo are two of England’s best players. They are brilliant technical athletes. Of all England’s players, they are two of the best at keeping the ball.

Tuchel chose not to use them at the World Cup. He ignored Trent Alexander-Arnold, too, another of England’s best technical players. And now he has the gall to suggest our players are like neanderthals who can’t keep possession. If you want to keep possession in a World Cup semi-final against Argentina, maybe pick players in the squad who are the best at keeping possession.

It is surely not too great a stretch to suggest that Tuchel’s disdain for the ball-retention abilities of England’s players is not conducive to future harmony in the squad as the country turns its eyes towards a home European Championship in the summer of 2028.

If Tuchel could admit the errors he made in Atlanta, if he could take responsibility for the failure against Argentina, then maybe England could move forward with confidence. But he can’t. The delusion of infallibility has been his downfall before. And so doubt remains.

LIGHT SHONE ON UNITED'S ABSURD RECRUITMENT POLICY

Watching Fulham play Manchester United at Craven Cottage on Sunday afternoon, it was hard not to be reminded once more of the absurdity of United’s stated plan of fixing their team section by section in successive summer transfer windows.

The rationale, apparently, is that they fixed the attack in the summer of 2025, they fixed the midfield this summer and they will turn their attention to the defence next summer.

It is, frankly, bizarre. Football doesn’t work like that. Maybe Matheus Cunha, for example, will want out by next summer. Andrey Santos can’t get a kick at the moment. Football teams are like whack-a-mole: problems crop up everywhere.

And in the meantime, the creaking defence is a liability and another season’s hope of winning the Premier League is over already.

Manchester United's policy of fixing the team section by section is frankly odd. What if Matheus Cunha decides he wants out next summer?

And what of the newly-acquired £50m signing Andrey Santos who cannot get a kick at the moment?

CALLING IT 'THE DOCKERS' DERBY' IS JUST WRONG!

A point of order: a West Ham-supporting friend of mine wishes to advise that the habit of referring to the Championship match between his side and Millwall at the weekend as ‘The Dockers’ Derby’ ground the gears of him and many of his fellow Hammers.

‘West Ham were born from an ironworks yard, not a dockyard,’ he writes. ‘Prior to the advent of people needing to place some corny moniker on every football match, it was never, ever included in the vocabulary of sensible people growing up on the terraces of Upton Park and The Den.’

A fair point, I think. As an adjunct, reports from the aforementioned derby on Saturday, which ended in a 2-2 draw, suggest it was played in a fiercely wonderful atmosphere.

Sports.title: Celtic chief offers full backing to under-pressure boss Martin O'Neill
Sports.content:
Celtic chief executive Michael Nicholson insists the club remain fully supportive of Martin O'Neill despite the veteran manager being under mounting pressure.

O'Neill stated after the 1-0 defeat to Rangers at Parkhead last Sunday that he would take time to consider his future during the international break and whether it might be time to 'wrap it up'.

The 74-year-old, who agreed a one-year deal back in the summer to remain at the helm, has presided over three damaging defeats to Rangers and Ferencvaros over the past week.

Although Celtic do still remain top of the league by two points, a large section of the support had called for a change to be made in recent days.

But, as Celtic released their latest annual accounts showing a post-tax loss of £4.8million as well as cash reserves of £66.4m, Nicholson was adamant the club remain fully behind O'Neill.

'We were delighted to end season 2025/26 on a high, winning the Scottish Premiership on the final day of the season and adding the Scottish Cup and Women's Scottish Cup in the weeks following,' said Nicholson.

Martin O'Neill says he's considering his future as Celtic boss after three defeats on the bounce

Celtic chief Michael Nicholson has offered his support to the under-fire manager

'But last season was a challenging one for the club, both on and off the pitch. Following a period of stability, which has borne fruit in terms of success and growth over recent years, we experienced turmoil which affected the club's performance.

'We will address and learn from the challenges faced and mistakes made.

'The final weeks of the Premiership season; the final match at Celtic Park; the Scottish Cup final; these will live long in the memory for Celtic fans, whose support was a decisive factor.

'I thank Callum McGregor and all of the players and staff for their hard work and determination throughout the season that made the success possible.

'As the Chairman has noted, the environment was unstable, following Brendan Rodgers' resignation and our decision to move on from Wilfried Nancy.

'We owe a debt of gratitude to Martin O'Neill and his management team, who stepped up for Celtic, twice, and who guided the team to success.

'We were therefore delighted that Martin agreed to lead the Club again this season and we have worked with Martin and his team over the summer transfer window to invest in the squad.

'Having started well in the Premiership this season, we experienced disappointment in the UEFA Champions League play-off.

'Reaching the league phase of the Champions League is an objective for us all, and we are sorry not to have achieved it.

'On top of that, the losses in the last week have been painful for us all. We will now come together and support Martin and the players, as we focus our efforts on achieving success domestically and in the Europa League.'

In his own address to supporters, Celtic chairman Brian Wilson claimed that the disastrous appointment of Nancy last season could have worked had it not happened mid-season.

Nancy lasted only a month in the job after presiding over a shambolic run of form and eventually left as statistically the worst – and shortest-serving – manager in the club's history.

The Celtic hierarchy at full-time in Sunday's 1-0 home defeat to Old Firm rivals Rangers

'The events of the past 12 months have been dramatic, sometimes joyful and at other points deeply frustrating,' said Wilson.

'The departure of Brendan Rodgers was an unanticipated event which initiated a period of instability.

'In other circumstances, the appointment of Wilfried Nancy might have worked but his arrival in mid-season and the changes which followed clearly did not.

'Parting ways with Wilfried was hugely disappointing but decisive action had to be taken.

'The return of the great Martin O'Neill, supported by his backroom team as well as a fine squad of players, then proved to be a triumphant success.

'The early stages of the 2026/27 season have brought mixed fortunes.

'Our league campaign started strongly and the first leg tie in the Champions League qualifier gave cause for optimism.

'The second leg defeat to LASK was, accordingly, all the more deeply disappointing for every supporter of the Club.

'This has been followed by our exit from the League Cup. We now move into the Europa League as well as pursuing our defence of the Scottish Premiership and Scottish Cup, with renewed commitment to success.'

In terms of their annual accounts for the year ending June 30, 2026, Celtic's revenue decreased by 22.7 per cent to £111.0million (2025: £143.6million).

Operating expenses including labour increased by 4.3 per cent to £122.1million (2025: £117.1million).

Gain on sale of player registrations of £16.0million (2025: £31.5million). Acquisition of player registrations of £15.6million (2025: £38.6million)

Loss before tax of £6.6million (2025: profit of £45.7million). Loss after tax of £4.8million (2025: profit of £33.9million).Year-end cash of £66.4million (2025: £77.3million).

Sports.title: England's fastest bowler calls it quits: 97mph Mark Wood admits defeat after knee surgery and retires at 36 - ending his Ashes dream
Sports.content:
Mark Wood, England’s fastest ever bowler, has announced his international retirement after finally admitting defeat in an injury battle of 18 months.

Wood, 36, played only once - the Ashes Test defeat in Perth last November - after breaking down with a left knee issue during the Champions Trophy in late February 2025.

He put himself through intensive rehabilitation to get fit for last winter’s Ashes, but it ended in anguish when his body reacted badly to him bowling at close to maximum speed in the first innings of the eight-wicket loss to Australia.

It was his ability to produce 90mph pace without much in the way of build-up that persuaded England’s selectors to gamble on him against the Australians, throwing him into the first Test despite reporting discomfort in an internal practice match - but he managed just 11 overs and sported a knee brace post match.

Wood was ruled out of the 4-0 series drubbing on December 9, saying he was ‘gutted’ but it was not for the want of trying.

Now, having spent the summer trying to prolong his career under the guidance of knee consultant Simon Ball, he is calling time on a career that produced high-octane theatre on the international stage and 118 Test wickets at a cost of 31 runs each.

Mark Wood made his last Test appearance in the first Test at Perth last November

'When you speak to other people, they say it hits you in the face, there’s a big feeling around that being it, "you’re done",' he told Sky Sports.

'I’ve never really had that, I love playing cricket, I love playing for England, that’s been something I’ve felt really strongly about and proud to do. But I’ve had a lot of injuries.

'I’ve always found a way where I’ve believed I’d come back and had that resilience where I’m going to come back again, or I’ll be better, or I’ll prove somebody wrong again, but this time it’s just ground me down really.

'It’s been a long time since Perth, that was in November 2025 my last game, so it’s been a year and a half really where it’s just sort of ground me down to thinking I’m never going to get back to that level.

'Plus the contract situation. My contract ends in September, and I think it just feels like the right time.

'I never really wanted to give up England, but the lads that are coming through are doing a fantastic job and the news should be about the lads going to get their contracts and I can just focus on other things.'

A decision to have ‘tidy-up’ surgery in July appears to have been his last throw of the dice, after becoming frustrated with taking a patient approach to a return. ‘How long is a piece of string? It was improving, but slowly, slowly,’ he said, of his rehabilitation prior to undergoing the knife.

Wood was a member of England’s 2019 and 2022 World Cup-winning teams in 50-over and T20 cricket respectively, but it was as much for his 100 per cent commitment to bowling fast that makes him stand out from any other player of his generation.

Two years ago, he produced a delivery of 97.1mph against West Indies at Trent Bridge, while his average speed was 91.2mph - the highest recorded in a Test match on British soil.

The newly-retired Wood embraces one-day captain Harry Brook ahead of Tuesday's game against Sri Lanka at Chester-le-Street

Twelve months earlier, he was man of the match with seven wickets at Headingley as England defeated Australia to keep their hopes of an Ashes comeback alive.

Wood’s Test record against Australia, in fact, was better than his overall return and he was the visiting bowler that came out with the most credit from the 2021-22 Ashes when he claimed 17 scalps in four appearances. His hopes of reprising his role in next year's home series, though, are now over.

Hugely popular with supporters for his affable personality and fulsome heart, it is understood he is paying homage to his north-east roots by saying goodbye to the game at his home ground of Chester-le-Street on Tuesday, during England’s one-day series opener against Sri Lanka.

Wood’s central contract runs out next week and it is anticipated that he moves straight from dressing room to commentary box with a more regular role with Sky Sports, for whom he has worked on several occasions this summer.

England managing director Rob Key paid tribute to the departing Wood, saying: 'It’s been a privilege to watch the latter part of a great career.

'To have been a point of difference in Ashes series wins, a World Cup, and to have thrilled crowds every time he got the ball in his hand is something very few players achieve.

'He can look back with enormous pride on a career very well spent.'

Sports.title: Willie Mullins tribute to legendary dual champion hurdler Hurricane Fly after death aged 22
Sports.content:
Willie Mullins tribute to legendary dual champion hurdler Hurricane Fly after death aged 22

The star jumper scored at the Cheltenham Festival in 2011 and 2013 under Ruby Walsh and won the Irish Champion Hurdle a remarkable five times

View 3 Images Ruby Walsh and Willie Mullins with Hurricane Fly (Image: PA)

Willie Mullins’s legendary dual champion hurdler Hurricane Fly has died aged 22.

‌



The star jumper triumphed at the Cheltenham Festival in 2011 and 2013 under Ruby Walsh and also won the Irish Champion Hurdle a remarkable five times from 2011 to 2015. His nine-year career came to an end in August 2015 when he was retired from racing to spend the rest of his days at the Irish National Stud in Kildare.

‌



Announcing the sad news to the Sporting Life, Mullins said: “He won a record-breaking 22 Grade 1 races, which was remarkable. He’s one of the greatest horses to ever come through our stable.

‌



Value Scope Extra: Saffie Osborne could have more reason for tears at Ascot READ MORE :

Jockeys to wear black armbands on Tuesday after death of popular ex-rider READ MORE :

“He was a horse who loved a battle and was so brave. Ruby was able to stand back anywhere on him and he’d answer. He just put his rivals into trouble. He was such a proper horse. He was awesome, one of the biggest legends ever to come through Closutton.

“I want to say my personal thanks to Leona Harman at the National Stud who does such a wonderful job looking after the Living Legends who are retired there. My thoughts are with Gail Carlisle who was Hurricane Fly’s groom throughout his days with us at Closutton and had such a wonderful relationship with him.

“I was lucky enough to visit him today just before the end and met Gail who had popped over to see him as well as she’d heard the news. It was very poignant and we were able to say our goodbyes.

‌



View 3 Images Hurricane Fly: won the Champion Hurdle twice (Image: PA)

"It's especially poignant following so shortly after the passing of his co-owner Frank Boyd and I'm thinking of his family and George Creighton's family too at this time. Hurricane Fly provided us all with so many wonderful days and memories."

The owners released a statement which read: "The Boyd and Creighton families are deeply saddened to hear of the passing of Hurricane Fly. He provided us with so many great days and long lasting memories. We would like to thank Willie Mullins, Gail Carlisle, Harold Kirk and all the staff at Closutton, as well as the National Stud who provided him with such a happy retirement."

Article continues below

View 3 Images Hurricane Fly: won five successive Irish Champion Hurdles (Image: PA)

Walsh said: “Hurricane Fly was a brilliant racehorse but was without doubt the best jumper of a hurdle I ever rode. He was incredible, his accuracy, his bravery, the speed at which he could move his feet. He was bombproof, you could ride him down to hurdles like they weren’t there because he was going to do the right thing every time.

“He had the engine to go with it. He had speed, class, he stayed and was in my eyes, for a little horse, the perfect horse.”

Sports.title: Anthony Joshua questions Tyson Fury drug testing for mega-fight
Sports.content:
Anthony Joshua questions Tyson Fury drug testing for mega-fight

Joshua and Fury will clash in Cardiff on December 11 with an official announcement now imminent and a press conference expected to take place in London early next week

View Image Anthony Joshua speaks out (Image: Mark Robinson, Matchroom Boxing/Getty Images)

Anthony Joshua has appeared to question why Tyson Fury has not enrolled in drug-testing for their mega-fight.

‌



Joshua and Fury will clash in Cardiff on December 11 with an official announcement now imminent and a press conference expected to take place in London early next week. But questions have been raised over Fury's drug-testing protocol with Joshua's promoter Eddie Hearn insisting testing should be underway by now.

‌



Joshua has now posted a copy of an email to his Snapchat account, showing correspondence between the VADA drug-testing agency and an unknown recipient. The email reads: "Is Mr. Fury going to enroll? Typically, we enroll opponents at the same time. We also need the whereabouts form to enroll either fighter." Joshua posted the email along with a caption which read: "I'm not accusing TF of anything".

‌



In response, a statement from Fury's team read: "Once the fight has been officially finalised, VADA will be the first people we will be calling."

Tyson Fury breaks silence with TWO Anthony Joshua rants READ MORE :

Anthony Joshua could have secret weapon for Tyson Fury fight READ MORE :

Speaking on Saturday night, Hearn claimed Fury should have started testing when he signed to contract to fight Joshua. “The drug testing protocol is the same as what has always been in the contract," he said. “It wasn’t adhered to in its form.

‌



"I don’t actually, necessarily blame Tyson Fury for that because I don’t think – as we have found out on many occasions – I don’t think what is in AJ’s contract is the same as what is in AJ’s contract. Testing was supposed to start when the original contracts were signed. And it didn’t for them.

"I don’t think it had it in his contract that it had to start then, so this is not me saying he didn’t enrol, I don’t think he was obligated to enrol. But in our contract he was obligated to enrol."

Joshua and Fury signed separate contracts and Hearn explained why this has caused issues. “There have been many issues along the way, with the contracts, that we have let slip, because we want to stay in the fight and we want to make sure the fight happens," he added.

Article continues below

"The ones we weren’t willing to let slip were the location and TKO’s involvement. The protocol was supposed to start earlier but it is now in line with most other fights. I don’t necessarily blame Tyson Fury for that, I just think what we asked for was not in his personal contract, so he did not have to do it."

Fury served a backdated two-year ban from UK Anti-Doping after tests in 2015 showed elevated levels of nandrolone. Fury blamed the positive test on eating uncastrated wild boar.

Sports.title: Lewis Hall says it was a 'no-brainer' to snub Man Utd despite transfer interest
Sports.content:
Lewis Hall says it was a 'no-brainer' to snub Man Utd despite transfer interest

Lewis Hall has chosen to extend his contract with Newcastle despite being heavily linked with Manchester United in the summer, explaining the reasons for his decision

View 2 Images Lewis Hall has chosen to extend his Newcastle contract (Image: Serena Taylor, Newcastle United via Getty Images)

Lewis Hall admits it was a "no-brainer" to sign an extension with Newcastle despite Manchester United's interest as he talked up the impact of Matthias Jaissle.

‌



The new boss, who replaced Eddie Howe in the summer, has made an immediate impression and impressed with a Magpies side that endured a poor campaign last time out and looked to have lost a bit of direction under the previous regime.

‌



Hall had to watch leading lights like Sandro Tonali, Bruno Guimaraes and Anthony Gordon leave St James' Park in the summer, which led to speculation he would follow. United were particularly keen and need a left-back at Old Trafford, but Newcastle dug their heels in and maintained he wouldn't be sold.

‌



Hall has got his head down under Jaissle, still only 38, and quickly decided that the former Red Bull Salzburg manager can lead Newcastle to great heights, committing to the club for the next five years.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



Quizzed on whether the transfer talk impacted on him he said: “No, honestly, it didn’t [affect me]. I guess whenever you’re linked to another team, you know that you’re doing something right. I guess it’s just a credit to your own performances and how you are as a player, how you are as a person.

“I took that as a positive, but at the same time, I knew how much I love playing here and I knew that since the manager came in, I knew the ambitions and what we wanted to achieve.

“After not many conversations, not many training sessions, I knew that the manager was going to be really good for this club and I knew that as a team, bringing in new players and improving the squad was really important and as soon as we did that, it was a no-brainer really to sign.”

‌



View 2 Images Matthias Jaissle has made an immediate impression in Newcastle

Newcastle have won two of their five games, losing just the once, with Jaissle impressing as he transitions in a host of new summer signings, many of whom were largely unknown quantities.

Hall, whilst enduring difficult moments, which included giving away a stoppage time penalty against Liverpool, has been a strong performer and that has seen him recalled to the England squad.

Article continues below

He missed out on the World Cup in the summer, which owed to his performance levels dipping in the final weeks of the season. Hall was left frustrated that Howe played him on the right, not his natural position, which he reportedly attributed to his form dropping off.

Sports.title: JJ Gabriel 'reaches first major agreement' as Man Utd star tells four clubs his preference
Sports.content:
JJ Gabriel 'reaches first major agreement' as Man Utd star tells four clubs his preference

Manchester United starlet JJ Gabriel expressed a desire to leave Old Trafford last week and has since been linked with some of the biggest clubs in the world

View 2 Images JJ Gabriel of Manchester United (Image: Manchester United/Manchester United via Getty Images)

Manchester United teenager JJ Gabriel reportedly wants to move to Spain if he is granted an exit from the Red Devils. It emerged earlier this month that Gabriel had expressed a desire to leave United, and there are already reports of where the playmaker could end up joining.

‌



Reports last week claimed that Gabriel had refused to take part in training for United ahead of their Carabao Cup third-round tie against Brighton. The 15-year-old was expected to be involved in the matchday squad for Michael Carrick’s side before expressing a desire to leave United.

‌



Gabriel has been tipped to have a bright future in the game, and would have been United’s youngest-ever player had he made his debut against the Seagulls at Old Trafford last week. Yet Gabriel's determination to leave United has sparked intense speculation surrounding the youngster's next move.

‌



A new update has surfaced from Spain suggesting that Gabriel could be heading across Europe should he leave United. Spanish publication Sport have reported that Gabriel's shortlist of potential destinations now features four clubs, two of which are based in Spain. Real Madrid and Barcelona are among those reportedly keen on securing Gabriel's signature, alongside Bayern Munich and Paris Saint-Germain.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



The report further claims that Gabriel and his camp have already visited Spain, touring both Madrid and Barcelona. The United starlet has reportedly reached a 'first major agreement' to join one of those clubs instead of any other team. Reports suggest Gabriel is now keen on a move to Spain, giving Barcelona and Real Madrid the upper hand in the race to sign the coveted United youngster.

Gabriel has enjoyed an impressive opening few weeks of the season, most recently scoring a hat-trick against Sabah in the UEFA Youth League earlier this month. The playmaker has also contributed two goals and two assists across just two appearances for United's Under-21s in Premier League 2.

View 2 Images JJ Gabriel of Manchester United (Image: Manchester United/Manchester United via Getty Images)

‌



Despite his request to depart, Gabriel remains registered with United for the remainder of the season and cannot be de-registered. United believe the matter can still be resolved, despite Gabriel's unexpected desire to leave the club. The teenager is just a couple of weeks away from being eligible to sign a scholarship with United when he turns 16 on October 6, and will need to wait until his 17th birthday before putting pen to paper on a professional contract.

Speaking on Friday, Carrick was keen to shift the focus away from speculation surrounding the teenager and towards his wellbeing. He said: "I’ll just repeat what I said [earlier this week]: he’s a young boy, it’s important we don’t put anything out here, the exposure and scrutiny we have to be careful.

"We have to be sensible and think about him. The situation will work itself out."

Sports.title: Do £100m transfers work? Liverpool hit major hurdle as record deals come under fire
Sports.content:
There's something about being a £100million player that just spells danger.

Once the initial fanfare has died down, the expectation sets in and that shirt feels that bit heavier. Obviously, seeing your club spedt a nine figure sum is exciting and manifests a real sense of ambition, which inevitably galvanises a fanbase - at least at the start. But with so many players nowadays moving for fees which are based on potential, rather than a genuine body of work over a decent period, it is no surprise that so many mega-money signings have failed to provide the desired bang for buck over the last decade or so.

Recent evidence shows that the deals which sit in the £50m to £80m bracket often prove more successful; think a Kevin De Bruyne, a Bruno Fernandes or a Virgil van Dijk.

For the few who sit in the expanding nine-figure club, they must embrace a spotlight that they never asked for, but ultimately comes with the territory.

Florian Wirtz is very much a man under pressure right now; he is struggling to regularly impact games for Liverpool with Jamie Carragher now adamant he should not be in the team given his current form.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

In Wirtz's case, it is not to say that the price tag he came with was unfair off the back of what he did at Bayer Leverkusen. The bigger issue was, as mentioned, whether he did it for long enough. Wirtz excelled in a team that won the Bundesliga, but did so off the back of a team embracing the underdog tag. Wirtz enjoyed two truly productive years with his former side and then got his move.

Now working in a different environment, where perhaps the system isn't geared to him as much, and at a club where the expectation is ramped up, Wirtz has found it far tougher to thrive.

View 3 Images Jack Grealish was never able to justify his fee in Manchester (Image: Getty Images)

There are parallels to Jack Grealish, who up until recently remained Manchester City's record buy following his £100m move from Aston Villa in 2021. He undoubtedly stepped into a bigger environment and was no longer the cog that everything went through. His numbers never came close to justifying his gargantuan fee, with Grealish scoring double figures just once in his career - at Villa.

On the continent, Spanish sides have also fallen foul of spending big on players only to be left short changed. Barcelona made Antoine Griezmann and Philippe Coutinho £100m players years back. Neither delivered in the way the Nou Camp crowd expected, nor did they stay too long.

In 2019, off the back of one season in Benfica's first-team, Atletico Madrid signed Joao Felix for a club-record fee of £113m. He was locked down to a mammoth seven-year deal, but within three seasons he was fifth choice in the pecking order and on the lookout for a new home. Seeing him bounce around clubs before landing in Saudi Arabia suggests the Portuguese star will struggle to become the player he threatened to once be.

Talking of players who never achieve what their potential and price tag suggests, Neymar will likely remain the world's most expensive player for some time. He joined PSG for £200m, which was seen as a major coup, but despite the numbers, accrued largely in Ligue 1, few would argue with any passion that the Brazilian delivered on his fee.

View 3 Images Antoine Griezmann and Philippe Coutinho were costly deals who never delivered at Barcelona

In fact, of the 20 most expensive transfers in history, only one has gone on to win the Champions League at the club they signed for. That being Jack Grealish. Others are either still newly at their latest club, have categorically underdelivered, or simply not got over the line yet. Think the likes of Kylian Mbappe at PSG, Ousmane Demebe at Barcelona, Enzo Fernandez, Alexander Isak or Declan Rice.

Wirtz currently doesn't look like the type of player who will take Liverpool back to the levels they enjoyed under Jurgen Klopp, even if there is a huge amount of goodwill coming from the Kop, determined to see him become a player who can throw his once British record fee in the face of his critics.

He's part of a lavishly assembled attack at Liverpool, which features three player who cost north of £100m. Isak himself has had to face his fair share of criticism. Time will tell on Bradley Barcola after his switch from PSG in the summer.

Perhaps telling about Liverpool's wave of transfer business over the last two summers is that Hugo Ekitike, who cost £79m, is by far the most impressive of their new arrivals.

Of course, it goes without saying that £100m players are often individuals with real talent, and can take just months before you're going "he was worth every penny". Rice certainly looks to be among those in that category.

Sports.title: NBA hero who played with LeBron James went to get alcohol and didn't go home for 10 years
Sports.content:
NBA hero who played with LeBron James went to get alcohol and didn't go home for 10 years

The former Cleveland Cavaliers and Boston Celtics star has detailed how his life fell apart

View 3 Images Delonte West of the Boston Celtics while going up against Lebron James, then of the Miami Heat. The pair were team-mates at Cleveland (Image: Mike Ehrmann/Getty Images)

An NBA legend and former colleague of LeBron James has detailed his acute addiction problems, including leaving home to buy booze and not returning for 10 years. Delonte West played with James for the Cleveland Cavaliers between 2008 and 2010.

‌



He also represented the Boston Celtics, Seattle SuperSonics and Dallas Mavericks during his eight seasons in the NBA. Spells playing in China and Venezuela followed before his life descended into chaos with addictions to drugs and alcohol, plus a long spell of homelessness.

‌



Because of his profile as an ex-NBA star, much of his decline played out in the public eye through viral photos and videos, sparking widespread concern from fans, former team-mates and the wider basketball community.

‌



However, after a spell in rehab, West has taken steps in the right direction, including reconnecting with his family, although there have been relapses along the way. West is using his status to try and inspire others to get the help they need, chronicling his journey on social media and making public appearances.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

He was recently a guest on the Rise Above podcast with former addict Kevin Lanning, detailing the depths to which he sank, including a spell living on the streets and begging for food.

‌



NBA icon LeBron James sends message to ex-Arsenal forward before World Cup star sent off READ MORE :

He said: "I went to the liquor store. I knew everyone in the area. There were guys in the parking lot. They sit out there, talk, hang around the store all day, sit at the side of the store and drink.

"I cracked open what I brought out of the store and drank it out there. I was hanging out. I sat down on the curb and I didn't get back up for another 10 years.

View 3 Images West (number 13) with his Cleveland Cavaliers team-mates, including James, in 2009 (Image: David Liam Kyle/NBAE via Getty Images)

‌



"I didn't go back home, I didn't know what was going on. I didn't even have a phone for about eight years."

West was exposed to drugs from an early age, revealing he first smoked weed in the fourth grade (nine to 10 years ago). In later life, his drug habit got so extreme that it was all he could think about.

‌



He added: "The first thing I thought about, the second thing, the third thing and the fourth thing, all day, every day, it was, 'How is this going to lead to another score.'

View 3 Images West has candidly detailed his struggle with addiction (Image: Rise Above with Kevin Lanning)

"With humbleness, you have to see your foolishness and be OK with it. I'm not making fun or glorifying it but when I look at videos online [of him during his dark days], I can deal with it."

Article continues below

He credits his ongoing commitment to sobriety to his faith, finding the right medication and treatment, the support of his family and partners and applying the same mental discipline he used during his basketball career toward his recovery.

Sports.title: Roy Keane refuses to apologise as Andy Robertson tells Man Utd icon he went too far
Sports.content:
Roy Keane refuses to apologise as Andy Robertson tells Man Utd icon he went too far

Roy Keane and Andy Robertson have reflected on the incident that saw the ex-Liverpool defender elbowed by an assistant referee and branded as a "big baby"

View 2 Images Andy Robertson and Roy Keane were reunited on The Overlap

Roy Keane has refused to apologise to Andy Robertson after labelling the former Liverpool left-back as a "big baby" following his altercation with an assistant referee.

‌



Back in April 2023, Robertson claimed he had been elbowed in the throat by linesman Constantine Hatzidakis during a 2-2 draw between Liverpool and Arsenal. The Scot was incensed after Hatzidakis appeared to swing at him at half-time, but Keane had little sympathy and insisted he should instead focus on his defending.

‌



When asked about the incident by presenter David Jones, Keane said: "But Robertson, do you know what, does he grab the linesman first? I'm not sure, but he's complaining. He should be more worried about his defending.

‌



Roy Keane points finger after JJ Gabriel quit bombshell with reminder about Man United starlet READ MORE :

"Do you know what it is, that Robertson? I've watched him a number of times. He's a big baby. That's what he is. Just get on with the game and concentrate on your defending. He does grab the linesman first."

Now, more than three years on, Robertson and Keane have reflected on the infamous incident with the former Hull City and Dundee United defender, who is now at Tottenham, appearing on the latest episode of The Overlap.

Keane said: "Players have to remember, and this is not an apology, when in the studio, we can have long days can't we? Can be a bit flat, a player can do something and you're agitated by like a long day."

‌



Replying to Keane, Robertson joked: "The first two babys were alright, the third was one too far."

View 2 Images Andy Robertson was called a 'baby' by Roy Keane

Keane then responded in a tongue-in-cheek manner, adding: "In my defence, traffic all the way to game, and what have you, but they're not saying anything, you've got to say something, that's why I said the last 'baby'. They're all staring at me like, 'f****** say something'. Am I right?"

‌



Robertson finished with a comment to Jamie Carragher, who laughed at Keane at the time. "I wasn't happy with you (Carragher) laughing either by the way)," Robertson said.

In the end, Hatzidakis faced no punishment from the PGMOL for the incident but didn't assist another Liverpool game up until January 2025, when he ran the line for the Carabao Cup semi-final first leg against Tottenham.

Robertson, meanwhile, left Liverpool earlier this summer after nine years at Anfield and has since joined Spurs on a free transfer. However, his start to life in north London has been difficult with Roberto De Zerbi's side without a win from their opening five Premier League matches this season.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."
