Sports.title: Red Bull admits Verstappen's mysterious car issue cannot be fully fixed until 2027
Sports.content:
During several weekends this season, Verstappen has complained that the Red Bull Formula 1 car gets worse over the course of a session or race. It usually happens at the rear axle, including during qualifying at Monza, where Verstappen called the RB22 "a car made of paper".

Notably, the four-time world champion added that he has been complaining about this internally for years. According to Verstappen, Red Bull has been struggling with car degradation during a session for multiple seasons, which is remarkable given that the 2026 car is completely new following the overhaul of the technical regulations.

It raises the question of why the problem is so persistent and whether Red Bull now finally understands what is behind it.

When Autosport puts those questions to Red Bull team principal Laurent Mekies, the Frenchman replied: "I don't think we are going to explain what it is and how we are going to fix it. But I think Max is right [in saying] that there is an element of car performance degradation that is happening through a session and through a race.

"He's also right in saying that it's not a new issue. We are not sleeping on it. We have been trying to tackle that in different ways.

"I consider it a complex issue. Otherwise, we would get to the bottom of it. But everyone is very constructive about it and we are trying to make small steps at the time to be able to finally get to the bottom of it."

Verstappen said at Monza that the Red Bull car is “made of paper” after he suffered from “car degradation” during qualifying Photo by: Alex Bierens de Haan / Getty Images

As for those small steps, Mekies says several lessons were learned on the Saturday in Monza, when Verstappen voiced his frustration, and Red Bull tried to put those lessons into practice in Madrid. The problem did not occur during F1’s first visit to the Madring, or at least not to the same extent.

"We had a couple of positive steps in that regard this weekend," Mekies said. "It will never be the full picture, but we certainly have, through pain, made progress into our understanding. We don't have all the solutions on the car yet, but I trust that we are in the right way. It will not be fast, so it's something that will probably take us through next year."

In doing so, Mekies acknowledges what Verstappen had already hinted at earlier: some problems simply cannot be fixed this season and require bigger changes to the design and chassis for 2027.

The fact that Red Bull is limited in what it can do for the remainder of this year is partly because the budget cap will come into play at some point and because the focus behind the scenes has already shifted to 2027, but also because certain changes simply cannot be made to the RB22.

Mekies therefore acknowledges that the issue could occur more often in the remaining races this year, although he does not want to go into further detail about exactly what is behind it.

"I'm not going to give any more details here. But as I said, it's true that there are some aspects of the car performance that sometimes don't stay at the optimum level. And that’s serious lap time," he said.

If Verstappen does not win a Grand Prix this season, it will be the first year since 2015 without a race win Photo by: Sam Bagnall / Sutton Images via Getty Images

"So, it's something we [need to get on top of]. There is no doubt that we have everyone trying to improve that for the future."

For this year, Verstappen already knows that there is little left for him to fight for. The Dutchman acknowledged early on that he is not a factor in the title fight and can only hope for a race win.

Should he fail to achieve that, it would be the first time since 2015, when Verstappen was still driving for Toro Rosso – now Racing Bulls. Since his promotion to Red Bull in May 2016, the Dutchman has won at least one grand prix every year.

Sports.title: Mercedes aims to end pole drought with upcoming Malaysia F1 upgrades
Sports.content:
Mercedes has confirmed its next big Formula 1 car upgrade will arrive at the forthcoming grand prix in Malaysia, where it hopes to get back into contention for pole.

The Silver Arrows is the runaway leader of the 2026 championship with a 145-point advantage over second-placed Ferrari, despite its last major upgrade package being Montreal in May.

Mercedes has instead preferred to fit minor race-specific updates whereas its nearest challengers Ferrari and McLaren have been significantly more aggressive with developments.

So although Mercedes won the first six grands prix, it has since won four of the last eight as McLaren and Ferrari have closed their respective gaps taking two wins each in that time.

But the German outfit is hoping to reestablish its dominance during the Malaysian weekend on 2-4 October, the race after Baku, as the Asian country replaces Bahrain to make its F1 return.

Speaking on the Nu Silver Arrows Radio Show podcast, trackside engineering director Andrew Shovlin said: “We haven't got much new coming to Baku, but actually that's a circuit that's more about drag than downforce.

“So the car was good in Monza, hopefully it will work well in Baku. But, you need a car that can have a good straight line speed.

Toto Wolff, Mercedes, James Allison, Mercedes, Andrew Shovlin, Mercedes Photo by: Sam Bloxham / LAT Images via Getty Images

“There's other things, though, you need in Baku, like the sort of street circuit nature, almost that Monaco-esque being able to deal with the low speed, keeping all the wheels on the ground.

“And then the updates, well, they're going to come Malaysia onwards and hopefully we'll make a decent step.

“I don't think we're going to be out front by miles, but hopefully we'll be back into a position where we can really go into qualifying, knowing that we're fighting for pole.”

Although Mercedes has won the last two races - Monza and Madrid - via the dominant Kimi Antonelli, it hasn’t actually claimed pole since the Italian went quickest at Spa in July.

So that is a run of four, three of which saw McLaren’s Lando Norris take pole, marking a far cry from the start of 2026 where the Silver Arrows took pole for each of the opening 10 rounds.

“Early in the season, we tended to go thinking, we have a car that if we do a really good job, it should be on pole,” added Shovlin.

“We should be fighting for a race win. Whereas now the margin between finishing first and finishing sixth is one or two tenths and it's difficult to predict because Monza is a unique track.

“It needs a car that's quite slippy with low drag and then new circuit like Madring couldn't be more different. But we just focus on getting the most out of the car and if we win, awesome.”

Sports.title: Cadillac F1 owners Mark Walter and TWG Global face class-action lawsuit
Sports.content:
Cadillac Formula 1 shareholder Mark Walter has officially become the subject of a class-action lawsuit, while a concurrent investigation into potential fraud between his insurance companies is ongoing.

The class-action lawsuit was filed in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Florida, and the complaint alleges that Walter used his firms - TWG Global, alongside Delaware Life Insurance and Group 1001 - to execute a scheme aimed at concealing federal investigations and diverting billions of dollars from policyholders' funds.

The lawsuit claims that insurance companies affiliated with Walter used money from annuity policyholders to finance a broader business network.

This network enabled the mogul to acquire stakes in sports franchises like the Los Angeles Dodgers and the Los Angeles Lakers, before expanding into motorsport through TWG Motorsport (a division of TWG Global) by acquiring Andretti Global and partnering with General Motors to launch the Cadillac F1 team.

Media outlets report that instead of maintaining low-risk investments, the insurers funneled approximately 42% of their assets - around $17 billion - into Walter’s private network of business interests.

The lawsuit was brought by 67-year-old Florida resident Ira Rosner, represented by law firm Robbins Geller Rudman & Dowd, who alleges that the insurance companies intentionally withheld key financial disclosures.

Valtteri Bottas, Cadillac Racing Photo by: Alex Bierens de Haan / LAT Images via Getty Images

USA Today reported receiving a response from a spokesperson for Group 1001 Insurance, who acknowledged awareness of the suit while emphasizing: "No court has ruled that Group 1001 Insurance or Delaware Life Insurance Company did anything wrong, and we intend to defend the case vigorously, consistent with our long track record of serving policyholders with integrity."

TWG Global plays a vital role in Cadillac F1's organizational structure, acting as both an investing partner and an operational entity for the team.

While the civil lawsuit does not directly halt track operations and no criminal charges have been filed against executives, the controversy raises questions about the future of Walter's sports holdings. Walter recently agreed to sell his stakes in both the Lakers and Premier League side Chelsea - the latter case a combined 25% holding with Todd Boehly, for which the pair have received almost $1 billion from private equity firm Clearlake.

Just this past August, amid rising scrutiny over Walter's business practices, the team's parent company took a firm stance on Cadillac F1's future, issuing a statement to deny any plans to offload its Formula 1 assets.

"TWG is not considering a sale of the Cadillac team or any other part of TWG Motorsport," the company stated categorically during the Dutch Grand Prix.

Sports.title: How Antonelli's luxury problem is causing Wolff and Mercedes grey hairs
Sports.content:
For better or for worse, there seems to be no slowing down Kimi Antonelli.

Just ask Pete Bonnington, who channelled his inner schoolteacher in Madrid as he relentlessly had to remind the 20-year-old Italian to pay attention to track limits.

Having benefited from an earlier virtual safety car on a circuit where overtaking proved impossible, all Antonelli had to do was to keep it clean until the finish line, with Max Verstappen and Lando Norris resigned to following him home.

Bonnington and Mercedes had already suffered a scare earlier in the race with what almost sounded like a prank call from the young Italian.

Antonelli: "Check the car!"

Bonnington: "Which corner?"

Antonelli: "No I didn't touch any wall, but the steering feels weird..."

But with five laps to go, despite little genuine pressure from behind, Antonelli did tag one of the many concrete walls lining the challenging Madring circuit. "I touched the wall on the entry to Turn 7," Antonelli yelled.

Despite being in control, it was another race where Antonelli had been dangerously flirting with the track limits, much to the dismay of his father Marco and team boss Toto Wolff. There's just no slowing Antonelli down.

"I just discussed it with his father and we were joking: 'What an idiot!'. No, that's just Kimi,” the Mercedes boss said after the race. “The white lines, we had to drum it into his head that he shouldn't go over the white lines. Even in Monza, he still went over the white lines and [risked] the car. And the same with track limits.

"At a certain stage, I said to him: 'Don't you see out of the car? Do we need to sit you that high up so that you have [avoid] those track limit things? We had a laugh about it.

"And today, six laps to the end or whatever it was, he says: 'Check the car, I just brushed the wall.' What?! He's causing us grey hair. But maybe he's like this and maybe that's what's making him so quick."

Wolff added: "He had to hit the wall again because he wants to go fast. Sometimes for me, he's an inch too cool."

Kimi Antonelli is giving Toto Wolff a few grey hairs Photo by: Anni Graf - Formula 1 via Getty Images

Antonelli's flat-out approach appears to be a trait that Wolff and Mercedes are going to have to live with for now, at least until it goes wrong one day. Could that day come when Antonelli starts thinking about the big prize at the end as he careens towards a maiden world championship?

Wolff is adamant that won't be the case, despite Antonelli being by far the youngest driver to ever be in that position. "I promise you he's not thinking about it," Wolff insisted. "The way this kid is able to compartmentalise and be the young kid and then get into the car and be the mature racing driver...

"If Kimi says to himself: 'I'm not thinking about the championship', then he's not thinking about the championship. We are also trying, the parents and myself, the team is saying: 'You know, this is not finished.'

"There are black swan events. They can come and you're losing something out of your hands when you didn't think it was possible to lose. So, he's not going to think about it. We're too grown up and mature for this. We think about worst-case scenarios. He doesn't think about it."

Building on the lessons of a troubled debut year in 2025, Antonelli feels he has the right support system around him to carry him through to the finish line, whether that be in Abu Dhabi or at an impromptu home race in Imola near his native Bologna.

Kimi Antonelli has a strong support network in the paddock Photo by: Sam Bloxham / LAT Images via Getty Images

"I’m lucky to have really good people around me," Antonelli explained. "I have an incredible team that supports me, a great family. Especially my dad is the one who keeps me on the ground. Especially when he sees that I might lose a little bit the way, he doesn’t [hesitate] to tell me off or to just tell me to come back to the ground.

"On my side, as I said many times, I just try to do my best every race, trying to really drive as fast as I can whenever I go in the car. And then we’ll see where we end up at the end of the year. But definitely I don’t want to over-complicate things or just drive worrying about championship or results. Just driving, doing my best."

Driving as fast as he can all the time, is certainly working for Antonelli right now. As far as his team is concerned, almost to a fault.

Sports.title: Saturday race, Williams’ upgrade, title fight fades and more Azerbaijan GP talking points | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Formula 1 is embarking on nine rounds in 11 weeks – in theory. Here are the six talking points for the Azerbaijan Grand Prix.

Don’t forget to remember

Formula One Management has shifted the entire race weekend forward 24 hours in order to accommodate Azerbaijan’s Remembrance Day on Sunday. Azerbaijan’s president Ilham Aliyev, who succeeded his father in charge of the country over two decades ago, inaugurated the day in 2020.

The day marks the beginning of that year’s war in the Nagorno-Karabak, the region where Azerbaijan subsequently expelled around 100,000 ethnic Armenians. Has F1 adjusted its calendar for the benefit of a repressive regime which is using it for ‘sportswashing’? Perhaps the subject was discussed when F1 CEO Stefano Domenicali met in 2024 with Aliyev and “Formula 1 consultant Flavio Briatore”, as the president’s office curiously described the Alpine executive at the time.

Antonelli’s to lose

Until lap 15 of the Spanish Grand Prix Lando Norris looked poised to take his third win in four races, further trimming Andrea Kimi Antonell’s points lead. Then the Virtual Safety Car intervened.

Antonelli now leads his increasingly struggling team mate George Russell by 81 points, Lewis Hamilton by 101 and Norris – the only driver who’s looked like a regular threat to the champion-elect over the last four rounds – by 106. Realistically, unless one of Antonelli’s pursuers can pull off a Max Verstappen-2025 style resurgence, this is all over bar the shouting.

The 2026 season has turned into the kind of title fight which will have Domenicali gazing covetously at NASCAR’s Chase for the Cup and musing that his vision of F1 is at least one more gimmick away from perfection. Until that happens, the remaining races will be a case of whether Antonelli might fumble his big change. Baku is exactly the kind of track which can punish a driver – remember what happened to Oscar Piastri last year – but Antonelli has shown few signs of committing such errors so far.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Virtually unfair

Norris’s turn of misfortune prompted criticism of F1’s Virtual Safety Car rules. The timing of the VSC period allowed every driver bar the race leader the chance to make a pit stop with minimal time loss.

Should F1 tweak its rules to avoid a repeat? Such a change would probably only make a difference to a very small number of cases, but that could be taken as an argument for or against it.

Williams’ long-awaited upgrade

Williams’ fortunes as F1 returns to Baku are in sharp contrast to their situation 12 months ago. Carlos Sainz Jnr parked his car on the front row and finished on the podium, scoring more points in one race than the team has over the whole of 2026.

The Grove squad will bring a significant upgrade for Sainz and Alexander Albon’s cars this weekend. But team principal James Vowles says it will not transform their difficult season.

“We’re going to be bringing two new chassis to the event in a bid to get our car mass below the [minimum weight] limit,” he said in a video released by the team. “So that should be a strong step of performance for us. In addition to that, we’ll have some aerodynamic upgrades that go with it.

“There is a ‘however’: the field has moved on so significantly, and these upgrades, whilst powerful, simply won’t be what we are looking for in order to consistently score points.”

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

F1’s ‘treble triple’ begins – or does it?

This weekend’s round will be the first of three consecutive events. It kicks off a run of nine rounds in the space of just 11 weeks which will bring the 2026 season to an end.

Or will it? FOM is yet to confirm whether its planned final two events in the Middle East will go ahead, despite rising hostilities in the region. F1 has announced next season will begin with the two rounds it had to scratch this season, but it remains to be seen whether the current championship will conclude as planned.

Three-pointed stars

Mercedes have again proved the masters of a new set of power unit regulations. They haven’t been beaten to pole position all year and Antonelli scored the 12th grand prix victory for their power units in Spain.

With that, Mercedes engines have won as many grands prix in F1 history as Ferrari, one of the sport’s greatest names. Mercedes will surely topple their rivals before the season is over, and will quite likely do so this weekend – unless Charles Leclerc can conjure up more of his Baku magic.

Sports.title: Formula 1 cuts grand prix distances for 2027 in latest power unit rules compromise | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Formula 1’s engine regulations have led the series to cut the length of grands prix next year.

The current maximum race distance of 305 kilometres, for all events except Monaco, has been in place for decades.

The FIA confirmed a new maximum of 290 kilometres will apply from next year. The sport’s governing body said the change is being made “in line with the refinements to the power unit regulations to be introduced in 2027 on fuel flow.”

The change has been made necessary as a result of the alterations to the 2027 engine rules which were agreed soon after this season began. After teams realised the current rules forced cars to slow significantly at most circuits to save electrical energy, teams agreed to increase the proportion of combustion power for next year.

As this change will lead to an increase in fuel flow and consumption, some teams faced having to redesign their cars for next year to a greater extent than they originally intended in order to complete existing race distances under the new rules. To avoid this, the FIA has instead agreed to shorten races.

“In line with the refinements to the power unit regulations to be introduced in 2027 on fuel flow, a reduction in the total race distance from 305km to 290km was approved, corresponding to a reduction of two or three laps,” said the FIA in a statement.”

Separately, the FIA has removed the thee-hour time limit on interrupted races. “Regarding races that are disrupted by rain or other factors, it was decided that a hard stop time would be introduced for the end of any racing activity, but that the current limitation of a race to three hours (from its start to its end – including interruptions) would be removed,” it explained. “The limit of two hours of actual racing will remain.”

“These changes were introduced to ensure that the spectators have the best possible chance to enjoy a full race if disruptions occur. It was also agreed that there would be greater flexibility to extend free practice sessions should they be interrupted.”

The FIA also approved rules granting teams greater freedom in developing their gearboxes for next year. “Following consultation with the relevant manufacturer working group, and a recommendation from the Sporting Advisory Committee, it was agreed to remove gearbox homologation for 2027 which would preserve supplier development freedom,” it said.

Sports.title: Wolff tried to help Masi ‘for the good of the sport, and for us’ in 2021 | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff has revealed details of his conversations with former race director Michael Masi before his controversial call in the 2021 championship-decider.

Masi lost his job over his mishandling of the 2021 Abu Dhabi Grand Prix. He arranged a final-lap restart in contravention of the rules which led Wolff’s driver Lewis Hamilton to lose the championship to Max Verstappen.

Hamilton and Verstappen were involved in a series of controversial collisions over the course of 2021. Wolff, who previously called Masi “disrespectful” and a “liability”, said he had concerns over how the race director reacted to feedback from the drivers.

“I really tried to speak to Michael and guide him all along the year,” Wolff told High Performance. “I said ‘listen I’ve been in the sport for a long time, listen to the drivers, don’t always be stubborn in your decision making, don’t be arrogant’.”

Wolff admitted his motivation in speaking to the race director was partly to advance Mercedes’ interest.

“I tried that for the good of the sport, and obviously also for us as a team not to be vulnerable to situations that could be totally detrimental,” he said.

Masi contradicted the regulations and his past interpretation of them by arranging a final-lap restart at Yas Marina by removing the lapped cars between Hamilton and Verstappen, but not any of the others. The FIA later ruled this had been an error. Verstappen passed Hamilton immediately after the restart, clinching his first world championship and denying Hamilton a record-breaking eighth.

Wolff said Masi’s actions were “inexcusable.”

“You could say the empathy should make me realise how he feels,” he said. “I realise how it feels.

“And I know that’s not good, and bad, but he could have thought about it all year long, when people, not only me, tried to support him in the right way.

“So sometimes you have to just realise that someone is just doing his own thing or taking his own decisions. So for me, I don’t care about it anymore.”

However he admitted he still reflects on the lost championship “every week”.

“I mainly think about it because I think Lewis deserved to be the greatest of all time with eight world championship titles,” he said. “And you can argue all along about that year.

“I think Max and Lewis were deserving champions. There were instances during the year where Max lost some points that he shouldn’t have lost. You look at the crash in Monza both of them had. So both deserving champions, but on that particular afternoon in Abu Dhabi, it was unfair.”

Following his departure from F1, Masi joined SRO Motorsports Australia last week as head of sporting operations.

Sports.title: Denzel Bentley’s Yoenli Hernandez Defense Heads to Purse Bid
Sports.content:
Denzel Bentley’s first defense as WBO middleweight champion is headed toward the fight he hoped to delay. Talks with mandatory challenger Yoenli Hernandez have failed, with a September 29 purse bid set to decide who stages the bout.

Bentley had a unification with IBF champion Aaron McKenna in reach. The WBO blocked it, ruling that its overdue mandatory obligation passed to Bentley when he was elevated to full champion. The sanctioning body also rejected a proposed title fight with Conor Benn. Bentley has the belt, but little freedom to choose what comes next.

Bentley has every reason to be frustrated. McKenna offered a UK fight with commercial appeal and, on paper, a more manageable opponent. Instead, he must face Hernandez, a highly regarded Cuban who brings far less name recognition and a serious risk of taking his belt. Bentley earned the interim title in the ring, but gained the full championship through elevation. If Hernandez beats him, there is no guarantee he finds another route to a world title. The McKenna unification and the bargaining power that comes with being champion would be gone.

Hernandez is a two-time amateur world champion, but Bentley has the deeper professional experience. He went twelve rounds with Janibek Alimkhanuly; Hernandez has yet to fight twelve as a professional. Bentley’s best chance is to close the distance with discipline, work to the body, and make Hernandez fight at a pace he cannot set himself entirely. Loading up on single punches would give the challenger time to move and score between Bentley’s attacks.

Hernandez’s August win over Francisco Daniel Veron offers a useful caution, though not a ready-made plan. Veron kept pressing and reached the final bell, but two judges gave Hernandez the fight by wide margins; the third scored it even. Pressure alone did not erase the Cuban’s cleaner work.

The purse bid adds another uncertainty. If a promoter outside Bentley’s camp wins, the champion may have to defend away from home. The WBO’s $200,000 minimum bid says where bidding starts, not what either fighter will earn.

Bentley wanted McKenna and a chance to add a second belt. Now he must beat Hernandez to keep the first one. For a champion who waited years for this position, that is a steep price for a fight with so little commercial upside.

Facing Yoenli carries massive tactical risk, but it remains the only move that preserves Bentley’s championship equity. Even if Hernandez outboxes him, Bentley at least collects a champion’s 75 percent purse bid share and goes down swinging with his career earnings maximized. If he vacates out of self-preservation, he surrenders the title for zero dollars, forfeits the McKenna unification anyway, and brands himself as a champion who ran from his mandatory.

In professional boxing, getting outpointed by a world-class Cuban amateur hurts, but surrendering the belt in a conference room without getting paid ruins a career far worse.

Without the WBO belt, Bentley reverts instantly to being a tough, high-risk, low-reward domestic gatekeeper. At thirty-one years old, clawing back up the sanctioning body rankings could take years, with no guarantee of ever receiving another title shot.

Sports.title: Teofimo Lopez Questions WBA Future After Catterall Order
Sports.content:
Teofimo Lopez is sitting down with his management and legal team to figure out if he actually wants to keep the WBA in his plans moving forward. The sanctioning body just ordered him to defend his welterweight belt against mandatory challenger Jack Catterall, and the immediate reaction from Lopez’s camp tells you everything.

“NEWS: Teofimo Lopez’s team says 3 weeks ago Gilberto Mendoza personally assured them the Catterall fight wouldn’t be ordered & Lopez could pursue a bigger fight. He’ll meet with his managers, Keith Connolly & Mike Borao, & legal team to decide if he wants to allow the WBA to be part of his future plans. #boxing,” said Dan Rafael on X.

Teofimo has stopped short of saying he will drop the belt, yet the wording speaks volumes. If his side had any real desire to mix it up with Catterall, they would not be sitting around plotting an exit from the WBA system.

His camp claims WBA president Gilberto Mendoza promised them three weeks back that Catterall would get bypassed so Teofimo could chase a massive payday. Mendoza owes the public an answer on that. The official stance from the sanctioning body states that Teofimo inherited the mandatory commitment the moment he took the welterweight super title from Rolando Romero on August 22. Both camps have until October 22 to work out terms before purse bids enter the picture.

Stylistically, Catterall represents pure problems for Teofimo without offering a massive purse to justify the danger. The British contender works out of a disciplined southpaw stance, glides along the perimeter, controls distance with a sharp jab, and punishes aggressive mistakes. We watched Sandor Martin and Jamaine Ortiz give Teofimo fits simply by making him lead, refusing to trade inside the pocket, and circling away from his power. Catterall has the exact tools to drag Teofimo through another frustrating night.

The financial upside looks completely upside down. Dropping a decision to Catterall destroys any massive showdown with Ryan. Picking up a decision keeps the hardware but does not build extra hype for that blockbuster. If this saga goes to a purse bid, Matchroom holds the muscle to outbid Top Rank, take control of the promotion, and stick Teofimo on hostile territory.

The calendar is open for this defense anyway. Ryan is currently in talks to face Isaac Cruz, meaning Teofimo does not have to clear his schedule right this second to stay in position. That reality makes this summit with Connolly, Borao, and the attorneys look weak. Teofimo possesses a clear path to defend the belt, collect a win, and still secure Ryan down the road.

A champion cannot reasonably claim the title’s advantages while treating its mandatory challenger as an inconvenience to be removed.

Sports.title: Jacob Bank Gets Zhanibek Alimkhanuly Title Shot
Sports.content:
Jacob Bank protested when the WBO reinstated Zhanibek Alimkhanuly at the peak of its super middleweight rankings following a doping suspension. Now the sanctioning body has ordered Bank to trade punches with him for its vacant championship. The Danish contender possesses the exact opening he demanded, paired with the most dangerous opponent of his professional life.

WBO president Gustavo Olivieri announced on X that both camps have fifteen days to finalize terms before purse bid proceedings take over. The formal written decree will surface shortly.

Bank previously insisted that gifting Alimkhanuly an immediate path to the belt cheated active contenders who climbed the rankings through merit. Accepting the match does not erase that criticism. It forces Bank to validate his complaints inside the ring.

A massive incentive exists for Danish boxing. Bank built a dedicated local following in Kolding, yet capturing a world belt would provide Denmark its first premier 168 pound titleholder since the Mikkel Kessler era. The jump in class remains extreme. Bank has never shared a ring with a world champion possessing Alimkhanuly’s southpaw timing, pedigree, and precision.

Alimkhanuly faces his own trial. He dominated at middleweight, but moving up eight pounds tests his punch resistance and speed against a naturally bigger man. If Bank absorbs the early fire, applies relentless pressure, and attacks the ribs along the ropes, he will expose how well the Kazakh fighter holds up across twelve rounds at 168 pounds. Marching forward behind an upright guard will get Bank wrecked by Alimkhanuly’s signature straight left and counter uppercuts.

Pacheco holds the number two ranking above Bank, yet Olivieri bypassed him entirely by labeling Bank the first available contender. Pacheco squares off against Darius Fulghum on November 14 on DAZN. That booking hints at calculated matchmaking from his handlers, choosing to protect his trajectory rather than jump straight into a bout against an avoided southpaw.

The WBO had no choice. Olivieri had to keep the belt moving once Sheeraz vacated, and Pacheco effectively took himself off the board. Bank might be a far less marketable name internationally, but he is doing what Pacheco chose not to do: taking the fight that actually tests him.

If the fifteen-day window expires without signatures, a purse bid determines who controls the ring, the location, and the network. A Top Rank bid takes Bank to America on ESPN, while local backing from promoter Kasper Holgersen could bring the event to Denmark. Bank complained about the sanctioning body cutting corners for Alimkhanuly. He now holds the contract to settle that dispute with his fists.

Sports.title: Jack Catterall Corners Teofimo Lopez With WBA Order
Sports.content:
Teofimo Lopez has a Ryan Garcia payday in sight, but Jack Catterall now has a deadline and a WBA order. Lopez must negotiate a welterweight title defense against Catterall by October 22, leaving little time to keep both fights in play.

Eddie Hearn announced that the WBA had ordered immediate negotiations for Teofimo to face Catterall next. The organization’s resolution gives the fighters 30 days to reach a deal before a purse bid.

Catterall has already waited while another champion took the more appealing fight. He beat Shakhram Giyasov for the WBA’s secondary title, only to see Rolando Romero defend his top belt against Lopez. Now Catterall can demand his shot from Lopez, and asking him to step aside a second time would likely be expensive.

Lopez also has a boxing reason to dislike this order. Sandor Martin dropped him in their 2022 fight, while Jamaine Ortiz spent much of their 2024 meeting moving away and frustrating his attempts to set the pace. Catterall is another disciplined southpaw who can make Lopez lead, catch him with straight left hands and tie him up when he gets close. Lopez won both earlier fights, but neither offered an encouraging blueprint for this assignment.

The financial choice is harsher. Garcia draws an audience with or without a WBA belt, although Lopez would bring more to a unification promotion as champion. Defending against Catterall first puts that larger fight at risk. Vacating would cost Lopez his title and invite criticism, but it could protect his route to Garcia.

Hey mate @TeofimoLopez, you fancy scrapping on the furyA-J card ? If not, don’t worry, I’ll come to America and get my belt. Either way, I’ll see you soon, champ 🤝,” said Catterall on X.

A purse bid would create another concern for Lopez’s team: Matchroom could pursue the right to stage the fight in Britain. That outcome is possible, not guaranteed, and depends on who bids and how much.

Catterall does not have to accept a small payment to clear Lopez’s schedule. The October 22 deadline puts the pressure where he wants it: Lopez must make a deal, fight him, or decide how much the WBA belt is really worth.

It’s predictable what Teofimo will do next. He will almost certainly search for a way around this fight, and if that door slams shut, he will drop the WBA title rather than enter the ring with Jack Catterall. Getting into the ring with Catterall makes zero financial or strategic sense for Teofimo right now. Catterall is a nightmare-style match. He is a defensive, calculating southpaw who refuses to walk forward, ties opponents up on the inside, and fires sharp straight lefts.

Teofimo looked completely disorganized against Sandor Martin and spent twelve frustrating rounds chasing Jamaine Ortiz around the ring. Fighting Catterall offers terrible money, massive tactical risk, and a high probability of blowing an eight-figure payday. Teofimo’s first playbook will be an attempt to pay Catterall off. They will test the waters on a step-aside package. The problem is that Eddie Hearn and Catterall know they have Teofimo cornered. Catterall already stepped aside once so Romero could face Teofimo.

For Catterall to wait again while Teofimo fights Ryan, the check would have to be enormous. If Matchroom demands an unreasonable price or insists that Catterall gets his mandated shot, negotiations will grind to a halt. When that happens, expect Teofimo to vacate the strap. He will not travel to the UK for a purse bid, nor will Top Rank overpay to stage a low-drawing stylistic trap in the United States. Teofimo knows the public will buy a fight with Ryan on name recognition alone. Ryan just stopped Conor Benn in two rounds, owns the WBC belt, and brings massive commercial traction.

Ryan does not need Teofimo to hold the WBA strap to sell pay-per-views. If Teofimo drops the belt, he avoids a dangerous opponent, keeps his promotional schedule intact, and goes straight into a massive 2027 event with Ryan. Given his history of avoiding tricky stylistic operators when big money is on the table, discarding the title is the cleanest escape route he has.

Lopez’s manager Keith Connolly says his team received a different message from the WBA before the order. In a post on X, he wrote:

“I respect everyone’s opinion, including yours @BoxeoPats, but we were told something different by WBA, so yes, we’ll sit with Teo and decide what we will do. Teo wants the biggest fights possible 💪🏻”

Connolly did not explain what the WBA had previously told them. His response leaves open whether Lopez will negotiate with Catterall or pursue another route to a Ryan Garcia fight.

Sports.title: Daniel Dubois Knockdowns Hand Fabio Wardley a Dangerous Illusion
Sports.content:
Fabio Wardley convinces himself that dropping Daniel Dubois twice proved he can shatter the WBO heavyweight champion inside three rounds. The harsher reality is that Dubois took the best shots Wardley could muster, shifted the battle lines, then methodically battered the challenger into submission the moment that initial explosion burned out.

The rematch arrives October 17 at The O2, just five months after Dubois stopped Wardley in the eleventh round in Manchester. Wardley intends to rush the champion and extract him before the fourth round ends.

“I had it done almost in the first round of our first fight, almost in the third round of our fight. So we’re gonna go back to the drawing board, pick apart those moments, pick apart you stylistically, what worked, what didn’t work, and within the first quarter of the fight you’ll be gone, you’ll be outta there,” Wardley told DAZN.

Wardley blindsided Dubois early with clubbing right hands while Dubois kept an undisciplined guard. The opening blow landed seconds into the contest, followed by another shot dropping Dubois in round three. Those trips to the canvas proved to be fool’s gold.

Dubois found success with a heavy jab, wiping out the mid-range Wardley needed to whip wide hooks. Shoved into retreat, Wardley hunted single haymakers instead of creating openings through straight punches.

The physical disparity turned brutal. Wardley loaded full body weight into every power shot, ignoring feints, declining light jabs, betting everything on immediate destruction. Once Dubois absorbed the barrage, Wardley stood exposed, with no alternate plan.

Glaring technical habits made Wardley target practice down the stretch. He retreated in straight lines with his chin up, giving Dubois easy reads to crunch straight right hands. Dubois no longer worried about looping rights coming back. He slipped inside the arc, took away the room, then unloaded heavy leather at will.

Dubois brought mental toughness that abandoned him during past losses. Hitting the canvas twice never rattled him into trading wildly. He regained his legs, relied on his stamina, letting Wardley punch himself dry. Wardley labels himself a victim of his own early success, claiming that hurting Dubois seduced him away from boxing discipline.

The promise of a rapid blowout reveals the same psychological flaw still rules his thinking. He treats the knockdowns as a guarantee that swinging harder produces a finish. Relying on a three-round blitz assumes Dubois will repeat the identical defensive lapses without making adjustments.

If Wardley rushes Dubois looking for the knockout, he burns his stamina rapidly and leaves himself open to Dubois’ straight right hand. Wardley possesses the raw power to stun Dubois early, but counting on Dubois to crumble rather than weather the storm is an enormous gamble that previously cost Wardley the fight.

Sports.title: Johnny Fisher Returns Where Dave Allen Broke Him
Sports.content:
Zuffa Boxing paid an extraordinary premium for Johnny Fisher, but its primary task is repairing a heavyweight Dave Allen dismantled. Saturday’s main event against Michael Pirotton at London’s Copper Box Arena is tailored to make Fisher look dangerous again without placing him near anyone capable of repeating Allen’s handiwork.

The venue provides its own uncomfortable history. This is the very ring where Allen dropped Fisher twice before stopping him in the fifth round. Zuffa is attempting to scrub that humiliation away immediately, yet sending Fisher straight back to the scene of his worst professional defeat risks backfiring if those lingering technical flaws remain uncorrected.

“That is an accurate number, without going into the actual nitty-gritty of numbers,” Fisher admitted to Ariel Helwani regarding reports that Zuffa offered roughly six and a half times Matchroom’s proposal. Fisher previously called the figures life changing while giving Eddie Hearn an opportunity to match the package before abandoning the promoter who built his London ticket base.

Matchroom recognized Fisher’s true market ceiling. Hearn reaped the rewards of Fisher, his father, and the Romford Bull Army packing local arenas, but he refused to match Zuffa’s wild numbers. Matchroom placed a hard cap on Fisher’s financial value the moment his raw gate appeal collided with his actual boxing ability.

Zuffa made an aggressive gamble instead. The company purchased a regional ticket seller for money normally reserved for genuine world title contenders.

Allen demonstrated why protecting that investment is such a difficult chore. Allen did not rely on blistering hand speed to shatter Fisher. He simply timed Fisher’s stiff posture, waited for him to telegraph looping right hands, and capitalized on Fisher’s sluggish recovery. Fisher charged in straight paths, abandoned head movement, and offered up his chin the second he swung for knockouts.

In pure boxing terms, Dave Allen is a durable domestic gatekeeper who was routinely handled whenever he stepped up to world level. If a heavyweight gets stopped in five rounds by Allen, the dream of turning him into a legitimate world title contender is essentially dead in the water.

Yet Zuffa handed Fisher a contract worth six or seven times what Matchroom offered. To avoid lighting that cash on fire, Zuffa cannot treat Fisher like a traditional prospect on a path toward Oleksandr Usyk or the world top ten. Instead, Zuffa has to treat him as a purely commercial vehicle.

Pirotton (12-2, 6 KOs) was chosen precisely because he cannot replicate that danger. The 6’5″ Belgian has height and moves reasonably well, but he lacks Allen’s infighting craft and carries no signature power to discourage Fisher. Pirotton’s six-round decision defeat to Piotr Lacz in the WBC Grand Prix confirms he presents minimal danger to Zuffa’s costly new asset.

The bout serves as a gentle laboratory for trainer Tony Sims. Sims inherited Fisher following the Allen destruction, taking on the burden of rebuilding a fighter’s defensive structure under the glare of top billing. Basic technical questions demand answers: Can Fisher keep his chin tucked, work behind a stiff jab, and recover his stance with discipline, or will the crowd tempt him into another wild shootout?

This situation creates an immediate matchmaking trap for Zuffa. A rapid knockout over Pirotton proves nothing about Fisher’s growth. A sloppy, competitive scrap, on the other hand, confirms that the Allen stoppage was no fluke.

Paying astronomical purses for safe European trial horses is unsustainable. Domestic names like Frazer Clarke and Solomon Dacres possess the exact tools Allen used to undo Fisher. Zuffa cannot compensate Fisher like a world-class attraction while matchmaking for him like a fragile prospect.

Fisher is basically the Essex version of former four-round fighter Butterbean: big, loud, relatable, flanked by his dad chanting on social media, and backed by a crowd that drinks the arena dry. If Fisher blasts Pirotton out on Saturday, Zuffa faces a fork in the road, but continuing down the Butterbean path runs into a massive financial problem.

Butterbean was cheap to stage. Zuffa is paying Fisher world-class contender money. You cannot pay a heavyweight six or seven times Matchroom’s rate and keep feeding him Michael Pirottons or Ivan Balazs without bleeding cash. The UK boxing public also has a very low tolerance for obvious mismatches in televised main events. If Zuffa keeps serving up obscure European opponents on Sky Sports, the Romford Bull Army might still show up for the pints, but the wider viewing audience will tune out.

Sports.title: Has Canelo Alvarez Declined Too Far for Christian Mbilli?
Sports.content:
Canelo Alvarez’s decline did not begin with Terence Crawford. Crawford removed the remaining doubt after Jaime Munguia, Edgar Berlanga and William Scull demonstrated that Canelo was losing the speed, activity and aggression that separated him from ordinary champions.

Those opponents suited Canelo, yet none fell before the final bell. He fought in brief spurts, leaned on single power punches and allowed long stretches to pass without forcing the action. His last stoppage occurred against Caleb Plant in November 2021.

The deterioration shows clearly in Canelo’s jab. During peak campaigns against Gennadiy Golovkin and Callum Smith, he drove an authoritative lead hand to dictate distance, split high guards and create openings for hooks. That punch has deteriorated into a lazy pawing motion that opponents parry with little concern.

Without an authoritative jab collecting a toll at the perimeter, aggressive opponents march straight into pocket range. That grants Christian Mbilli direct access to unload combinations without having to solve a layered defense first.

Canelo’s multi-punch body combinations vanished as well. The classic left hook downstairs doubled with a hook upstairs demanded explosive torque from his hips. He now settles for isolated overhand rights and looping hooks. Opponents brace for those solitary attempts and fire back before Canelo reorganizes his guard.

Scull exposed another troubling pattern. Once the Cuban gained confidence and let his hands go, Canelo spent long stretches parked against the ropes. That was not the slick baiting technique Canelo displayed in his prime.

A younger Canelo rested dynamically through trunk movement while keeping his base centered. The current version retreats straight back, physically resting his weight on the cables to catch his breath. That passive posture hands opponents ring generalship, influences judges, and gives away rounds on sheer inactivity.

Crawford dismantled those exact tendencies. Canelo chased him flat-footed in straight lines, loaded up on telegraphed blows and lacked the sustained output needed to flip the narrative. An elbow ailment provides an easy excuse, but that physical issue fails to explain the missing fire against Munguia, Berlanga and Scull.

Working alongside Oleksandr Usyk brings plenty of promotional chatter. Usyk provides tactical insights and conditioning drills, yet he cannot turn back the clock on Canelo’s legs or reflexes. Canelo started fighting professionally as a teenager in 2005. Over twenty years of prize fights, hard gym wars and brutal training have ground down his joints, leaving wear on his shoulders, knees and arms that no single training camp can scrub away.

Mbilli’s relentless tempo presents severe danger. The contender attacks in waves, pounding the torso, arms and shoulders when clean head openings close up. An aging veteran hunting for breathers between thirty-second charges struggles when confronted by someone who ignores the referee’s breaks and pushes the pace.

Canelo retains the superior boxing brain, but Mbilli meets him when the physical engine can no longer execute those master plans over twelve exhausting rounds. Spending over twelve months on the shelf following joint surgery rarely produces a fountain of youth. It often produces a slower fighter burdened with ring rust and relying on lucky one-shot counters. The debate no longer centers on how prime Canelo handled crude swarmers. The issue is how little of that elite operator walks into the ring tonight.

Canelo built his entire hall of fame run on intimidating guys into low-output chess matches. When opponents feared the return fire, they stayed on the outside, threw tentative jabs, and let Canelo dictate a glacial pace where his limited gas tank never became a liability. He could sit in neutral for two minutes of every round because thirty seconds of explosive, flashy counter combinations were enough to bank the frame on the cards.

Mbilli completely breaks that formula. He is the ultimate volume merchant. He does not possess top-shelf technical defense, but he does not care to. He enters the pocket like a bowling ball, throws 70 to 80 punches a round, and beats fighters around the collarbones, biceps, and ribcage until their guard drops from sheer exhaustion.

If Canelo cannot make Mbilli taste severe, concussive power in the opening three rounds, he is in for a horrific night. Without blazing hand speed, Canelo’s single-shot counters will bounce off Mbilli’s forehead while the Frenchman keeps driving forward.

Once Canelo gets forced into the ropes, the fight transforms from a technical boxing match into an attritional brawl. An aging fighter with twenty years of wear, a surgically repaired elbow, and a shallow engine cannot survive being battered along the cables for twelve continuous rounds. If Canelo spends the second half of the fight covering up in a high shell while Mbilli unloads hooks to his sides, the referee or the corner will be forced to save him from a punishing beating.

Sports.title: Jaime Munguía Ordered Into Bektemir Melikuziev Defense
Sports.content:
Jaime Munguía faces a mandatory defense that carries serious danger. The WBA ordered its super middleweight champion to negotiate with Bektemir Melikuziev, giving both camps until October 21 to reach an agreement.

Munguía spent years benefiting from calculated matchmaking. The clearest exception came against Canelo Alvarez, who dropped him and coasted to a wide decision in May 2024. Melikuziev lacks Canelo’s complete skillset, but his southpaw power and vicious body punching present an unusually severe threat.

“The WBA orders negotiations between Jaime Munguía and Bektemir Melikuziev for the super middleweight championship. They have until October 21 to reach an agreement,” said ESPN’s Salvador Rodriguez about the WBA’s order.

Failure to agree before the deadline will force the sanctioning body to send the bout to a purse bid.

Munguía (46-2, 35 KOs) captured the belt by outworking Jose Armando Resendiz over twelve rounds on May 2. He controlled that bout with sheer punch output, but Resendiz lacked the speed or punching power to make him pay for his customary defensive holes.

Bruno Surace revealed the real cost of those habits. The French underdog detonated a single overhand right to flatten Munguía in round six during their December 2024 meeting in Tijuana. Surace entered that ring with only five career knockouts.

Munguía avenged that defeat on points five months later in Saudi Arabia, but going twelve rounds did nothing to erase the technical carelessness that got him dropped. If an unproven puncher like Surace can connect so cleanly, Melikuziev can do considerably worse.

Melikuziev (17-1, 11 KOs) attacks with heavy hands and relentless intent downstairs. The 2016 Olympic silver medalist hunts from a southpaw stance, waiting for opponents to overcommit before uncorking his straight left hand.

That punch serves as the ultimate weapon against Munguía. The Tijuana native habitually drops his lead shoulder, flaring his elbows wide as he charges inside with looping rights. His guard splits apart, presenting an inviting path straight down the pipe. Canelo exploited that exact opening, splitting Munguía’s gloves with a short counter uppercut to put him on the canvas.

Munguía holds advantages in height and reach, yet physical dimensions offer little protection if he ditches his jab to brawl inside. Melikuziev relishes opponents who plant their feet in front of him. He ducks under wild punches, gains dominant foot position, and digs crunching hooks into the ribcage. Munguía’s smartest path requires pumping a stiff jab from range while refusing to get drawn into mid-ring fire fights. That approach demands strict round-by-round composure, a quality Munguía rarely maintains. His first reaction to taking a punch is always firing back with wild, prolonged flurries.

Melikuziev carries his own flaws. Gabriel Rosado knocked him unconscious with a single counter right hand in 2021 by timing his reckless forward rushes. Munguía throws the necessary volume to exploit that vulnerability, but trading on the inside turns the bout into an outright chin contest.

The WBA ruling presents an awkward problem for Golden Boy Promotions. Oscar De La Hoya relies on Munguía to headline cards and generate box office revenue. Melikuziev remains a high-risk stablemate who brings minimal commercial upside. Pitting them against each other risks derailing a major asset. Munguía could drop the belt and chase a softer payday. Vacating the title immediately after beating Resendiz would only validate complaints about his protected matchmaking.

Accepting the Melikuziev bout forces him to defend his belt against the exact puncher his career architecture was built to dodge.

Panic is the only realistic word for what Fernando Beltran and Oscar De La Hoya are experiencing right now. This WBA order is an operational disaster for Zanfer and Golden Boy because it blows up the entire business model they built around Munguía.

The belt was supposed to improve Munguía’s bargaining power, not force him into a low-paying fight with perhaps the most dangerous opponent available. Golden Boy finally rebuilt Munguía after the Canelo and Bruno Surace losses, secured a title against a manageable champion, and positioned him for another major event. Now the WBA is demanding a defense against a powerful southpaw who can attack every defensive flaw Munguía still has.

Golden Boy’s initial maneuver will likely involve offering Melikuziev step-aside compensation to clear the path. Promoting both fighters gives Oscar De La Hoya room to guarantee the Uzbek a showcase slot, a substantial fee, and a promised title shot down the road. That arrangement would buy Munguía time to hunt down a far more profitable voluntary defense while keeping his belt intact.

The October 21 deadline offers plenty of room to stall. Munguía’s team can easily drag out talks over financial splits, site locations, or distribution rights before asking for an extension. The WBA already let Rolando Romero bypass Shakhram Giyasov without rushing to a purse bid, handing Munguía’s side a proven playbook to drag their feet and test the sanctioning body’s resolve.

Dropping the title remains the ultimate eject button. Munguía could announce that lucrative opportunities elsewhere require his attention, but surrendering the belt without a single defense exposes the farce of taking it from Reséndiz in the first place. The hardware served its purpose when it promised leverage for major paydays. Melikuziev now forces Munguía to prove whether keeping that belt is worth risking his career against a genuine puncher.

Ghana News.title: Lekzy DeComic to feature four generations of comedians on upcoming show
Ghana News.content:
Lekzy DeComic has announced a comedy show featuring four generations of Ghanaian comedians.

Dubbed Lekzy Unleashed: The Godfather Edition the programme will be held on Friday, 7th November 2026, at the UPSA Auditorium in Accra.

On the night, the two-time Comedian of the Year, Lekzy will host Kweku Sintim-Misa (KSM), Clemento Suarez, Fritz Baffour, Tommy Annan-Forson, DKB, Foster Romanus, Jeneral Ntatia, Kwaku Manu, and Khemikal.

Others are Mr Beautiful, David Oscar Dogbe, Parrot Mouth, Percy Obrempong, James Brown, Jeffery Nortey and, from South Africa, Chris Mapane.

The comedy night will be tinged with a spot of music by Ghana’s Rap Doctor, Okyeame Kwame.

KSM is touted as the Undisputed King of Comedy, after filling the National Theatre for 13 sold-out nights and cementing his brand as Ghana’s finest satirists. Fritz Baffour, on the other hand, became the Father of Prime Time Comedy. He started stand-up comedy in Ghana in 1986 with Tommy Annan Forson at a time when no one believed anybody could make a living making people laugh.

Tommy Annan-Forson’s story is quite interesting. He was the first to laugh on state-owned radio (the GBC) and got queried for it. He then had to move the humour to the stage.

Over the years these two have not just proven their mettle as pacesetters of comedy in Ghana. They have supported the younger generation of comedians in various ways.

Tickets are available via *714*800#.

Ghana News.title: Nigeria wins arbitration as Sunrise’s $400 million hydropower claim dismissed
Ghana News.content:
President Bola Tinubu

Nigeria has won an international arbitration case after a tribunal dismissed ​a $400 million claim by Sunrise Power and ‌Transmission over the long-delayed Mambilla hydroelectric project, Attorney-General Lateef Fagbemi said on Tuesday.

The September 17 ruling removes a ​major legal obstacle to the 3,050-megawatt hydropower ​project, potentially reviving Nigeria's biggest hydroelectric scheme ⁠after nearly two decades of delays.

Jumpstart your morning with the latest legal news delivered straight to your inbox from The Daily Docket newsletter. Sign up here.

Fagbemi said the ​International Chamber of Commerce tribunal found that settlement ​agreements relied on by Sunrise were not binding on Nigeria because the officials who signed them lacked the authority ​to commit the government without presidential approval.

He ​said the tribunal also found the agreements were tainted by ‌corruption ⁠and contrary to Nigerian public policy, making them unenforceable.

Fagbemi said Sunrise was ordered to pay 75% of Nigeria's legal fees and expenses, with 10% ​interest compounded ​annually.

Sunrise did ⁠not immediately respond to a request for comment.

The ruling could clear the ​way for renewed efforts to advance the ​project, ⁠whose financing from China's Export-Import Bank had been contingent on resolving the dispute.

Fagbemi added that Sunrise ⁠is ​pursuing a separate arbitration claim ​against Nigeria worth more than $2.7 billion.

Ghana News.title: Xhaka under investigation over Covid-19 certificate
Ghana News.content:
Switzerland captain Granit Xhaka is under investigation by Swiss prosecutors over allegations he obtained a forged Covid-19 vaccination certificate.

The 33-year-old is alleged to have obtained the certificate in 2022, when it was a requirement in Switzerland for some travel abroad.

The public prosecutor's office of the city of Lucerne confirmed that an investigation was underway to determine whether any criminal behaviour occurred in obtaining a "false or forged" certificate.

The Sunderland midfielder, who was playing for Arsenal at the time, posted a statement on social media on Monday saying he had a "mistrust" towards the vaccine and had been "influenced by worries and uncertainty".

He said: "In this troubled state of mind, I acquired a vaccine certificate instead of clarifying my unanswered questions in the proper way.

"Today I see clearly that this way was not correct. It was a mistake. I'm sorry.

"I take responsibility for this decision and will engage with the process of establishing the facts and fully co-operate with the relevant authorities."

The Swiss Office of Public Health confirmed that while there was never a general legal requirement to obtain or hold such a certificate, it was needed for access to various activities, venues and travel, meaning that participation was restricted for anyone who did not possess one.

These measures in Switzerland were in place until spring 2022. After that point, Covid-19 certificates continued to be issued, primarily to enable members of the public to meet entry requirements when travelling abroad.

It is unclear what punishments Xhaka could face, but in 2023 the then Switzerland men's ice hockey coach Patrick Fischer was found guilty of using a fake Covid-19 certificate to work at the 2022 Winter Olympics ‌in Beijing.

Fischer was fined 38,000 Swiss francs by a criminal court. In April this year, he was sacked from the Switzerland job and earlier this month, he was banned for four years by the International Ice Hockey Federation.

The Swiss Football Association said Xhaka, the country's record appearance holder with 152 caps, had withdrawn from the Swiss camp for their upcoming Nations League matches against Scotland, North Macedonia and Slovenia following his statement.

It added the decision to withdraw had been made jointly by the player and management and that they would discuss Xhaka's future with the team after the international window.

Switzerland have away fixtures against North Macedonia and Scotland on 26 and 29 September, before facing Slovenia and North Macedonia at home in early October.

Sunderland boss Regis le Bris refused to comment on the allegations following the Black Cats' defeat at Manchester City on Sunday.

"It is not my area to speak about those problems or situations," he said. "My area is football. About football, he is really good."

Xhaka captained Switzerland at the World Cup earlier this year, where they were knocked out in the quarter-finals by eventual runners-up Argentina.

Ghana News.title: FAW chief questions Infantino’s Fifa reform claims
Ghana News.content:
FIFA president Gianni Infantino

Football Association of Wales chief executive Noel Mooney has played down suggestions Fifa is planning major reforms.

Fifa president Gianni Infantino has proposed an external review of how world football's governing body operates and says he is open to reform.

In a letter sent to members of the Fifa Council and all of its national associations, Infantino explains the independent process would "recommend potential improvements".

"I've seen the headlines today about major reform at Fifa - that's not how the letter read to me, to be frank," Mooney said.

"I saw the letter itself that was sent out, it doesn't actually say reform of Fifa itself.

"It talks about reform around strategic projects and initiatives.

"They would look at how they were consulted and how decisions were made around that."

Infantino has come under increasing pressure over his aborted Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal.

That would have involved selling stakes in the World Cup and other competitions to private investors, and it sparked a major backlash.

The Welsh governing body was among the first national associations to withdraw backing for Infantino's bid to continue his leadership of Fifa.

Infantino will stand for election for a fourth time in March 2027, with his opponents having until 18 November to find an alternative candidate.

Mooney reiterated the FAW would not be endorsing Infantino's candidature.

"With the Fifa president, you're looking for a moral guardian of the game," Mooney told the BBC Radio Wales Phone In.

"You're not looking for somebody to sell off parts of the game.

"The World Cup does not need private equity. They have billions and billions of dollars in reserve.

"Give us the money. Let us build the pitches. You've got loads of reserves. Let's have it as soon as possible.

"There was a summit in Miami before as the World Cup kicked off, a meeting of all 211 federations.

"I stood up at that meeting and said, look, I mean, the revenue for Qatar was around eight billion.

"The revenue for this World Cup in Canada, USA and Mexico is 16 billion. Therefore, it's 100% increase in revenue, give us 100% growth."

Ghana News.title: La Liga chief dismisses Real’s ref conspiracy claims
Ghana News.content:
Javier Tebas has had several past disputes with Real Madrid

La Liga president Javier Tebas says claiming there is a refereeing conspiracy against Real Madrid is like "living in another galaxy".

Real manager Jose Mourinho accused officials of making key errors after his side were beaten 2-1 by rivals Atletico Madrid last week.

Mourinho brought printouts of screenshots to the post-match news conference, claiming Atletico should have been given two red cards in the first half.

Writing in response to an article in the Spanish media which claimed there is a "conspiracy" against Real, Tebas dismissed the allegations.

"Claiming that referees are directed against Real Madrid is living in another galaxy," Tebas said on social media.

"That narrative serves as an excuse to cover up other shortcomings that are plain to see in these first matches of the season.

"It's more comfortable to point to a conspiracy than to explain what's happening on the pitch."

Real said in statement, external that it was "intolerable" for Tebas to use his position to keep attacking the club and that his comments were "particularly serious and incomprehensible".

"It is utterly surprising that the president of La Liga dedicates his time and personal platforms to constantly trying to publicly discredit Real Madrid," said the club.

"By doing so, he continues to damage the image of our competition and Spanish football worldwide."

Real said that given Tebas' "inappropriate behavior" professional football in the country needs a "leader capable of managing it and developing its full potential" as well as having a "fundamental duty of neutrality".

"The president of La Liga is not the owner of the competition but a manager serving the clubs that comprise it and entrust him with its direction," added the statement.

"The clubs need someone who serves this mission with honesty."

Real are fourth in La Liga, six points behind Barcelona who top the table on 21 points after winning all seven of their league games this season.

After defeat by Atletico, where Real went down to 10 men in a feisty encounter after defender Dean Huijsen was sent off, Mourinho blamed the officiating.

"We can skip the press conference because the story of the match is right here," Mourinho said as he showed media the printed images.

"Those were two clear red cards. Given the difficulties we faced afterwards playing 11 against 10, we can only imagine what 50 minutes of 11 against nine would have been like."

Tebas has been critical of Real and its president Florentino Perez in previous years after disagreeing with their plans to join a European Super League in 2021.

In 2025 he said Real had "lost their head" after the club sent a formal letter of complaint to the Spanish FA about officiating in the league.

Ghana News.title: GMA rejects claims its vessel monitoring system is ineffective
Ghana News.content:
The Ghana Maritime Authority (GMA) has rejected claims that vessels operating in Ghana’s waters are not being monitored.

The Authority says its vessel monitoring system is fully operational and that it maintains 24-hour surveillance of Ghana’s maritime domain.

The GMA was responding to comments made by Dennis Miracles Aboagye on TV3’s Daily Brief and Joy FM’s Newsnite programmes on Tuesday, September 22, 2026.

The comments suggested that the Authority’s vessel monitoring system was ineffective and that vessels sailing within Ghana’s waters were not being monitored.

The GMA has described the claims as false and misleading.

In a statement, the Authority said its maritime domain awareness tools remain in use to continuously monitor vessels within Ghana’s maritime jurisdiction.

It said the surveillance system also supports the monitoring and protection of offshore oil and gas facilities, pipelines and submarine cables.

The GMA explained that it uses standard operating procedures to track vessels and verify their identities and compliance.

According to the Authority, the system is also critical to maritime safety, security and environmental protection.

“The GMA categorically refutes these claims. They are false, misleading, and do not reflect the operational reality of maritime surveillance in Ghana.”

The Authority further insisted that the suggestion that vessels operating in Ghana’s waters are not monitored is inaccurate.

“The Authority continues to use its maritime domain awareness tools to monitor vessels and maintains 24-hour surveillance and monitoring of vessels in Ghana’s maritime domain.”

The GMA said it remains committed to continuous surveillance and the protection of Ghana’s maritime interests.

It urged the public to disregard the claims and to rely on official communications from the Authority regarding vessel monitoring and maritime surveillance.

Ghana News.title: I was close to joining Liverpool in 2016 – Mbappe
Ghana News.content:
Kylian Mbappe (right) is France's all-time leading goalscorer

Kylian Mbappe has revealed how "close" he came to joining Liverpool in 2016, saying he went against the advice of his mother who "fell in love" with Anfield.

The France and Real Madrid striker said the Reds tried to sign him at 18, while he was playing for Monaco in Ligue 1.

Former Liverpool boss Jurgen Klopp said the club laid on a private jet and food for Mbappe and his family in an attempt to sign him, before he eventually joined Paris St-Germain.

Speaking to the Athletic, Mbappe said his mum was a "big fan" of Klopp and wanted her son to move to Merseyside.

"I was close to [joining] Liverpool. My mum's favourite destination was Liverpool. She wanted me to go there," he said.

"I didn't listen because I wanted to play in my city, Paris. I didn't want to leave my country before I was someone.

"But yes, my mum was always saying, 'Liverpool — you're going to be there, playing at Anfield; it's going to be insane for you'."

Mbappe, now 27, said his mother went to Liverpool for the "first step" in the negotiations.

"She went to the city, the stadium; she met the people. She was like, 'it's a wonderful club, everybody's so kind, it's a family club, a big club', said Mbappe.

"She went to Anfield and fell in love with it. She watched a few games alone, to feel the atmosphere, because she wanted to imagine me in this stadium."

Klopp, who spoke about the possible move on Magenta TV as a pundit at the 2026 World Cup, explained how a flight was taken from Blackpool to Nice in France, where "the entire Mbappe family boarded a private jet with five rooms or something".

"We really went all out. Then we flew around in a circle, talked with the family, ate good food," Klopp said.

He said they had not wanted to be seen having talks, but the meeting proved fruitless.

"We flew in a circle. It was fantastic. And then he went to Paris," Klopp added.

"It's a funny story," said Mbappe.

"But in the end, I took the decision to go to PSG because for me, born and raised in Paris, there was no better feeling than to show I could be a star in my hometown."

Mbappe later joined PSG on loan, in a deal that included an option to make the move permanent for 180m euros (£165.7m). He went on to spend seven years in Paris, becoming the club's record scorer before leaving for Real Madrid in 2024.

Ghana News.title: Ministry of Sports and Recreation holds national validation workshop on National Sports Policy Draft
Ghana News.content:
The Ministry of Sports and Recreation has held a national validation workshop on the National Sports Policy draft today, September 22, at the GNAT Hall in Accra.

The workshop was intended to grant stakeholders an opportunity to review and confirm programmes and strategies collectively identified in the draft document.

This forms part of the ongoing process to finalise the National Sports Policy 2026, which envisions a vibrant sports ecosystem that empowers Ghanaians, fosters social cohesion and inclusivity, and propels sustainable development through global sports excellence and competitiveness.

Key speakers at the event included Dr Austin Luguterah, Senior Lecturer and Director of the Sports and Wellness Directorate at the University of Ghana, Legon, who emphasised the core objectives behind the policy review:

"So, this review, which we reviewed the previous policies, was to seek to transform sports from largely a recreational activity into a strategic instrument for health promotion, social inclusion, economic development, youth empowerment, national unity, and international competitiveness while aligning the sector with national, continental, and global priorities," he said.

Also in attendance was the Minister of Sports and Member of Parliament, Hon. Kofi Iddie Adams, who assured stakeholders present of the commitment to pushing the policy through the necessary legislative processes:

"I can assure you, we have pushed very hard to have this validation so that we can go to the other processes. My prayer is that before Parliament returns, we should have concluded this document and taken it to Cabinet so we can have it presented for Parliament to consider, so it becomes a policy that we all have agreed that this is the way our sports will be handled," he stated.

Group breakout sessions were held to identify loopholes and refine the draft strategies to create a comprehensive final document.

Building on global best practices, the draft policy is structured to align with the UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), AU Agenda 2063, the ECOWAS Sports Framework, the Sports Act 2016 (Act 934), and the 1992 Constitution of Ghana, securing a sustainable framework to elevate Ghanaian sports on the international stage.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.
