The Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority has ordered every filling station in the country to recalibrate its pumps. The agency, known as the NMDPRA, licenses and polices Nigeria’s fuel depots, pipelines and retail outlets.

Its circular, issued in Abuja on Tuesday 22 September 2026, warns that serious or repeated under-dispensing can end in NMDPRA licence revocation. It was issued in the authority’s own name rather than by a named official.

A nationwide order to check the pumps

The circular tells operators to carry out immediate calibration and verification of all dispensers and totalisers. A totaliser is the meter that records how much fuel a pump has sold.

“All retail outlet operators are hereby directed to carry out immediate calibration and verification of all dispensers and totalizers,” the circular said. The order was meant “to safeguard the interests of consumers,” it added.

The authority said it had observed under-dispensing at retail outlets nationwide and had stepped up inspections. It called the practice “a serious breach of consumer trust that will not be tolerated.”

The regulator asked four trade bodies to notify their members: MEMAN, DAPPMAN, IPMAN and PETROAN. They speak for major energy marketers, depot owners, independent marketers and retail station owners.

What the warning actually says

“Persistent or serious violations will be subject to appropriate sanctions, up to and including revocation of the outlet’s license, in line with NMDPRA’s regulations,” the circular said. Outlets with improperly calibrated equipment must take immediate corrective action.

The document points to the authority’s own regulations rather than to a numbered section of the Petroleum Industry Act 2021. That law created the NMDPRA and gave it power to license and sanction downstream operators.

The circular gives no figure for how many outlets have been caught. It says only that inspections and enforcement have been intensified nationwide.

A filling station in Kafanchan, northern Nigeria. File photograph, not one of the sealed outlets (Photo: Kambai Akau, CC BY-SA 4.0 via Wikimedia Commons)

Eleven stations sealed in Rivers State in February

The warning follows months of enforcement in individual states. On Friday 6 February 2026 the authority sealed 11 filling stations in Rivers State, in Nigeria’s oil-producing south.

The sites stood in the Obio-Akpor and Port Harcourt City local government areas. Inspectors cited under-dispensing, failed pumps and other regulatory infractions.

Victor Owodiasa, the authority’s regional coordinator for the South-South zone, announced the sweep. He said it belonged to a campaign called Operation One Litre for One Litre.

“If we discover that some of them have become persistent or perpetual offenders we will be left with no option but to recommend revocation of their licences,” Owodiasa said. He spoke to reporters after the operation.

Two Ogun State outlets closed in July

On Monday 13 July 2026 a team from the authority’s Abeokuta field office sealed two outlets in Ogun State, north of Lagos. They were Mangarborn Energy and a Mobil filling station in the Akute/Ajuwon area of Ifo local government area.

Olufemi Adebowale, head of distribution systems, storage and retailing infrastructure at that office, led the exercise. He said one of the two stations had under-dispensed repeatedly, removed official seals and reopened without approval.

“It is high time we made it clear that they cannot continue to under-dispense products, deliberately remove our seals and believe that nothing will happen,” Adebowale said during the exercise. He added that the team was there to enforce the Petroleum Industry Act 2021.

The stations would stay shut until all regulatory requirements were met, including payment of penalties, he said. The authority was also considering suspending their operating licences, subject to management approval.

The Sun reported that one of the two had been monitored since 2025 and sealed at least six times. Reopening a sealed site without authorisation can bring criminal prosecution, Adebowale warned.

Why pump accuracy is political in Nigeria

Nigeria is Africa’s largest oil producer, and fuel retailing there is a heavily cash-based business. Pump prices feed straight into inflation, transport fares and household budgets.

A few centilitres shaved from each sale are invisible to a driver but add up across a forecourt’s day. That is why metering accuracy is treated as a consumer-protection question rather than a technical one.

What to watch next

No NMDPRA licence revocation under the new warning has been reported. The first one would show how far the authority intends to go.

The other test is whether the calibration order is applied evenly across Nigeria’s 36 states and its federal capital. Uneven enforcement would cost the regulator credibility with the operators who comply.

Nigeria’s downstream rules are being redrawn as its refining and distribution map changes. The Africa: The New Scramble pillar follows those shifts.

Frequently Asked Questions

What did the NMDPRA order on 22 September 2026? It told every Nigerian filling station to calibrate and verify its dispensers and totalisers immediately. The circular warned that persistent or serious under-dispensing can end in revocation of an outlet’s licence. Which petrol stations have been sealed, and when? The authority sealed 11 stations in Rivers State on Friday 6 February 2026 and two in Ogun State on Monday 13 July 2026. The Ogun pair were Mangarborn Energy and a Mobil filling station in Ifo local government area. What is the legal basis for NMDPRA licence revocation? The September circular cites the authority’s own regulations. The NMDPRA was created by the Petroleum Industry Act 2021, which the Ogun enforcement team cited when it sealed the two stations.

World.title: Mark Swift remanded after teens allegedly shot at on LaCroix Boulevard; gun found in drain
World.content:
Mark Swift remanded after teens allegedly shot at on LaCroix Boulevard; gun found in drain

By Breaking Belize News Staff: A 28-year-old Belize City businessman was remanded to the Belize Central Prison on Tuesday after being charged in connection with an alleged shooting involving two teenage boys and the subsequent discovery of a loaded revolver in a drain.

Mark Anthony Ryan Swift, of LaCroix Boulevard, appeared unrepresented before the Chief Magistrate in Court #1, where he pleaded not guilty to keeping an unlicensed firearm, keeping ammunition without a gun licence and aggravated assault.

Due to the nature of the firearm charges, Swift was denied bail and remanded until November 13, 2026.

The charges stem from an incident shortly before 1:00 a.m. on Saturday, September 19, when police on mobile patrol reportedly encountered two boys, ages 15 and 16, running along Police Street.

According to police, the teenagers told officers that a man they identified as Swift had just fired a shot at them with a revolver. The boys accompanied police back toward LaCroix Boulevard and allegedly pointed out Swift near the corner of Police and Rootsville streets.

Police allege that when Swift was detained, he told officers that the teenagers had been harassing him and offered to show police where he had thrown the gun.

Officers subsequently searched a dried drain in the area and reportedly recovered a rusty revolver bearing the serial number “5823.” Police say the weapon contained six rounds in its chamber — five live .38 rounds and one spent casing.

The teenagers later gave statements in the presence of a Justice of the Peace.

According to their account, the 16-year-old had gone outside a Police Street residence to lock a gate when he encountered Swift allegedly armed with a .38 revolver. The 15-year-old subsequently came outside looking for his friend and allegedly heard Swift threaten to kill the 16-year-old.

The boys said they ran and that Swift pursued them before allegedly firing a shot in their direction. Neither teenager was reported injured.

Police detained Swift and later charged him with aggravated assault, keeping an unlicensed firearm and keeping ammunition without a gun licence.

The allegations against Swift have not been proven in court.

World.title: Seven-months pregnant in jail for a crack pipe: Woman remanded after old $155 fine blocks her bail
World.content:
Seven-months pregnant in jail for a crack pipe: Woman remanded after old $155 fine blocks her bail

By Breaking Belize News Staff: A 35-year-old woman who is seven months pregnant was remanded to the Belize Central Prison on Tuesday after an outstanding court fine prevented her from taking up bail on a charge of possession of utensils used for smoking a controlled drug.

Leeanna Monique Samuels, a self-employed cosmetologist of Banak Street, Belize City, appeared unrepresented before a Magistrate in Court #5 after police allegedly found a silver pipe during a search on Tigris Street earlier Tuesday.

Police allege that around 10:30 a.m., officers conducting searches approached a room where Samuels was seated on a plastic chair. Police say she was holding a silver pipe in her right hand and dropped it to the floor after being informed that a search would be conducted.

The pipe, measuring about 3¼ inches, was later described by police as having been made or adapted for smoking crack cocaine or another controlled drug.

Samuels initially pleaded guilty, but when the facts were read to her, she disputed the police account. She told the court that the pipe was not found in her hand, but was beneath the chair, and that something fell when she stood up before police claimed it belonged to her.

Because her explanation amounted to a possible defence and conflicted with the prosecution’s facts, the Magistrate declined to accept the guilty plea and entered an equivocal plea of not guilty on her behalf.

Samuels was offered bail in the sum of $400 with one surety, but was required to first settle an outstanding $155 fine dating back to August 2025.

Unable to pay the old fine, a warrant was prepared for Samuels to serve the default prison term, and she was escorted to the Belize Central Prison late Tuesday evening.

Her next court appearance on the crack pipe charge is scheduled for November 30, 2026.

World.title: Police to make inquiries into Carnival video; say Human Services should intervene and parental consent would not prevent police action
World.content:
Police to make inquiries into Carnival video; say Human Services should intervene and parental consent would not prevent police action

By Breaking Belize News Staff: The Belize Police Department says it will make inquiries into a viral video showing three adult women engaging in highly sexualized dancing with a young boy during the Orange Walk Carnival, stressing that a parent’s consent would not necessarily prevent authorities from intervening where the welfare of a child is concerned.

The issue was raised with police during a press briefing on Tuesday, after BBN questioned whether authorities would investigate the incident and determine whether any criminal charges could arise.

“If the circumstances are as you are relaying them to be, certainly it is a matter of concern,” police responded, adding that the Department of Human Services should also be made aware of the video.

Police said they were not previously aware of the matter but would make inquiries.

Asked whether authorities could still take action if the child’s parent consented to the behaviour or did not wish to pursue charges, police stressed that decisions involving possible abuse of a child are not left solely to a parent.

“Any abuse concerning a child, that discretion is not left to the parent to decide whether or not actions should be taken,” police said, pointing to the role of social workers and the Human Services Department.

Police noted that in other child abuse cases, a parent may not want charges pursued against an alleged offender, but Human Services can still intervene independently. The best interests of the child, police said, remain the paramount consideration.

The comments come hours after the National Evangelical Association of Belize (NEAB) called for arrests over the video. In a statement reported earlier by BBN, NEAB described the incident as an “abusive sexual situation involving a child” and called on the Government and Police Department to enforce existing laws.

NEAB said the adult women involved should face police action and went further, saying that if the boy’s mother was the person who recorded and posted the footage, she should also face arrest. The organization also called for police officers deployed at Carnival events to be instructed to intervene when adults engage children in sexualized behaviour.

The video, highlighted by BBN earlier Tuesday, was recorded during Monday’s September 21 Orange Walk Carnival Road March and shows the boy dancing closely behind three different adult female revelers at separate points as they bend and dance provocatively in front of him. The woman who originally posted the video identified the child as her son.

The scenes have drawn comparisons to a similar incident during the 2024 Belize City Carnival. At the time, then-Commissioner of Police Chester Williams described an adult woman’s sexualized dancing with a young boy as “tantamount to an assault of a sexual nature upon that child.”

Williams stressed that the fact the boy appeared to be laughing did not mean he understood what was happening to him, and police subsequently announced an investigation. Belize Carnival Association President Patrick Thompson also condemned the behaviour at the time.

Facebook has since removed the latest Orange Walk video from BBN’s page after determining that it violated the platform’s rules relating to child sexual exploitation.

Police acknowledged Tuesday that Carnival raises a broader national discussion involving culture, personal views and morality, saying the controversy invites a larger conversation about what Belizeans are prepared to accept or embrace.

However, as it relates specifically to children, police made clear that a parent’s approval or unwillingness to pursue action does not necessarily end the matter, with Human Services empowered to intervene where the best interests of a child are at stake.

World.title: Belizean Coast Guard officer makes history with Gunnery Training in India
World.content:
Belizean Coast Guard officer makes history with Gunnery Training in India

By Zoila Palma: Chief Petty Officer Windel Ogaldez has made history as the first Belizean to attend the Gunnery Instructors Foreign Course in India, representing the Belize Coast Guard alongside military personnel from 10 countries.

The course, held at INS Dronacharya, focuses on weapons systems, sensors, weapons training, small arms and the instruction of military personnel.

The Belize Coast Guard said the training will enhance Ogaldez’s professional expertise, with the knowledge and experience expected to contribute to weapons training and institutional development within the Service upon his return to Belize.

The training also marked a special moment of friendship between Belize and India as the Indian Navy joined Ogaldez in commemorating Belize’s 45th Independence Anniversary on September 21.

The Belize Coast Guard expressed appreciation to the Government of India, the Indian Navy and the leadership and instructional staff of INS Dronacharya for the training opportunity.

World.title: International News: 22 countries back global push to keep Artificial Intelligence under human control
World.content:
International News: 22 countries back global push to keep Artificial Intelligence under human control

By Zoila Palma: Twenty-two countries have adopted a declaration calling for artificial intelligence to remain under human direction, oversight and control, while urging stronger international cooperation to manage the risks posed by rapidly developing AI systems.

The declaration was adopted on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly this week, Politico reports.

The countries acknowledged AI’s potential to improve lives, advance science and strengthen economies, but warned that increasingly powerful AI models could create serious safety and security risks if not properly managed. The declaration calls for AI companies to implement transparent safety protocols, including pre-deployment testing and independent evaluations.

The initiative also proposes stronger international standards, greater transparency and shared reporting of serious AI safety incidents.

Finnish President Alexander Stubb, one of the declaration’s organizers, said he hopes the effort will eventually bring the United States and China on board, emphasizing that “we need human intervention, so humans need to be in charge.”

Neither the United States nor China signed the declaration, which comes ahead of a planned meeting between U.S. President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping.

Stubb said potential risks include AI-assisted bioweapons, cyberattacks and autonomous weapons, while stressing that the benefits of AI could be “much higher” if the technology is used responsibly, including in areas such as disease eradication, productivity and access to information.

World.title: Prime Minister: “Belizeans are compassionate, creative and innovative”
World.content:
Prime Minister: “Belizeans are compassionate, creative and innovative”

By Zoila Palma: Prime Minister John Briceño has called on Belizeans to proudly embrace their national identity as the country marks its 45th anniversary of Independence under the theme, “Look at Me, I Am Belize at 45.”

In his Independence Day message, Briceño said the anniversary provides an opportunity for Belize to showcase its people, diversity, resilience and potential.

“Today, more than ever, it is time for Belizeans to show the world who we truly are,” he declared.

The Prime Minister said the national identity is reflected in the contributions of Belizeans from all walks of life. “To say, ‘Look at me, I am Belize,’ is to stand proudly in our Belizean identity,” he stated.

He pointed to farmers, fishers, teachers, entrepreneurs, public officers, union leaders and other hardworking Belizeans as examples of the people who contribute to the nation’s growth.

The Prime Minister also said Belize’s identity extends beyond its natural attractions and cultural heritage. “The world must know us not only for our natural beauty, our barrier reef, and our rich cultural heritage, but also for the resilience, talent, and determination of our people,” Briceño said.

He urged Belizeans to continue building the country through unity, respect for differences, community support and a shared commitment to its future.

“The world must also know that Belizeans are compassionate, creative and innovative.

But showing the world who we are must begin with how we treat one another, how we respect our differences, how we support our communities and how we always choose unity over division,” the Prime Minister said.

World.title: Prime Minister urges Belizeans to choose unity over division
World.content:
Prime Minister urges Belizeans to choose unity over division

By Zoila Palma: Prime Minister John Briceño used his 45th Independence Day message to urge Belizeans to strengthen national unity and take greater responsibility for the future of the country.

Reflecting on the theme, “Look at Me, I Am Belize at 45,” Briceño said demonstrating Belize’s identity must begin at home, particularly in how citizens treat one another. “But showing the world who we are must begin with how we treat one another, how we respect our differences, how we support our communities and how we always choose unity over division,” he said.

The Prime Minister said national unity should be reflected in practical efforts within communities, including improving neighbourhoods and looking out for one another. “It means communities coming together to keep our neighbourhoods cleaner and safer, where we look out for one another,” Briceño stated.

He also emphasized the importance of ensuring that Belizeans can live with dignity and security while contributing to the country’s development. “It means taking responsibility for the future of our country and ensuring that every Belizean can live with dignity, security and hope,” he said.

As Belize celebrates 45 years as an independent nation, Briceño said the country must continue building on the work of previous generations. “As we celebrate 45 years of Independence, let us honour those who came before us by continuing the work of building a stronger Belize,” he declared.

World.title: PM Briceño: Belize at 45 must carry strength, diversity and promise into the future
World.content:
PM Briceño: Belize at 45 must carry strength, diversity and promise into the future

By Zoila Palma: Prime Minister John Briceño has called on Belizeans at home and abroad to celebrate the country’s 45 years of Independence by looking confidently toward the future while carrying Belize’s identity with them wherever they go.

Briceño said the anniversary is more than a commemoration of independence in 1981. “Today, we invite the world to look at us—to see our strength, our diversity, our beauty, and our promise,” he declared in his Independence Day message.

The Prime Minister said Belizeans should continue to demonstrate their national pride through their actions and achievements. “Wherever we go and whatever we accomplish, let us carry Belize proudly within us,” he stated.

He also emphasized the importance of unity as the country moves forward. “And with the guidance of our Creator, we continue, firmly focused on the future and committed to living as one,” Briceño said.

World.title: ‘Not the full picture’: Gov’t rejects Opposition ‘robbery’ claims over hurricane housing costs
World.content:
Houses in Whitehouse, Westmoreland, left in ruin by Hurricane Melissa. (Photo: Garfield Robinson)

The Ministry of Economic Growth and Infrastructure Development is pushing back against criticism from the Opposition over the cost associated with the installation of semi-permanent housing units for Hurricane Melissa victims in Westmoreland and St Elizabeth, arguing that the figures being cited do not reflect the full scope of the project.

Speaking at the People’s National Party annual conference on Sunday, the part’s general secretary Dr Dayton Campbell accused the Government of carrying out “robbery in plain sight” in relation to the costing of the project. Campbell, who is the Member of Parliament for Westmoreland Eastern, said a team that includes him and his councilors “put up over 40 homes in Eastern Westmoreland” and, every base he and his team erected, were done at a cost between $60,000 and $80,000.

READ: ‘Daylight robbery’

Pointing to the $1 billion value of the government contract to mount the semi-permanent houses, and the fact that the National Housing Trust had already procured the container homes, Campbell argued that it meant that the government was “going to spend $3.7 million to build a foundation to put a container house on.”

However, in a release on Tuesday, the ministry noted that while it welcomes public scrutiny of the recovery programme, “it is important that a discussion of the associated costs reflect the full scope of what is being procured and delivered, rather than characterising a comprehensive site-development, servicing and housing-installation package simply as the cost of ‘building a base’.”

It said the suggestion that the Government is spending approximately $3.7 million merely to construct a concrete “base” or “foundation” for each housing unit does not accurately reflect the scope of the contracted works.

“The intervention provides for a comprehensive package of site development, structural, plumbing, sanitation and installation works required to establish a safe and functional housing site,” the ministry said.

According to the ministry, there are three distinct units, requiring distinct construction needs. Depending on the type of unit and the specific requirements of each site, the works include site preparation and excavation; reinforced concrete foundations and footings; structural anchoring systems; entrance and exit steps; plumbing and sanitary connections; solar generator/electrical works; bathroom and kitchenette works; water-tank infrastructure, including the provision of bases for water tanks; wastewater treatment and disposal systems; preliminaries, including security arrangements for materials stored on site; and the transportation and installation of the housing unit, the ministry stated.

It said there is no flat cost for every housing unit. The cost varies according to the type of unit and the conditions and requirements of each beneficiary site.

The ministry said its costing has also been informed and corroborated by estimates obtained from the National Works Agency (NWA) and costings from the municipal corporations within some of the affected parishes.

“The costings provided by these are broadly consistent with the ministry’s assessment of the works required, providing further assurance that the costs are reflective of the scope and prevailing requirements for the works and are not arbitrary or excessive,” the release stated.

Although the housing units are classified as semi-permanent, the Government has maintained that there will be no compromise on the safety and security of residents. The objective, it said, is to provide affected households with housing that is properly founded, securely anchored, adequately serviced, technically inspected and suitable for occupation, while meeting applicable technical and resilience requirements.

Further, the ministry said the rationale for the construction of robust structural bases, is that though semi-permanent containerised solutions will be placed on them, the intention is that should the beneficiaries’ circumstances improve, they could build more permanent structures on a solid base, given that provisions for water and sewerage would be already in place.

According to the ministry, the Government’s approach to the structural base reflects a longer-term consideration of the housing needs of beneficiaries, while the immediate intervention is intended to provide a safe and secure semi-permanent housing solution for families displaced or affected by Hurricane Melissa.

“The intention, where the site and design permit are concerned, is that the investment in a properly engineered structural base and supporting infrastructure will provide a platform for future improvement,” said the ministry. “In this way as beneficiaries’ circumstances improve, expansion or upgrading of the housing accommodation can be undertaken. In the same way, provision for water, sanitation and wastewater management is therefore not simply an additional cost associated with the immediate placement of a semi-permanent unit; it represents an investment in the functionality and potential future development of the site.”

According to the ministry, this approach is particularly important given the scale of devastation caused by Hurricane Melissa. The urgency of the recovery response cannot come at the expense of safe and functional housing. The programme is therefore intended to move affected families from emergency shelter towards more secure housing solutions, with the necessary supporting infrastructure, it said.

World.title: ‘Pastor shot me twice’
World.content:
SMITH... was pastor of Pathways International Restoration Ministries in Albion, St James

A witness broke down in tears on Monday while recounting the terrifying ordeal of being shot twice in the back by his late pastor, Dr Kevin Smith, who had assured him that he was immortal and could not die.

The witness, who also testified that Smith emptied two firearm magazines at members of the security forces on October 17, 2021 at Pathways International Restoration Ministries in Albion, St James, received permission from Justice Leighton Pusey to remove his shirt in court to show the scars from the ordeal.

Last week, the witness told the court that Smith had another member of the congregation stab him in the back. He also used the opportunity, while he was shirtless, to point to the area of his back where he had been stabbed.

Monday was the witness’s second day on the stand in the Home Circuit Court murder trial in Kingston of Andre Ruddock, who is accused of killing 39-year-old Taneka Gardner during an alleged human sacrifice ritual at the church on October 17, 2021.

Ruddock allegedly acted on the instructions of Pastor Smith, who had asked Gardner if she believed that he could bring her back to life if her throat was cut.

Gardner’s throat was subsequently cut, allegedly by Ruddock, after she gave an answer in the affirmative to Smith’s question.

The witness had testified that after Gardner’s throat was cut, Smith further instructed Ruddock to cut her head off. It was alleged that while Ruddock was doing as he was instructed, a cow broke loose from a section of the church property and Ruddock’s attention was shifted from Gardner after Smith gave more instructions for the cow to be caught and slaughtered. A member of the church allegedly chased the cow.

The witness, Gardner, and Ruddock were members of Smith’s congregation.

The witness recalled Smith walking over to him while he was on the ground in agony and stuffing his fingers in his wounds.

“I was saying, ‘I am in pain, I am in pain.’ I remember he walked over to me. I don’t remember him speaking but I can remember him pushing his fingers in the wounds in my back. On the compound, there were a lot of individuals sitting on the boardwalk. The persons he [Smith] had called to come in, they were also sitting on the boardwalk. I looked up and I saw my mom sitting there,” the witness said.

He also testified that police and soldiers came to the boardwalk.

“One of the soldiers was kicking me in my side. He was saying to me that I was shooting at him. I told him I wasn’t doing that, and a police officer came and said to the soldier to ‘Stop, don’t you see that he was shot and cramped?’

“The soldiers started ordering the other [church] members outside, telling them to hold their heads straight. They were very hostile. An ambulance came and the police assisted them to wrap my back. They placed me on a stretcher and brought me through the side gate that was there,” the witness said, explaining that Gardner’s body was still laying on the church compound at that time.

“Taneka’s body was there. Blood was there. I was able to see. I was laying face down on the stretcher so I was able to see because the compound was not dark. When I was going through the gate, I saw Andre Ruddock on the ground. He was laying on his side. I also saw Dr Smith on the ground with his hands behind him. There was nothing blocking my view. Kevin Smith was laying face down. Security forces were all over the compound. At the gate there were police and soldiers. I was taken to the Cornwall Regional Hospital,” he told the court.

The witness said Smith was the one who shot him with a firearm he had taken from a member of the church.

“There were like three police jeeps on the outside of the premises. They were opposite the gate on the other side. At that time, a police officer was climbing on the fence [to see what was happening]. Mr Smith started to say he was Elijah and he was saying just as Elijah called down fire from heaven to consume the army, he said ‘If I be a prophet of God, I call down fire from heaven to consume these 50. He said it like three times, and he then called out for a member of the Jamaica Constabulary Force who was there [as a member of the church]. She came to him and he spoke to her and she spoke back to him,” the witness said.

By that time, Gardner was already killed, allegedly by Ruddock.

The witness, who was asked by lead prosecutor LaToya Bernard to tell the court what happened after the member of the police force spoke to Smith, explained that the pastor used the gun he had received from the member of the church to open fire at the security forces who were outside the compound of the church.

“Dr Smith started shooting at the police. At that time I stepped away and went right behind a round column that was there when Dr Smith took the gun from her. I could see him firing the gun from behind the column. He was firing the gun towards the police. I wasn’t observing everything happening on the compound. I was mainly watching him and was wondering if the police were going to shoot back,” the witness told the court.

“That was why I was behind the column. When I was looking towards where the police were I could see police bending down. I did not see them return any fire. After that happened, Dr Kevin Smith then called [the police member of the church] to bring an extra magazine [for the gun]. Dr Smith continued to fire. The police did not retaliate. Outside the premises there were members from the congregation out there along with the police. Those members on the outside weren’t running or moving or anything at all. They were just out there,” the witness testified.

He said the next thing he remembered after Smith shot at the security forces were loud explosions at the gate where the police shot and killed a member of the church who was following Smith’s instructions to attack them with a knife.

After he put his shirt back on, the witness, who had been standing during his testimony, was given an opportunity to sit and compose himself while he cried.

“Yes, Mr Kevin Smith shot me. I can remember hearing loud explosions coming from right beside me, where Mr Smith was. I fell to the ground after I felt like I got a hard punch. I remember jumping up back like I was shocked. He looked on me and said to me that, ‘You are immortal and you cannot die’. Yes, that’s what he said. I could see some police officers standing at the top of where a boardwalk was. They were on the premises by this time.

“Mr Smith then spoke to Kevaughn Plummer. I can’t recall where Andre Ruddock was at the time when Dr Smith was firing at the police. Dr Smith spoke to Kevaughn Plummer and he ran towards the police to attack them. He had a knife and he ran towards them to attack them. Upon reaching close proximity to the police, I just started seeing fire coming from the police’s gun. I could hear the loud explosions. I saw when Kevaughn Plummer’s body fell to the ground. It happened so quickly. It was just a lot of shots being fired all over the compound. By that time, because of the pain I was feeling, I was laying flat on my belly at that time on the boardwalk. I was hearing a lot of shots. At that time I turned my head and saw him [Dr Smith] sitting in the same place where he was sitting when we first came up the boardwalk. He was sitting and pointing to the sky,” the witness said.

Pastor Smith died on October 25, 2021 in a motor vehicle crash on the Linstead bypass in St Catherine while being transported to Kingston to face charges.

World.title: Motorcycle mayhem
World.content:
In this file photo Inspector Amos Thompson points to a number of motorcycles that were seized by the Westmoreland police.

WESTMORELAND is recording one of its lowest murder counts in years but police say the parish is facing another public safety threat involving motorcycles, prompting a call for tougher national measures to tackle dangerous riding.

Commanding officer for the division, Senior Superintendent Othneil Dobson said the police will continue seizing and prosecuting offenders but believes the country must change its approach to the motorcycle problem.

The call comes as Westmoreland records a 29 per cent reduction in murders between January 1 and September 12, with the number falling from 28 in 2025 to 20 this year.

But while the division works to maintain the reduction in violent crime, Dobson said motorcycle-related crashes remain a persistent road safety concern, particularly in a parish where motorcycles are widely used as a means of transportation.

Speaking during a recent episode of the Jamaica Constabulary Force’s Force4Good Podcast, Dobson said the police have been carrying out daily enforcement operations, supported by specialised teams, but dangerous riding continues to result in fatalities.

“I would not sit here and tell you that most of the persons are obeying the road traffic law. Most of the accidents are a result of careless driving, persons not having the best will or thinking about the other road users. So, we have high numbers of fatalities — but it’s not a lack of trying from the police,” he said.

Dobson reported the police have recorded some success, but the recurring nature of motorcycle crashes means enforcement must be accompanied by broader public education and changes in how Jamaica manages the issue.

“As a country, we’ll have to change some of what we’re doing with motorcycles. Most of the stations in Westmoreland are overrun with motorcycles… You seize 20 or 30 bikes and you’re driving to work the next morning and you see four or five persons riding past you with new bikes. They don’t even come back to the stations to retrieve the bikes after going through the licensing process again,” he said.

“So, as a country, we have to go from a policy perspective in terms of dealing with this bike situation. We will continue to seize, we will continue to prosecute, we will continue to educate… but the penalties just have to be higher penalties as it relates to bikes,” he argued.

World.title: Love & Harmony turns 10 with a family affair at sea
World.content:
The Love and Harmony entertainment package for 2027 will include: (clockwise from top left) Aidonia, I-Wayne, D’Yani, Kevin Downswell, Beres Hammond and Sanchez.

For a decade, Love & Harmony Cruise has been bringing Caribbean music lovers together on the high seas. Next year the celebration is getting even more personal as the popular music cruise marks its 10th anniversary.

With a special Mother’s Day voyage scheduled from May 6 to 11, 2027, the whole family will be invited to celebrate a milestone that has become as much about community as it is about music.

Reggae icon Beres Hammond will be captaining the ship once more and, as it has done for the past nine years, the Love and Harmony crew expects to deliver an unforgettable experience on the high seas.

Veteran Beres Hammond will be joined by Sanchez, D’Yani, Aidonia, Kevin Downswell, and I-Wayne for the special anniversary sail dates, with more artistes and entertainment still to be announced.

The six-day, five-night experience will be a round trip from Miami aboard the Norwegian Jewel, making stops in Montego Bay, Jamaica, and Nassau, Bahamas.

But while the 10th anniversary promises the concerts, parties, and entertainment that guests have come to expect, organisers are placing a special emphasis on family this time around.

“Ten years is an incredible milestone for Love & Harmony, but what makes this anniversary even more meaningful is that we are sailing over Mother’s Day weekend,” Director of Marketing and Public Relations Ronnie Tomlinson said.

“Love & Harmony Cruise has always felt like a family reunion at sea. We have guests who return year after year, and this time we want them to bring their mothers, children, and loved ones and celebrate together. This is more than a cruise, it is six days of Caribbean culture, music, food, laughter and memories,” he said

That family-friendly approach is reflected in the offer for the 2027 sailing, with children 12 and younger sailing for free, subject to applicable taxes and fees.

And for those who have experienced Love & Harmony before, the promise is familiar: Once the ship leaves Miami, the party does not stop simply because the sun goes down.

Live concerts, themed parties, DJ experiences, karaoke, games, comedy, poolside activities, and the Captain’s Dinner will fill the schedule, while Caribbean flavours will remain an important part of the experience.

Guests can expect a mix of Caribbean and American fare alongside Norwegian Jewel’s fine and casual dining options, with Jamaican favourites such as oxtail, ackee and saltfish, jerk chicken, and curry goat among the flavours that have helped bring the island experience aboard.

While music remains the heartbeat of Love & Harmony, laughter has increasingly become part of its soundtrack and as such comedy will play a big part in the cruise’s itinerary come May. Canadian comedian Trixx will return following his appearance on the 2026 sailing, while Jamaican-British comedian White Yardie will make his Love & Harmony debut. The comedy offering adds another layer to a voyage that has evolved beyond a traditional music cruise, giving guests something to do whether they are catching a concert, lounging poolside, or simply looking for a reason to laugh.

The anniversary celebration makes its way back to Jamaican soil when the Norwegian Jewel docks in Montego Bay on Saturday, May 8. Love & Harmony will take over Tropical Bliss Beach for a special destination experience hosted by dancehall star Aidonia, giving guests the chance to trade the ship for sand, sea, and the unmistakable energy of Montego Bay. The ship is scheduled to be in port from 10:00 am to 4:00 pm, allowing Harmonisers to spend the day experiencing Jamaica before returning to the vessel and continuing the anniversary festivities.

Then, on Sunday, May 9 — Mother’s Day — the ship will remain at sea.

For organisers, the timing is intentional.

Rather than rushing from one destination to another, families will have the entire day to celebrate together, surrounded by music, food, entertainment, and the community that Love & Harmony has cultivated over the past decade.

The cruise will then head to Nassau, Bahamas, on May 10 before returning to Miami on May 11.

With additional artistes, DJs, special events and anniversary surprises still to be announced, the 2027 sailing is shaping up to be both a look back at Love & Harmony’s first decade and a celebration of the people who helped make the journey possible.

World.title: THE HUNDRED THAT WASN’T ENOUGH
World.content:
Jayden Seales of Antigua and Barbuda Falcons celebrates the dismissal of Kirk McKenzie of Jamaica Kingsmen during the Republic Bank Caribbean Premier League Final on Sunday.

JAMAICA Kingsmen Captain Rovman Powell said he was proud of his team despite an eight-wicket defeat to Antigua and Barbuda Falcons in the Republic Bank Caribbean Premier League final at Kensington Oval in Bridgetown, Barbados, on Sunday.

Antigua and Barbuda Falcons needed just 16.4 overs to chase down Kingsmen 170-9 and win their first-ever Republic Bank Caribbean Premier League (CPL) title, turning Maaz Sadaqat’s brutal 114 from 58 balls into a footnote.

“It’s a good feeling, to be honest. I think it’s a very hard-fought campaign for us. I’m so proud of the boys,” Powell said in a televised interview.

Batting first after losing the toss, Kingsmen were 30-2 in the fourth over before Sadaqat exploded. The left-hander hammered nine sixes and eight fours in a stunning hundred, adding 80 runs for the third wicket with Saim Ayub (29) to surge to 100-2 after 10 overs where it looked like the Kingsmen would have reached the 200-run mark.

However, the Falcons’ left-arm spinner Sufyan Moqim produced the spell of the tournament — four for 14 runs from four overs — and ripped the guts from the Kingsmen’s innings. After Ayub’s dismissal at 110-3 in the 12th over, no Kingsmen batsman made double figures.

Powell said his side fell short with the bat in the second half of their innings.

“I think after the halfway stage we felt as if we were 10 to 15 runs short,” Powell admitted.

“We knew it was a pretty good batting wicket. Credit has to be given to our batters for the first 10 overs. Maaz played fantastically for us, and the partnership he strung with Saim Ayub carried us to 100 for 2 in 10 overs. It’s disappointing that as a batting group on such a good wicket we didn’t really capitalise on that start,” he further said, hailing Ayub’s removal of Rakheem Cornwall (20) at 20-1 in the first over, and Evin Lewis’s (38) fall to Vitel Lawes at 84-2 in the eighth over.

Despite these feats, however, the chase was a demolition as

Amir Jangoo (57 not out) and Hasan Nawaz (47 not out) never looked troubled as they finished the job with 20 balls to spare.

“I think as a batting group, when we lost four wickets in the middle overs, four key batters who were supposed to put the impetus on the game in the last 10 overs, and as a bowling group, we didn’t control the powerplay as well as we wanted to,” Powell said.

But for Jamaica, a team that lost its first few games and was written off, Powell said that the final itself was redemption.

“I honestly feel it’s a proud journey for us. We have accomplished a lot of things. We set out to be in the finals, and when we came to the tournament we wanted to see if we could progress all the way. It was a slow start to the competition, as we lost our first few games, but we built a little bit of momentum with our home crowd back home in Jamaica and from there the guys started to believe that we could actually play cricket,” Powell said.”

“We went to Trinidad, which is a difficult place to play cricket, and we played a very good game down there. That confidence kept building within the team. We knew that as soon as we squeezed into the last four of the competition how dangerous our team could be, and the guys just kept chipping in. Credit has to be given to them throughout the entire competition. They listened to the leadership that myself and the head coach provided and I am actually proud of the boys,” he said.

World.title: BAILEY’S OUT!
World.content:
Jamaica footballer Leon Bailey (Photo: Garfield Robinson)

WITH the Jamaica’s Reggae Boyz eyeing a spot in the knockout stages of the Concacaf Nations League, they will have to do so without winger Leon Bailey who has withdrawn from the entire group stage campaign.

Bailey, who recently signed for perennial Greek champions Olympiakos FC, was one of the marquee names in interim head coach Rudolph Speid’s 24-man squad and was due to join the group on Monday, ahead of their opening game against Guatemala at the National Stadium on Friday.

Although the Jamaica Football Federation (JFF) made no official announcement on Bailey’s withdrawal, Bailey didn’t arrive on the island and will stay in Greece as he recovers from an injury.

The 29-year-old has reportedly been suffering with the injury since playing just over 13 minutes in Olympiakos’s 2-1 win over Jagiellonia Bialystok in the UEFA Europa League last Thursday. Bailey missed the club’s Sunday’s Super League Greece clash against Levadiakos.

Greek journalist George Stasinopoulos played down the severity of the injury but said, “Olympiacos came to an agreement with the medical staff of the Jamaican national team, with both sides coming to an agreement and ultimately Leon Bailey not getting on the plane to make the trip for his national team.

“He suffered from injuries last season and faced several issues, so they have decided to pay enough attention to the Jamaican and take advantage of the break.”

Europa League champion Bailey will miss not only Friday’s game against Guatemala and Monday’s clash with Honduras at the National Stadium, but also the away fixtures against El Salvador next Friday and Honduras on October 5, which will complete Jamaica’s Group B fixtures in Nations League A.

It’s the second-consecutive season where he’s missed the national team’s group stage campaign, having missed all four games in 2024 against Cuba, Honduras (twice) and Nicaragua.

Bailey, who has seven goals in 41 caps for the Reggae Boyz, also missed the entirety of last year’s final round of Concacaf World Cup Qualifiers after picking up several injuries during his short loan spell at AS Roma in Serie A. Jamaica ultimately finished runners-up behind Curacao, and missed automatic qualification to the 2026 FIFA World Cup in United States, Mexico and Canada.

The former Aston Villa winger did feature in the World Cup play-offs in March against New Caledonia and DR Congo but has missed 17 of Jamaica’s last 28 competitive fixtures.

The Jamaica Observer has learnt that a replacement for Bailey is set to be announced Tuesday, with Speid and his technical staff still considering their options as late as Monday afternoon.

Last Friday, Speid revealed he scouted 72 players for the Nations League group stage before selecting the final squad. He also said he invited players outside of the initial 24 to train with the squad as part of a scouting mission, but those names haven’t been made public.

Most of the group participated in an activation session on Monday, with the others set to join the team in their first training session on Tuesday at the National Stadium.

The Reggae Boyz need to finish top two in their group to advance to the quarter-finals where they would play one of Concacaf’s top four nations, Mexico, USA, Canada or Panama, which were pre-seeded.

World.title: The Wellness Wedding: How Healthy Living Is Changing the Guest Experience
World.content:
Wedding bar trends are evolving rapidly. Mindful drinking is becoming increasingly common amongst guests, prompting couples to serve elevated zero-proof options.

Weddings have traditionally been celebrations of indulgence — open bars, impressive appetizers, fancy dinners, decadent desserts and late-night comfort food.. But as lifestyles change, so do weddings.

Today’s younger couples are increasingly health-conscious. They drink less, pay more attention to what they eat and are more aware of dietary restrictions and overall wellness. Naturally, those habits are beginning to influence how they entertain their wedding guests.

The result isn’t the completely “healthy wedding”. It is a more conscious wedding experience, where indulgence and enjoyment coexist with choice.

The Bar Is Changing

One of the biggest shifts is at the bar. Not drinking — or simply drinking less — has become increasingly normal, and zero-proof options are moving well beyond basic fruit punch.

Zero-proof spirits, botanical spritzes, alcohol-free sparkling wines and beautifully constructed mocktails can now be presented with the same attention as traditional cocktails. Couples can even create alcoholic and zero-proof versions of their signature drink.

The message isn’t that we don’t drink. It is you don’t have to drink to fully participate in the celebration.

Food Is Becoming Lighter But Not Boring

Wedding menus are changing too. Couples are increasingly balancing fried hors d’oeuvres, heavy sauces and late-night comfort foods with grilled proteins, ceviches, sushi, fresh seafood, vegetable-forward dishes, salads and fruit.

This isn’t about putting wedding guests on a diet. It is about balance.

A Jamaican wedding doesn’t have to abandon jerk, curry or other favourites. Those dishes can sit comfortably beside grilled seafood, roasted vegetables, vibrant salads and fresh tropical fruit. Guests can indulge while still having choices that reflect how they normally eat.

Dietary Consciousness Is Hospitality

Vegetarian, vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free and allergy-conscious options are also becoming part of normal event planning rather than afterthoughts.

Couples can collect dietary requirements through RSVPs, clearly label buffet selections and ensure alternative meals receive the same attention as the main menu. The vegetarian guest should no longer be served whatever the kitchen can quickly assemble after everyone else has eaten.

That is where wellness becomes good hospitality.

Smoking Is Being Reconsidered

Smoking is another part of the guest experience couples are approaching differently. Cigarette and cigar smoke doesn’t have to drift through lounges, dining areas or dance floors simply because a wedding is outdoors.

Designated smoking areas and thoughtfully positioned cigar lounges allow those who want the experience to enjoy it without imposing it on everyone else.

Wellness Beyond the Reception

For destination weddings, wellness can extend across the entire weekend through morning yoga, spa experiences, fresh juice and smoothie stations, healthier welcome amenities and lighter morning-after brunches.

The idea is simple: Enjoy yourself tonight and still feel good tomorrow.

A New Definition of Luxury

None of this means taking the fun out of weddings. Serve the Champagne, cake and late-night comfort food. Just remember that not everyone drinks, eats meat, wants fried food, or smokes.

The strongest interpretation of the wellness trend isn’t restriction. It is choice.

Luxury hospitality has always been about anticipating what guests might want before they have to ask. For today’s couples, that increasingly means creating a celebration where different lifestyles can comfortably coexist.

The modern wedding isn’t becoming less indulgent. It is becoming more considerate — and perhaps that is one of the most meaningful shifts in the modern guest experience.

World.title: A Cuban zoo, and its animals, in epic battle for survival
World.content:
Two Bengal tiger cubs (Panthera tigris) rest at the National Zoo of Havana in Havana on September 15, 2026. (Photo: AFP)

HAVANA, Cuba (AFP) — Every day, veterinarians and zookeepers make their way to Cuba’s National Zoo by whatever means they can, determined to not abandon the nearly 1,000 animals in their care and help save species at risk of extinction.

Their dedication and food donations are vital to keeping alive an array of rhinos, jaguars and tigers — including an extremely rare white tiger — in the midst of a severe crisis that has left many Cubans struggling to feed themselves.

Just getting to the reserve situated 20 kilometres (12 miles) from central Havana is a headache for staff, as public transportation has come to a near standstill nine months into a US fuel blockade.

“The workers come by bicycle, pedal scooter or electric motorbike to ensure the animals have food and water every day,” said Yoel Machado, the zoo’s animal welfare manager.

Their efforts are about more than keeping the animals fed.

The 345-hectare (850-acre) park serves as a genetic reserve of international conservation importance, housing breeding populations of vulnerable or endangered species, including black and white rhinos, hippos and jaguars.

Yet the same crisis that has left workers scrambling to source meat, medicine and water has forced the zoo to curb reproduction programs and increasingly rely on handouts to sustain its animals.

During a recent visit by AFP, two Bengal tiger cubs, one an extremely rare white specimen, frolicked in their enclosure beneath the watchful gaze of their mother, oblivious to the strenuous efforts made to keep them alive.

AFP did not see any animals that appeared malnourished or ill, but Angel Cordero, the veterinarian in charge of big cats, said the tiger cubs “could be in better shape.”

He revealed he needed to ration their food to prevent it from running out.

“It’s no use giving them plenty if it only lasts three days,” he said.

Big cats need about seven kilograms (15 pounds) of meat per day per adult, but such quantities are hard to come by.

Even when it is available, recurring blackouts of up to 30 hours at a stretch make it difficult to preserve.

With fuel extremely scarce, there’s also the issue of how to distribute food in a nature reserve the size of New York’s Central Park.

For now, private donors have come to the rescue for the zoo’s various needs.

Every Monday, Ana Fernandez, a Cuban-American woman born in Tennessee who has been living in Cuba for nine years, donates meat.

“The animals shouldn’t have to suffer,” the 50-year-old said, though she added that “some days it’s not enough for all of them.”

Recently, the reserve went 23 days without electricity, which meant it also lacked running water.

The staff “didn’t just sit around waiting for things to fall from the sky,” the zoo’s director Juan Carlos Corella said.

“We looked for solutions, water trucks were brought in, and we found food for the animals almost daily,” he said, while admitting that keeping the park open has become “very difficult.”

An exodus of vets has added to the zoo’s woes.

More than a third have left for better-paying jobs elsewhere, mostly in Cuba’s burgeoning private sector.

Some wait tables in cafes while others work for private veterinary clinics.

The zoo is home to the only breeding group of black rhinos outside of Africa, as well as a large population of white rhinos, the largest herd of Grant’s zebras in the Americas and hippos that regularly bear calves.

“Here we have a high genetic value, and one of immense international importance,” Machado, the animal welfare manager, explained.

However, the crisis has forced the park to slow down its breeding programs.

The reason is simple: each new offspring requires more food, medicine, and staff.

“We can’t keep increasing the number of animals,” Machado said, adding that he preferred to ensure the current population was “as well cared for as possible.”

And yet life keeps renewing itself, regardless.

In recent months, the zoo has welcomed baby tigers, hyenas, jackals, and a black dromedary named Esperanza (Spanish for “Hope”), the first of its kind born in Cuba in three decades.

World.title: France extends fuel subsidies to shield consumers from skyrocketing energy prices
World.content:
PARIS — The French government said Tuesday it would spend €450 million to extend fuel subsidies until the end of the year to help companies and workers affected by the economic consequences of the war in the Middle East.

“We hear the concerns of the French people, which sometimes take the form of anger. These concerns and this anger are sincere, and we must address them. That is what we are doing today,” Economy and Finance Minister Roland Lescure told reporters Tuesday.

The package includes a €0.15 per liter subsidy on non-road diesel for farmers and €0.20 per liter subsidy for construction company trucks. The government will also double the subsidy from €0.20 to €0.40 for those with low incomes who must drive for work, such as nurses who carry out home visits.

World.title: Nothing ‘to be ashamed of’: EU center right clashes with Socialists over far-right votes
World.content:
“We should go beyond that. On some issues, I think that they [the far right] are relatively sane. On some other issues, there’s insanity,” he added, while insisting a majority of votes in Parliament will involve the mainstream parties.

Since the 2024 EU election, the EPP has repeatedly passed legislation with support from right-wing and far-right groups, particularly on migration and green policy — topics where the centrist groups have the widest gaps between them — sidelining its traditional centrist and center-left partners.

Liberals and Social Democrats are now pushing for binding, coalition-style commitments among the three centrist forces to prevent the EPP from turning to the far right.

“We need to step up also our game in the center … if we don’t find compromises within files, we have to find it across files,” said René Repasi, head of the German Social Democrats in the Parliament, who was taking part in the panel debate with Aaltola. “We need to not to dilute everything in compromises, but give everybody their wins, and that is the point: You need to have this in an agreement with a binding governance structure that includes many other members than simply the leaders in order to increase ownership.”

However, Aaltola pushed back against the idea, arguing that the Parliament’s political reality is more diverse. “That’s kind of a Soviet election result type of politics, there’s always going to be diversity,” he said. “That’s what democracy is all about, and so we cannot hammer out that coalition agreement that would be millimeter tight, and no voter will buy it from us.”

Renew Europe Vice Chair Gerben-Jan Gerbrandy, who was also on the panel, argued that centrist unity is essential to tackle Ukraine, geopolitics, climate change, and the cost-of-living crisis, warning that fights over the far-right firewall are distracting from more pressing concerns for EU citizens.

World.title: EU and Canada to unveil new partnership, but it may not be ‘associate membership,’ says ambassador
World.content:
“Ultimately, I’m less fussed about what we end up calling it. I’m more fussed about that we have initiatives that are really going to drive prosperity, economic security, and a range of things moving forward,” he said.

The EU and Canada are in the process of identifying areas to upgrade their partnership, including critical raw materials, AI, research and innovation. Asked when those deals could be signed, Wilkinson said they would be coming “pretty soon,” with several planned for the joint EU–Canada summit in October.

“This is not something that you commit to do, and it’s five years later. This is something that we’re looking to do within the next 12 months,” he went on. “I’m not sure what you’re going to call it, but a much deeper and closer relationship.”

The idea of associate membership raised eyebrows among EU diplomats, who said capitals had not been asked whether they supported the plan — and pointed out that no such legal relationship is defined in the bloc’s foundational treaties.

However, two EU officials, granted anonymity to explain the arrangement, said it was a way to brand a new kind of partnership that goes deeper than existing trade, research and defense agreements.

World.title: Kyiv and Washington want war in Ukraine to end 'before winter,' Zelenskyy says
World.content:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has announced that Kyiv and Washington want to see the war in Ukraine end "before winter" following what he described as a "positive" meeting with his US counterpart Donald Trump.

 

Zelenskyy and Trump met on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly in New York on Tuesday, where the Ukrainian leader said they had discussed potentially "de-escalatory steps that can open up the way to diplomacy."

"I just had a positive and productive meeting with President Trump," he wrote in a post on social media. "Both the U.S. and Ukraine want to see this senseless Russian war ended before winter".

He added that he and Trump had also spoken about a winter air defence package for Ukraine as well as "other bilateral and multilateral issues."

Russia has kept up an almost relentless bombardment of Ukrainian cities and regions since launching its full-scale invasion of the country in February 2022, but it has particularly sought to target Ukraine's energy infrastructure over winter periods.

Ukraine has also targeted the Russian energy sector as part of its deep strike campaign, which aims to degrade a key driver of the Russian economy and impact the Kremlin's war machine.

Ukrainian forces have launched frequent strikes against oil facilities including refineries, terminals, and depots as part of this strategy. Earlier on Tuesday, Zelenskyy announced that one oil refinery had been hit in Bashkortostan and another in the Samara region over the past 24 hours.

Speaking to the press together with Zelenskyy in New York, Trump addressed Ukrainian attacks on Russian energy facilities, saying they had been a "very serious hit" on Russia but also "a serious hit on the price of diesel."

Trump said on Monday that Russia had "unfortunately lost control of its diesel oil industry due to its war with Ukraine" while calling for what he described as the "ridiculous and never ending" war to come to an end.

"A large number of their diesel refineries have been blown up and are, at least temporarily, out of commission," he wrote in a post on his Truth Social account. "The whole world suffers as 25,000 people, mostly soldiers, are being killed each month. What a shame!"

Zelenskyy responded by insisting that Ukraine was willing to halt strikes on Russia's energy industry if Moscow agreed to do the same.

"Ukraine’s energy sector, critical infrastructure, and our food exports must stop being targets for Russia, and this will lead to matching de-escalation steps on our part. Solutions are possible," he wrote on X.

World.title: At least four dead and six missing in Japan day after Typhoon Dujuan made landfall
World.content:
Typhoon Dujuan left at least four people dead and 22 injured in Japan, while thousands of houses near Tokyo were without power after the storm swept through the region, authorities said on Tuesday.

 

Officials warned that the death toll may continue to rise as six people remain missing, noting that search and rescue operations were underway to locate them.

The typhoon moved away from Japan's coast and out into the Pacific by the morning, allowing authorities to lift or downgrade most heavy rain and landslide warnings.

Dujuan had already led to the early closure in the capital of one of the world's biggest video game trade fairs.

Japan often sees strong typhoons in the late summer and early autumn, with other storms this season disrupting some events at the Asian Games being held in the country.

The Fire and Disaster Management Agency said three people died in Chiba prefecture and one in Kanagawa region, both near the capital, Tokyo.

Entire areas were completely submerged by floodwaters, causing considerable damage and bringing many critical services, major roads and public transportation to a standstill.

More than 45,000 households in Chiba near Tokyo were still without electricity on Tuesday afternoon, while over 460 houses suffered varying degrees of damage.

Although Dujuan weakened as it moved northeast, it dumped record rainfall in parts of the Tokyo area.

Oshima, an island about 120 kilometres south of central Tokyo, recorded 832 millimetres of rain over a 48-hour period, more than double its average rainfall for the whole of September, public broadcaster NHK reported.

Rainfall in Tokyo's Edogawa Ward reached a record 282.5 millimetres over 24 hours.

Scientists say human-driven climate change is intensifying the risk posed by heavy rains because a warmer atmosphere holds more water.

World.title: Burnham touts 'good connection' with Trump as pair meet for first time in New York
World.content:
British Prime Minister Andy Burnham and US President Donald Trump appeared to get along well as they met for the first time in New York this week.

 

The leaders gave short statements and took questions from the media on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly on Tuesday after holding talks together.

Trump, who remained polite and friendly throughout, opened by saying he thought Burnham was going to be a "great prime minister" and that he had "a lot of assets on his side," adding that the US was with him "all the way."

In response, Burnham thanked the president before touting their "good connection," while noting that the pair had discussed Ukraine, the Falkland Islands, and trade issues in their discussion.

Asked whether Burnham was someone he could do business with, Trump seemed positive, describing him as a "natural businessperson" - a label that might raise eyebrows among some of the prime minister's critics at home.

"We've had a lot of discussions even before this meeting," Trump told reporters. "We've spoken to each other numerous times on the phone. I think so, I think so. He gets it, he understands what he has to do".

On immigration, a politically charged topic on both sides of the Atlantic that has been central to Trump's presidency, Trump gave a diplomatic response despite having previously delivered strong criticism of the UK's approach to the issue.

For his part, Burnham acknowledged the growing importance of immigration in British politics and noted that the UK was continuing to tackle migrant boats arriving from continental Europe. He added that crossings were down roughly 50% over the summer compared to six years ago.

Trump wrapped up the news conference with a jab at former British Prime Minister Keir Starmer, saying that relations with the UK were "more up now" under Burnham while also slamming the Starmer government's Chagos Island's deal as "terrible." The proposed deal would give Mauritius sovereignty over the islands, which include the UK-US Diego Garcia military base.

"Right now, based on my relationship with your prime minister, Andy, I think we're doing very well," Trump said.

Burnham, who took office in late July, seems to have established a foundation he can build on with regards to his dealings with Washington, and he will likely be pleased with how the conference went given how unpredictable some live events with Trump can be.

World.title: Jorge Palma (1950-2026): the songs that will never die
World.content:
Jorge Palma, one of the most influential singers, songwriters and composers in contemporary Portuguese music, died on Monday at the age of 76 in physical years, even if metaphorically he had lived more than a hundred thousand, as he sang on Encosta-te a mim, a track from the 2007 album Voo Nocturno. The music video, in which Palma appears surrounded by lifelong friends and recent companions, will live on. Palma may have left us, but his songs will forever be part of Portuguese culture and soul.

 

On Estróina, a track on his most recent album, Vida (2023), he sings: "Whoever my undertaker may be, make sure I am properly dressed." There could be no finer attire than the many farewell words already dedicated to him, alongside the many he himself wrote.

And, as he went on singing, "and since life is meant to be lived live and in full colour, let us raise a glass to pleasure, with no false modesty." That is exactly what we will do. Euronews spoke to several people close to the singer, to Portuguese culture and to his work, all unconditional admirers of his legacy, to understand what remains after his passing and which songs they will never forget.

Herman José - Actor and comedian

For Herman José, who crossed paths with Jorge Palma many times and in many different settings, his death "leaves a silence that will be hard to fill".

One of his most cherished memories with the singer goes back to 1974. "I was one of his musicians, alongside the great Pedro Osório. It is one of those memories that time does not erase and that today returns with particular strength. We were all much younger, in a Portugal that itself was embarking on a new life, and even then Jorge's extraordinary musical personality was already there – restless, free, unpredictable, fascinating," he recalls.

The comedian says Jorge Palma was an "utterly unique musician", one of those who "never needed to resemble anyone else to be recognised from the very first chord, the first word, the first inflection of that voice".

From all the work Jorge Palma leaves behind, Herman José chooses Deixa-me Rir (from O Lado Errado da Noite, 1985), "perhaps because in it I find so much of Jorge: the intelligence, the irony, the mistrust of certainties, a certain melancholy hidden behind the smile. And that rare ability to say serious things without ever losing his irreverence," he concludes.

Song from the 1985 album

António Zambujo - Singer and songwriter

For the singer from Beja, choosing just one Jorge Palma song is "unfair" because "his body of work is immensely rich". Even so, he accepted Euronews' challenge and picked the song O Meu amor Existe, from the voice-and-piano album Só, released in 1991.

"I consider this record the best in the history of Portuguese music, and whatever I might say about Jorge Palma would never be enough, given the dimension I believe he has," he said.

Gabriel Gomes - Musician and composer

"I have lost a friend, a hero," Gabriel Gomes, accordionist and former member of Madredeus and Sétima Legião, tells us to begin with. He quickly adds: "But I gained so much from his presence in my life."

Gabriel Gomes and Jorge Palma performing together at the Almada Museum António Francisco Melão

Earlier this year he shared the stage with Jorge Palma and, at the Artes à Vila festival in the Batalha Monastery, presented his first solo project.

"The emptiness hurts, but his memory and his work will eventually fill it. It was quick, as he deserved," he sums up.

Gabriel Gomes chose the song Passos em Volta, from the album Bairro do Amor, which they played together on stage so many times and in which, just as in the lyrics, Jorge Palma "opened the window and flew away".

Tiago Cação - artistic agent

With a long career in the music, live entertainment and artist management industries, he confided that he had never wanted to meet Jorge Palma.

"I never wanted to meet Jorge. I never wanted to get close to him. I always wanted to keep Jorge in an intangible place, alongside the great poets and great musicians I have always admired. On Friday, my father (much younger than Jorge), whom I thought knew nothing about music, said: 'I would not like to die without seeing a Jorge Palma concert. Because with artists like Jorge, we always think they do not die. And they do not'," he shared.

For Tiago, the song he will never forget is Sonhadores inatos. "I identify with the simple idea of never stopping dreaming, despite the inevitabilities that come with being alive."

Fernando Vendrell - Film director

The filmmaker admits that today he can only think of Frágil (Bairro do Amor, 1989). "Tonight I feel so fragile," he paraphrases.

Director of films such as "Aparição" and "Sombras Brancas", Fernando Vendrell remembers Jorge Palma as "an extraordinary writer of songs".

"In my view, they are among the most perfect songs ever written in Portugal. His gaze and his writing were agile, his melodies graceful and unique. They brought with them a world we belonged to or wanted to be part of," he says.

Ana Margarida de Carvalho - Journalist and writer

When she heard the news of the singer's death, the song that came to her mind was Na Terra dos Sonhos, for its melody and because it was written by a "sceptical optimist".

Ana Margarida de Carvalho says she knows all the albums, songs, acoustic versions and live recordings, where his "virtuosity on piano, acoustic guitar or electric guitar" always stood out: "He had enormous versatility, a powerful voice that stood the test of time," she recalls, referring to the many concerts she attended. Jorge Palma's voice also became part of her everyday life. "He is always on my car playlist..." she says.

Among the many songs by Jorge Palma, the journalist also highlights Portugal, Portugal, which she considers "an anthem", and Estrela do Mar, whose chords "sound like waves, or the string quartet, in which he pays tribute to Durrell's Alexandria Quartet".

However, she told Euronews she was choosing Eu Fui um Lobo Malvado (Acto Contínuo, 1982). "With lyrics that are naïve, perhaps, but which in my view make it a song that turns back on itself and becomes the most beautiful declaration of welcome, a song about friendship and reconciliation, ultimately – and I know it by heart, and so do my children."

"I have not yet wielded a weapon that did not ricochet / and the scar always outlives even the neatest bandage / but whenever you want you are welcome in my castle / which perhaps because it is old and wrinkled / does not need painting," she quotes.

Luiz Carvalho - Photographer

The author of the cover photo for this article (kindly made available for publication) recalls his first encounter with the singer: "I have known you since that afternoon in 1980 in Paris when I photographed you singing in the Saint-Michel metro station. Afterwards we went for a drink, I think Graça Lamy was there too. The damned negative exists but I just cannot find it. I love your work and, above all, your attitude to life: free, non-conformist, polite, a musician with classical roots, at times too wild for the body to be able to keep up. I would have loved to make a documentary about you, something alive, handheld camera, direct sound... You will always be in my heart and in my ears, for as long as I still have road ahead of me."

The song he has chosen is O Lado Errado da Noite, "a striking melody, very much in tune with part of his own journey".

Finally... the choices of the authors of this piece

Ana Filipa Palma: A Gente Vai Continuar is not only one of his greatest songs, it is also one of the most listened to today and, above all, a promise that his voice will remain "for as long as there are winds and sea".

The tribute to Palma at the latest edition of the Play awards ended with the whole audience singing A Gente Vai Continuar.

Ricardo Figueira: I choose Bairro do Amor because it is comforting to believe there is a place drawn in coloured pencil by people who have suffered for not having anyone, a country with no prisons and no hospitals, where the sun seems bigger and there are waves of tenderness in every look. Even if that place exists only in songs.
